```css
@import 'tailwindcss';
@import '@nexusdi/meridian-ui/styles.css';

/*
 * next-themes writes the theme onto <html> as a class. Tailwind's dark:
 * variant follows that class and ignores the system setting.
 */
@custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *));

/*
 * The Meridian tokens on a Nextra site (spec §8.6). Three surfaces:
 * 1. --nextra-bg and the primary hue arrive through <Head> props from
 *    app/meridian-theme.ts.
 * 2. Tailwind's gray, neutral and slate steps map onto the Meridian palette
 *    below, one lightness ladder for both themes: 50 is the lightest value,
 *    950 the darkest.
 * 3. Headings take the display family, scoped to the article.
 */
:root {
  --x-font-sans: var(--meridian-font-body);
  --x-font-mono: var(--meridian-font-mono);
}

:root {
  --x-color-gray-50: var(--meridian-palette-light-space-0);
  --x-color-gray-100: var(--meridian-palette-light-space-2);
  --x-color-gray-200: var(--meridian-palette-light-rule);

  --x-color-gray-900: var(--meridian-palette-light-text);
  --x-color-gray-950: var(--meridian-palette-dark-space-0);

  --x-color-neutral-50: var(--meridian-palette-light-space-0);
  --x-color-neutral-100: var(--meridian-palette-light-space-2);
  --x-color-neutral-200: var(--meridian-palette-light-rule);
  --x-color-neutral-300: var(--meridian-palette-dark-text-secondary);
  --x-color-neutral-400: var(--meridian-palette-dark-text-tertiary);
  --x-color-neutral-500: var(--meridian-palette-light-control-border);
  --x-color-neutral-600: var(--meridian-palette-light-text-tertiary);
  --x-color-neutral-700: var(--meridian-palette-light-text-secondary);
  --x-color-neutral-800: var(--meridian-palette-dark-rule);

/*
 * The ground paints on html. body stays transparent in both themes, so the
 * fixed background canvas at z-index -1 shows between html and the surfaces.
 * The selector outranks the theme's body rule, which sets --nextra-bg.
 */
html {
  background: linear-gradient(
      180deg,
      var(--meridian-palette-light-space-0),
      var(--meridian-palette-light-space-2)
    )
    fixed;
  color: var(--meridian-text);
}

html.dark {
  background: linear-gradient(
      180deg,
      var(--meridian-palette-dark-space-0),
      var(--meridian-palette-dark-space-2)
    )
    fixed;
}

html body {
  background: transparent;
  font-family: var(--meridian-font-body);
}

/*
 * The reading surfaces. No text renders on the canvas: the chrome and the
 * article each sit on the hull (spec §8.2). surfaces.spec.ts fails on any
 * text node whose nearest painted ancestor is under 0.86 alpha.
 */
.nextra-navbar-blur,
.nextra-sidebar,
.nextra-toc,
.nextra-footer,
footer,
article {
  background-color: var(--meridian-hull);
  backdrop-filter: blur(12px);
}

article {
  border-radius: var(--meridian-radius-panel);
  box-shadow: var(--meridian-elevation-glass);
}

article :where(h1, h2, h3, h4):not([class*='meridian-']) {
  font-family: var(--meridian-font-display);
}

article h1:not([class*='meridian-']) {
  letter-spacing: var(--meridian-tracking-display);
}

/*
 * The concept page grid (spec §5.4, §10.2). Below 1280px the prose runs alone
 * and each ConsoleView renders inline; from 1280px the console sits in a
 * sticky right column below the navbar.
 */
.nexus-console-grid__console {
  display: none;
}

@media (min-width: 80rem) {
  .nexus-console-grid {
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: minmax(0, var(--meridian-measure)) minmax(0, 1fr);
    gap: var(--meridian-space-6);
    align-items: start;
  }

  .nexus-console-grid__console {
    display: block;
    position: sticky;
    top: calc(var(--nextra-navbar-height, 4rem) + var(--meridian-space-4));
  }
}

.nexus-console-grid__prose {
  max-inline-size: var(--meridian-measure);
}

/* Focus: a 2px ring at 2px offset, cyan in dark mode, its ink in light mode. */
:focus-visible {
  outline: 2px solid var(--meridian-focus);
  outline-offset: 2px;
}

a,
button,
summary {
  transition:
    color var(--meridian-motion-interaction) var(--meridian-motion-curve),
    background-color var(--meridian-motion-interaction)
      var(--meridian-motion-curve);
}

::view-transition-group(*),
::view-transition-old(*),
::view-transition-new(*) {
  animation-duration: var(--meridian-motion-console);
  animation-timing-function: var(--meridian-motion-curve);
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  ::view-transition-group(*),
  ::view-transition-old(*),
  ::view-transition-new(*) {
    animation: none;
  }
}
```

```ts
import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

import { createScheduler, frameCap, type SchedulerEnv } from './scheduler.js';

/** A 60 Hz display with a hand-driven clock. */
function fakeEnv() {
  const state = {
    clock: 0,
    frames: new Map<number, (time: number) => void>(),
    nextId: 1,
    draws: [] as number[],
    reducedMotion: false,
    saveData: false,
    paused: false,
    hidden: false,
    charging: null as boolean | null,
  };
  const env: SchedulerEnv = {
    now: () => state.clock,
    requestFrame: (callback) => {
      const id = state.nextId++;
      state.frames.set(id, callback);
      return id;
    },
    cancelFrame: (id) => void state.frames.delete(id),
    draw: (time) => void state.draws.push(time),
    reducedMotion: () => state.reducedMotion,
    saveData: () => state.saveData,
    paused: () => state.paused,
    hidden: () => state.hidden,
    charging: () => state.charging,
  };
  const advance = (ms: number) => {
    const until = state.clock + ms;
    while (state.clock + 1000 / 60 <= until + 1e-9) {
      state.clock += 1000 / 60;
      const due = [...state.frames];
      state.frames.clear();
      for (const [, callback] of due) callback(state.clock);
    }
    state.clock = until;
  };
  const drawsDuring = (ms: number) => {
    const before = state.draws.length;
    advance(ms);
    return state.draws.length - before;
  };
  return { state, env, advance, drawsDuring };
}

describe('frameCap', () => {
  it('caps at 30 while active on mains power or with no battery API', () => {
    expect(frameCap({ idleMs: 0, charging: true })).toBe(30);
    expect(frameCap({ idleMs: 0, charging: null })).toBe(30);
  });

  it('caps at 15 on battery', () => {
    expect(frameCap({ idleMs: 0, charging: false })).toBe(15);
  });

  it('drops to 10 after 30 seconds without input', () => {
    expect(frameCap({ idleMs: 30_000, charging: null })).toBe(10);
    expect(frameCap({ idleMs: 30_000, charging: false })).toBe(10);
  });
});

describe('createScheduler', () => {
  let fake: ReturnType<typeof fakeEnv>;

  beforeEach(() => {
    fake = fakeEnv();
  });

  it('draws 30 frames a second at the default cap', () => {
    const scheduler = createScheduler(fake.env);
    scheduler.start();
    expect(fake.drawsDuring(1000)).toBe(30);
    expect(scheduler.cap).toBe(30);
  });

  it('draws 15 frames a second on battery', () => {
    fake.state.charging = false;
    createScheduler(fake.env).start();
    expect(fake.drawsDuring(1000)).toBe(15);
  });

  it('drops to 10 after 30 idle seconds and returns to 30 on input', () => {
    const scheduler = createScheduler(fake.env);
    scheduler.start();
    fake.advance(30_000);
    expect(fake.drawsDuring(1000)).toBe(10);
    scheduler.activity();
    expect(fake.drawsDuring(1000)).toBe(30);
  });

  for (const reason of ['reducedMotion', 'saveData', 'paused'] as const) {
    it(`draws one frame and starts no loop under ${reason}`, () => {
      fake.state[reason] = true;
```

- [ ] Step 3: Implement the scheduler

`internal/meridian-ui/src/background/scheduler.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * When the background draws (spec §9.3). Pure: the browser reaches it through
 * `SchedulerEnv`, so a fake clock and a fake frame source drive the tests.
 *
 * The loop runs on the display's frame callback and skips frames to hold the
 * cap. A static condition (reduced motion, Save-Data, the reader's pause
 * switch) draws one frame and cancels the loop. A hidden tab cancels the loop
 * and draws nothing.
 */

export const IDLE_AFTER_MS = 30_000;

export interface SchedulerEnv {
  now(): number;
  requestFrame(callback: (time: number) => void): number;
  cancelFrame(id: number): void;
  draw(time: number): void;
  reducedMotion(): boolean;
  saveData(): boolean;
  paused(): boolean;
  hidden(): boolean;
  charging(): boolean | null;
}

export interface Scheduler {
  start(): void;
  refresh(): void;
  activity(): void;
  stop(): void;
  readonly looping: boolean;
  readonly cap: 30 | 15 | 10;
}

export function frameCap(input: {
  idleMs: number;
  charging: boolean | null;
}): 30 | 15 | 10 {
  if (input.idleMs >= IDLE_AFTER_MS) return 10;
  if (input.charging === false) return 15;
  return 30;
}

export function createScheduler(env: SchedulerEnv): Scheduler {
  let frame: number | null = null;
  let lastDraw = Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY;
  let lastActivity = env.now();
  let stopped = false;
  let staticDrawn = false;

  const cap = () =>
    frameCap({ idleMs: env.now() - lastActivity, charging: env.charging() });

  const cancel = () => {
    if (frame !== null) env.cancelFrame(frame);
    frame = null;
  };

  const tick = (time: number) => {
    frame = null;
    // Half a millisecond of slack absorbs the jitter in frame timestamps.
    if (time - lastDraw >= 1000 / cap() - 0.5) {
      env.draw(time);
      lastDraw = time;
    }
    frame = env.requestFrame(tick);
  };

  const refresh = () => {
    if (stopped) return;
    if (env.hidden()) {
      cancel();
      return;
    }
    if (env.reducedMotion() || env.saveData() || env.paused()) {
      cancel();
      if (!staticDrawn) {
        env.draw(env.now());
        staticDrawn = true;
      }
      return;
    }
    staticDrawn = false;
    if (frame === null) frame = env.requestFrame(tick);
  };

  return {
    start: refresh,
    refresh,
    activity() {
      lastActivity = env.now();
    },
    stop() {
      stopped = true;
      cancel();
    },
    get looping() {
      return frame !== null;
    },
    get cap() {
      return cap();
    },
  };
}
```

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

import { createStars, mulberry32, starCount } from './stars.js';

describe('starCount', () => {
  it('never draws fewer than 150 or more than 400 stars', () => {
    expect(starCount(320, 480)).toBe(150);
    expect(starCount(7680, 4320)).toBe(400);
  });

  it('scales with viewport area between the bounds', () => {
    const laptop = starCount(1440, 900);
    const desktop = starCount(2560, 1440);
    expect(laptop).toBeGreaterThan(150);
    expect(desktop).toBeGreaterThan(laptop);
    expect(desktop).toBeLessThanOrEqual(400);
  });
});

describe('createStars', () => {
  it('draws the same field from the same seed', () => {
    expect(createStars(200, 7)).toEqual(createStars(200, 7));
    expect(createStars(200, 7)).not.toEqual(createStars(200, 8));
  });

  it('packs x, y, brightness and a drift speed of 0.5 to 3 px/s, slower when dimmer', () => {
    const stars = createStars(300, 11);
    expect(stars).toHaveLength(1200);
    for (let at = 0; at < 300; at += 1) {
      const brightness = stars[at * 4 + 2]!;
      const speed = stars[at * 4 + 3]!;
      expect(speed).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0.5);
      expect(speed).toBeLessThanOrEqual(3);
      expect(speed).toBeCloseTo(0.5 + 2.5 * brightness, 5);
    }
  });
});

describe('mulberry32', () => {
  it('returns values in [0, 1)', () => {
    const next = mulberry32(1);
    for (let at = 0; at < 1000; at += 1) {
      const value = next();
      expect(value).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
      expect(value).toBeLessThan(1);
    }
  });
});
```

```ts
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';

import type { SchedulerEnv } from './scheduler.js';
import {
  BACKGROUND_MARKER,
  startBackgroundWith,
  type BackgroundDeps,
} from './start.js';

function deps(overrides: Partial<BackgroundDeps> = {}) {
  const frames = new Map<number, (time: number) => void>();
  let next = 1;
  const renderer = { draw: vi.fn(), resize: vi.fn(), dispose: vi.fn() };
  const base: BackgroundDeps = {
    env: (draw, paused): SchedulerEnv => ({
      now: () => 0,
      requestFrame: (callback) => {
        const id = next++;
        frames.set(id, callback);
        return id;
      },
      cancelFrame: (id) => void frames.delete(id),
      draw,
      reducedMotion: () => false,
      saveData: () => false,
      paused,
      hidden: () => false,
      charging: () => null,
    }),
    createWebGl: vi.fn(() => renderer),
    drawStatic: vi.fn(() => true),
    size: () => ({ width: 1440, height: 900, dpr: 2 }),
    listen: () => () => undefined,
    ...overrides,
  };
  return { base, frames, renderer };
}

describe('startBackgroundWith', () => {
  it('marks the canvas so the budget check finds the chunk', () => {
    const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
    const { base } = deps();
    startBackgroundWith(canvas, { theme: 'dark' }, base);
    expect(canvas.dataset['background']).toBe(BACKGROUND_MARKER);
    expect(canvas.dataset['renderer']).toBe('webgl2');
  });

  it('sizes the render target at half width and half height of the device pixels', () => {
    const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
    const { base, renderer } = deps();
    startBackgroundWith(canvas, { theme: 'dark' }, base);
    expect(canvas.width).toBe(1440);
    expect(canvas.height).toBe(900);
    expect(renderer.resize).toHaveBeenCalledWith(1440, 900, 2);
  });

  it('draws one static canvas 2D frame and no loop without WebGL2', () => {
    const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
    const { base, frames } = deps({ createWebGl: vi.fn(() => null) });
    startBackgroundWith(canvas, { theme: 'dark' }, base);
    expect(base.drawStatic).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(frames.size).toBe(0);
    expect(canvas.dataset['renderer']).toBe('canvas2d');
  });

  it('falls back to one canvas 2D frame when the context is lost', () => {
    const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
    let lost: () => void = () => undefined;
    const renderer = { draw: vi.fn(), resize: vi.fn(), dispose: vi.fn() };
    const { base, frames } = deps({
      createWebGl: vi.fn((_canvas, _seed, onLost: () => void) => {
        lost = onLost;
        return renderer;
      }),
    });
    startBackgroundWith(canvas, { theme: 'dark' }, base);
    lost();
    expect(renderer.dispose).toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(base.drawStatic).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(frames.size).toBe(0);
  });

  it('draws nothing in light mode and resumes in dark mode', () => {
    const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
    const { base, frames } = deps();
    const handle = startBackgroundWith(canvas, { theme: 'light' }, base);
    expect(base.createWebGl).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(frames.size).toBe(0);
    expect(canvas.dataset['renderer']).toBe('none');
    handle.setTheme('dark');
    expect(base.createWebGl).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(frames.size).toBe(1);
  });

  it('draws the seeded first frame and no loop when frozen', () => {
    const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
    const { base, frames, renderer } = deps();
    startBackgroundWith(canvas, { theme: 'dark', frozen: true }, base);
    expect(renderer.draw).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(renderer.draw).toHaveBeenCalledWith(0);
    expect(frames.size).toBe(0);
  });

  it('draws one frame and no loop when paused, and loops again when unpaused', () => {
    const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
    const { base, frames, renderer } = deps();
    const handle = startBackgroundWith(
      canvas,
      { theme: 'dark', paused: true },
      base,
    );
    expect(renderer.draw).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(frames.size).toBe(0);
    handle.setPaused(false);
    expect(frames.size).toBe(1);
  });

  it('releases the renderer, the frame and the listeners on stop', () => {
    const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
    const unlisten = vi.fn();
    const { base, frames, renderer } = deps({ listen: () => unlisten });
    const handle = startBackgroundWith(canvas, { theme: 'dark' }, base);
    handle.stop();
    expect(renderer.dispose).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(unlisten).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(frames.size).toBe(0);
  });
});
```

`internal/meridian-ui/src/background/stars.ts`:

```ts
/** A small seeded PRNG, so a seed always draws the same field. */
export function mulberry32(seed: number): () => number {
  let state = seed >>> 0;
  return () => {
    state = (state + 0x6d2b79f5) >>> 0;
    let value = state;
    value = Math.imul(value ^ (value >>> 15), value | 1);
    value ^= value + Math.imul(value ^ (value >>> 7), value | 61);
    return ((value ^ (value >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
  };
}

/**
 * 300 stars per 1920 by 1080 of viewport area, clamped to 150 and 400
 * (spec §9.1).
 */
export function starCount(width: number, height: number): number {
  const scaled = ((width * height) / (1920 * 1080)) * 300;
  return Math.round(Math.min(400, Math.max(150, scaled)));
}

/**
 * Four floats per star: x and y in [0, 1), brightness in [0, 1), and a drift
 * speed in CSS px/s from 0.5 to 3, slower for dimmer stars (spec §9.2).
 */
export function createStars(count: number, seed: number): Float32Array {
  const next = mulberry32(seed);
  const stars = new Float32Array(count * 4);
  for (let at = 0; at < count; at += 1) {
    const brightness = next();
    stars[at * 4] = next();
    stars[at * 4 + 1] = next();
    stars[at * 4 + 2] = brightness;
    stars[at * 4 + 3] = 0.5 + 2.5 * brightness;
  }
  return stars;
}
```

```ts
import { createStars, starCount } from './stars.js';

export interface Renderer {
  draw(timeMs: number): void;
  resize(cssWidth: number, cssHeight: number, dpr: number): void;
  dispose(): void;
}

/** A full-screen triangle from gl_VertexID, so the clouds need no buffer. */
const CLOUD_VERTEX = `#version 300 es
void main() {
  vec2 p = vec2(float((gl_VertexID << 1) & 2), float(gl_VertexID & 2));
  gl_Position = vec4(p * 2.0 - 1.0, 0.0, 1.0);
}`;

/**
 * Three layers of value noise, four octaves at most, each tinted by one cloud
 * colour at low alpha. Each layer translates one unit per period (120, 180 and
 * 240 s) and swells in opacity on its own period (12, 16 and 20 s). Output is
 * premultiplied, so the CSS gradient on html shows through.
 */
const CLOUD_FRAGMENT = `#version 300 es
precision mediump float;
uniform vec2 u_resolution;
uniform float u_time;
uniform float u_seed;
out vec4 outColor;
const float TAU = 6.2831853;
float hash(vec2 p) {
  p = fract(p * vec2(123.34, 456.21) + u_seed);
  p += dot(p, p + 45.32);
  return fract(p.x * p.y);
}
float noise(vec2 p) {
  vec2 i = floor(p);
  vec2 f = fract(p);
  vec2 u = f * f * (3.0 - 2.0 * f);
  return mix(mix(hash(i), hash(i + vec2(1.0, 0.0)), u.x),
             mix(hash(i + vec2(0.0, 1.0)), hash(i + vec2(1.0, 1.0)), u.x), u.y);
}
float fbm(vec2 p) {
  float value = 0.0;
  float amplitude = 0.5;
  for (int octave = 0; octave < 4; octave++) {
    value += amplitude * noise(p);
    p *= 2.0;
    amplitude *= 0.5;
  }
  return value;
}
float layer(vec2 uv, vec2 direction, float period, float swell, float offset) {
  vec2 p = uv * 2.2 + direction * (u_time / period) + offset;
  float cloud = smoothstep(0.45, 0.85, fbm(p));
  return cloud * (0.75 + 0.25 * sin(TAU * u_time / swell));
}
void main() {
  vec2 uv = gl_FragCoord.xy / u_resolution;
  uv.x *= u_resolution.x / u_resolution.y;
  float cyan = layer(uv, vec2(1.0, 0.2), 120.0, 12.0, 0.0);
  float magenta = layer(uv, vec2(-0.6, 0.8), 180.0, 16.0, 17.0);
  float violet = layer(uv, vec2(0.3, -1.0), 240.0, 20.0, 41.0);
  vec3 colour = vec3(0.369, 0.918, 1.0) * cyan * 0.18
              + vec3(1.0, 0.369, 0.784) * magenta * 0.14
              + vec3(0.545, 0.424, 1.0) * violet * 0.16;
  float alpha = clamp(cyan * 0.18 + magenta * 0.14 + violet * 0.16, 0.0, 0.4);
  outColor = vec4(colour, alpha);
}`;

/** Stars as point sprites; x drifts at the star's own speed in CSS px/s. */
const STAR_VERTEX = `#version 300 es
in vec4 a_star;
uniform float u_time;
uniform vec2 u_css;
uniform float u_scale;
out float v_bright;
void main() {
  vec2 p = fract(a_star.xy + vec2(a_star.w * u_time / u_css.x, 0.0));
  gl_Position = vec4(p * 2.0 - 1.0, 0.0, 1.0);
  gl_PointSize = mix(1.0, 2.5, a_star.z) * u_scale;
  v_bright = a_star.z;
}`;

const STAR_FRAGMENT = `#version 300 es
precision mediump float;
in float v_bright;
out vec4 outColor;
void main() {
  float d = length(gl_PointCoord - 0.5);
  float a = smoothstep(0.5, 0.0, d) * mix(0.25, 0.9, v_bright);
  outColor = vec4(vec3(0.91, 0.93, 1.0) * a, a);
}`;

function compile(
  gl: WebGL2RenderingContext,
  kind: number,
  source: string,
): WebGLShader | null {
  const shader = gl.createShader(kind);
  if (!shader) return null;
  gl.shaderSource(shader, source);
  gl.compileShader(shader);
  if (!gl.getShaderParameter(shader, gl.COMPILE_STATUS)) {
    gl.deleteShader(shader);
    return null;
  }
  return shader;
}

function link(
  gl: WebGL2RenderingContext,
  vertex: string,
  fragment: string,
): WebGLProgram | null {
  const v = compile(gl, gl.VERTEX_SHADER, vertex);
  const f = compile(gl, gl.FRAGMENT_SHADER, fragment);
  const program = gl.createProgram();
  if (!v || !f || !program) return null;
  gl.attachShader(program, v);
  gl.attachShader(program, f);
  gl.linkProgram(program);
  gl.deleteShader(v);
  gl.deleteShader(f);
  if (!gl.getProgramParameter(program, gl.LINK_STATUS)) {
    gl.deleteProgram(program);
    return null;
  }
  return program;
}

/**
 * One render target (the canvas, sized by the caller at half width and half
 * height), one vertex buffer (the stars), no textures. Returns null when the
 * browser offers no WebGL2 or a shader fails, so the caller draws the canvas
 * 2D frame.
 */
export function createWebGlRenderer(
  canvas: HTMLCanvasElement,
  seed: number,
  onLost: () => void,
): Renderer | null {
  const gl = canvas.getContext('webgl2', {
    alpha: true,
    premultipliedAlpha: true,
    antialias: false,
    powerPreference: 'low-power',
  }) as WebGL2RenderingContext | null;
  if (!gl) return null;

  const clouds = link(gl, CLOUD_VERTEX, CLOUD_FRAGMENT);
  const starsProgram = link(gl, STAR_VERTEX, STAR_FRAGMENT);
  if (!clouds || !starsProgram) return null;

  const buffer = gl.createBuffer();
  const vao = gl.createVertexArray();
  let count = 0;
  let css = { width: 1, height: 1, dpr: 1 };

  const cloudUniforms = {
    resolution: gl.getUniformLocation(clouds, 'u_resolution'),
    time: gl.getUniformLocation(clouds, 'u_time'),
    seed: gl.getUniformLocation(clouds, 'u_seed'),
  };
  const starUniforms = {
    time: gl.getUniformLocation(starsProgram, 'u_time'),
    css: gl.getUniformLocation(starsProgram, 'u_css'),
    scale: gl.getUniformLocation(starsProgram, 'u_scale'),
  };

  const lost = (event: Event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    onLost();
  };
  canvas.addEventListener('webglcontextlost', lost);

  gl.enable(gl.BLEND);
  gl.blendFunc(gl.ONE, gl.ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA);

  return {
    resize(cssWidth, cssHeight, dpr) {
      css = { width: cssWidth, height: cssHeight, dpr };
      count = starCount(cssWidth, cssHeight);
      gl.bindVertexArray(vao);
      gl.bindBuffer(gl.ARRAY_BUFFER, buffer);
      gl.bufferData(gl.ARRAY_BUFFER, createStars(count, seed), gl.STATIC_DRAW);
      const location = gl.getAttribLocation(starsProgram, 'a_star');
      gl.enableVertexAttribArray(location);
      gl.vertexAttribPointer(location, 4, gl.FLOAT, false, 0, 0);
      gl.viewport(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
    },
    draw(timeMs) {
      const seconds = timeMs / 1000;
      gl.clearColor(0, 0, 0, 0);
      gl.clear(gl.COLOR_BUFFER_BIT);

      gl.useProgram(clouds);
      gl.uniform2f(cloudUniforms.resolution, canvas.width, canvas.height);
      gl.uniform1f(cloudUniforms.time, seconds);
      gl.uniform1f(cloudUniforms.seed, (seed % 997) / 997);
      gl.drawArrays(gl.TRIANGLES, 0, 3);

      gl.useProgram(starsProgram);
      gl.bindVertexArray(vao);
      gl.uniform1f(starUniforms.time, seconds);
      gl.uniform2f(starUniforms.css, css.width, css.height);
      gl.uniform1f(starUniforms.scale, css.dpr / 2);
      gl.drawArrays(gl.POINTS, 0, count);
    },
    dispose() {
      canvas.removeEventListener('webglcontextlost', lost);
      gl.deleteBuffer(buffer);
      gl.deleteVertexArray(vao);
      gl.deleteProgram(clouds);
      gl.deleteProgram(starsProgram);
      gl.getExtension('WEBGL_lose_context')?.loseContext();
    },
  };
}
```

`internal/meridian-ui/src/background/renderer-canvas2d.ts`:

```ts
import { createStars, mulberry32, starCount } from './stars.js';

const CLOUDS = [
  [94, 234, 255, 0.16],
  [255, 94, 200, 0.12],
  [139, 108, 255, 0.14],
] as const;

/**
 * One static frame for a browser without WebGL2 or after a lost context: a
 * radial gradient per cloud and the star field. Returns false when the
 * browser offers no 2D context either.
 */
export function drawStaticFrame(
  canvas: HTMLCanvasElement,
  seed: number,
): boolean {
  const context = canvas.getContext('2d');
  if (!context) return false;

  const { width, height } = canvas;
  const next = mulberry32(seed);
  context.clearRect(0, 0, width, height);

  for (const [red, green, blue, alpha] of CLOUDS) {
    const x = next() * width;
    const y = next() * height;
    const radius = (0.35 + next() * 0.3) * Math.max(width, height);
    const gradient = context.createRadialGradient(x, y, 0, x, y, radius);
    gradient.addColorStop(0, `rgb(${red} ${green} ${blue} / ${alpha})`);
    gradient.addColorStop(1, `rgb(${red} ${green} ${blue} / 0)`);
    context.fillStyle = gradient;
    context.fillRect(0, 0, width, height);
  }

  const count = starCount(width * 2, height * 2);
  const stars = createStars(count, seed);
  for (let at = 0; at < count; at += 1) {
    const brightness = stars[at * 4 + 2] as number;
    context.fillStyle = `rgb(232 237 255 / ${0.25 + 0.65 * brightness})`;
    context.fillRect(
      (stars[at * 4] as number) * width,
      (stars[at * 4 + 1] as number) * height,
      1,
      1,
    );
  }
  return true;
}
```

`internal/meridian-ui/src/background/start.ts`:

```ts
import type { Renderer } from './renderer-webgl.js';
import { createScheduler, type SchedulerEnv } from './scheduler.js';

/** The string `check-budgets.mjs` looks for to find this module's chunk. */
export const BACKGROUND_MARKER = 'meridian-background';

export interface BackgroundOptions {
  seed?: number;
  theme: 'dark' | 'light';
  paused?: boolean;
  frozen?: boolean;
}

export interface BackgroundHandle {
  stop(): void;
  setTheme(theme: 'dark' | 'light'): void;
  setPaused(paused: boolean): void;
}

export interface BackgroundDeps {
  /** The scheduler environment, given the draw callback and the pause reader. */
  env(draw: (time: number) => void, paused: () => boolean): SchedulerEnv;
  createWebGl(
    canvas: HTMLCanvasElement,
    seed: number,
    onLost: () => void,
  ): Renderer | null;
  drawStatic(canvas: HTMLCanvasElement, seed: number): boolean;
  size(): { width: number; height: number; dpr: number };
  /** Subscribes `refresh` and `activity` to the browser's events; returns the unsubscribe. */
  listen(handlers: {
    refresh(): void;
    activity(): void;
    resize(): void;
  }): () => void;
}

export function startBackgroundWith(
  canvas: HTMLCanvasElement,
  options: BackgroundOptions,
  deps: BackgroundDeps,
): BackgroundHandle {
  const seed = options.seed ?? 7;
  let theme = options.theme;
  let paused = options.paused ?? false;
  let renderer: Renderer | null = null;
  let degraded = false;

  canvas.dataset['background'] = BACKGROUND_MARKER;

  const resize = () => {
    const { width, height, dpr } = deps.size();
    canvas.width = Math.max(1, Math.floor((width * dpr) / 2));
    canvas.height = Math.max(1, Math.floor((height * dpr) / 2));
    renderer?.resize(width, height, dpr);
  };

  const fallback = () => {
    renderer?.dispose();
    renderer = null;
    degraded = true;
    scheduler.stop();
    canvas.dataset['renderer'] = deps.drawStatic(canvas, seed)
      ? 'canvas2d'
      : 'none';
  };

  // A stopped scheduler stays stopped, so a switch back to dark builds a new one.
  const newScheduler = () =>
    createScheduler(
      deps.env(
        (time) => renderer?.draw(time),
        () => paused || options.frozen === true,
      ),
    );
  let scheduler = newScheduler();

  const begin = () => {
    if (theme === 'light' || degraded) {
      canvas.dataset['renderer'] = degraded
        ? canvas.dataset['renderer']
        : 'none';
      return;
    }
    scheduler.stop();
    scheduler = newScheduler();
    renderer = deps.createWebGl(canvas, seed, fallback);
    if (!renderer) {
      fallback();
      return;
    }
    canvas.dataset['renderer'] = 'webgl2';
    resize();
    if (options.frozen) {
      renderer.draw(0);
      return;
    }
    scheduler.start();
  };

  const unlisten = deps.listen({
    refresh: () => scheduler.refresh(),
    activity: () => scheduler.activity(),
    resize,
  });

  begin();

  return {
    stop() {
      scheduler.stop();
      unlisten();
      renderer?.dispose();
      renderer = null;
    },
    setTheme(next) {
      if (next === theme) return;
      theme = next;
      if (theme === 'light') {
        scheduler.stop();
        renderer?.dispose();
        renderer = null;
        canvas.dataset['renderer'] = 'none';
        return;
      }
      begin();
    },
    setPaused(next) {
      paused = next;
      scheduler.refresh();
    },
  };
}
```

`internal/meridian-ui/src/background/browser-env.ts`:

```ts
import type { BackgroundDeps } from './start.js';
import { createWebGlRenderer } from './renderer-webgl.js';
import { drawStaticFrame } from './renderer-canvas2d.js';

interface BatteryManagerLike extends EventTarget {
  charging: boolean;
}

/** The browser half of the background: media queries, visibility, battery, input. */
export function browserDeps(): BackgroundDeps {
  const motion = matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)');
  let charging: boolean | null = null;
  const navigatorWithBattery = navigator as Navigator & {
    getBattery?: () => Promise<BatteryManagerLike>;
    connection?: { saveData?: boolean };
  };

  return {
    env: (draw, paused) => ({
      now: () => performance.now(),
      requestFrame: (callback) => requestAnimationFrame(callback),
      cancelFrame: (id) => cancelAnimationFrame(id),
      draw,
      reducedMotion: () => motion.matches,
      saveData: () => navigatorWithBattery.connection?.saveData === true,
      paused,
      hidden: () => document.visibilityState === 'hidden',
      charging: () => charging,
    }),
    createWebGl: createWebGlRenderer,
    drawStatic: drawStaticFrame,
    size: () => ({
      width: innerWidth,
      height: innerHeight,
      dpr: Math.min(devicePixelRatio || 1, 2),
    }),
    listen({ refresh, activity, resize }) {
      const input = [
        'pointermove',
        'pointerdown',
        'keydown',
        'scroll',
        'touchstart',
      ] as const;
      for (const name of input)
        addEventListener(name, activity, { passive: true });
      document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', refresh);
      motion.addEventListener('change', refresh);
      addEventListener('resize', resize);

      let battery: BatteryManagerLike | null = null;
      const onBattery = () => {
        charging = battery?.charging ?? null;
      };
      navigatorWithBattery
        .getBattery?.()
        .then((manager) => {
          battery = manager;
          onBattery();
          manager.addEventListener('chargingchange', onBattery);
        })
        .catch(() => undefined);

      return () => {
        for (const name of input) removeEventListener(name, activity);
        document.removeEventListener('visibilitychange', refresh);
        motion.removeEventListener('change', refresh);
        removeEventListener('resize', resize);
        battery?.removeEventListener('chargingchange', onBattery);
      };
    },
  };
}
```

```ts
/**
 * The nebula background (spec §9). The `@nexusdi/meridian-ui/background`

import { browserDeps } from './browser-env.js';
import {
  BACKGROUND_MARKER,
  startBackgroundWith,
  type BackgroundHandle,
  type BackgroundOptions,
} from './start.js';

export { BACKGROUND_MARKER };
export type { BackgroundHandle, BackgroundOptions };

export function startBackground(
  canvas: HTMLCanvasElement,
  options: BackgroundOptions,
): BackgroundHandle {

}
```

```tsx
  __resetPauseMemory,
  readPaused,

/** A Storage whose every access throws, as Safari private mode and blocked site data do. */

  getItem() {
    throw new DOMException('denied', 'SecurityError');
  },
  setItem() {
    throw new DOMException('denied', 'QuotaExceededError');
  },
} as unknown as Storage;

function memoryStorage(): Storage {

  return {
    getItem: (key: string) => values.get(key) ?? null,
    setItem: (key: string, value: string) => void values.set(key, value),
  } as unknown as Storage;
}
```

`apps/docs/components/background/pause.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * The reader's "Pause background" preference (spec §16.1, WCAG 2.2.2).
 *
 * Every storage access sits inside try: Safari private mode, blocked site data
 * and some embedded browsers throw on the `localStorage` getter itself or on
 * `setItem`. When storage throws, the choice lives in module memory for the
 * session, so the switch still works.
 */

export const PAUSE_KEY = 'nexusdi:pause-background';

const EVENT = 'nexusdi:pause-background';

let memory: boolean | null = null;

function defaultStorage(): Storage | undefined {
  try {
    return globalThis.localStorage;
  } catch {
    return undefined;
  }
}

export function readPaused(
  storage: Storage | undefined = defaultStorage(),
): boolean {
  try {
    if (storage) return storage.getItem(PAUSE_KEY) === '1';
  } catch {
    // Storage refused the read; the session value below applies.
  }
  return memory ?? false;
}

export function writePaused(
  value: boolean,
  storage: Storage | undefined = defaultStorage(),
): void {
  memory = value;
  try {
    storage?.setItem(PAUSE_KEY, value ? '1' : '0');
  } catch {
    // Storage refused the write; `memory` holds the choice for this session.
  }
  globalThis.dispatchEvent?.(
    new CustomEvent<boolean>(EVENT, { detail: value }),
  );
}

export function subscribePaused(
  listener: (paused: boolean) => void,
): () => void {
  const handler = (event: Event) =>
    listener((event as CustomEvent<boolean>).detail);
  globalThis.addEventListener?.(EVENT, handler);
  return () => globalThis.removeEventListener?.(EVENT, handler);
}

/** Test hook: clears the session value between tests. */
export function __resetPauseMemory(): void {
  memory = null;
}
```

`apps/docs/components/background/PauseSwitch.tsx`:

```tsx
'use client';

import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';

import { readPaused, subscribePaused, writePaused } from './pause';

/** The footer and tool-header switch that pauses the background. */
export default function PauseSwitch() {
  const [paused, setPaused] = useState(false);

  useEffect(() => {
    setPaused(readPaused());
    return subscribePaused(setPaused);
  }, []);

  return (
    <button
      type="button"
      className="nexus-pause-switch"
      aria-pressed={paused}
      onClick={() => {
        const next = !paused;
        setPaused(next);
        writePaused(next);
      }}
    >
      Pause background
    </button>
  );
}
```

```tsx
'use client';

import {
  startBackground,
  type BackgroundHandle,
} from '@nexusdi/meridian-ui/background';
import { useTheme } from 'next-themes';
import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';

import { readPaused, subscribePaused } from './pause';

/**
 * Mounts the nebula behind every page (spec §9.1, §9.3). The module starts
 * after the page's load event, inside requestIdleCallback with a 2-second
 * timeout fallback, so the content paints first. `?background=frozen` draws
 * the seeded first frame with no loop, for the visual checks.
 */
export default function BackgroundCanvas() {
  const canvas = useRef<HTMLCanvasElement>(null);
  const handle = useRef<BackgroundHandle | null>(null);
  const { resolvedTheme } = useTheme();
  const theme = resolvedTheme === 'light' ? 'light' : 'dark';
  const themeRef = useRef(theme);

  useEffect(() => {
    const element = canvas.current;
    if (!element) return;
    let cancelled = false;
    let idle: number | null = null;
    let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;

    const begin = () => {
      if (cancelled || handle.current) return;
      handle.current = startBackground(element, {
        theme: themeRef.current,
        paused: readPaused(),
        frozen:
          new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('background') === 'frozen',
      });
    };

    const schedule = () => {
      if ('requestIdleCallback' in window) {
        idle = window.requestIdleCallback(begin, { timeout: 2000 });
      } else {
        timer = setTimeout(begin, 2000);
      }
    };

    if (document.readyState === 'complete') schedule();
    else window.addEventListener('load', schedule, { once: true });

    const unsubscribe = subscribePaused((paused) =>
      handle.current?.setPaused(paused),
    );

    return () => {
      cancelled = true;
      window.removeEventListener('load', schedule);
      if (idle !== null) window.cancelIdleCallback(idle);
      if (timer !== null) clearTimeout(timer);
      unsubscribe();
      handle.current?.stop();
      handle.current = null;
    };
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => {
    themeRef.current = theme;
    handle.current?.setTheme(theme);
  }, [theme]);

  return (
    <canvas
      ref={canvas}
      className="nexus-background"
      aria-hidden="true"
      tabIndex={-1}
    />
  );
}
```

`apps/docs-e2e/src/background.spec.ts`:

```ts
import { expect, test, type Page } from '@playwright/test';

/**
 * Counts drawArrays calls on the background canvas. The wrapper sits on the
 * prototype before any page script runs, so the module needs no test hook.
 */
const COUNT_DRAWS = `
  window.__backgroundDraws = 0;
  const original = WebGL2RenderingContext.prototype.drawArrays;
  WebGL2RenderingContext.prototype.drawArrays = function (...args) {
    if (this.canvas && this.canvas.dataset && this.canvas.dataset.background === 'meridian-background') {
      window.__backgroundDraws += 1;
    }
    return original.apply(this, args);
  };
`;

async function renderer(page: Page): Promise<string> {
  const canvas = page.locator('canvas[data-background="meridian-background"]');
  await expect(canvas).toHaveAttribute('data-renderer', /.+/, {
    timeout: 10_000,
  });
  return (await canvas.getAttribute('data-renderer')) ?? 'none';
}

const draws = (page: Page) =>
  page.evaluate(
    () =>
      (window as unknown as { __backgroundDraws: number }).__backgroundDraws,
  );

test.describe('the background', () => {
  test('draws one frame and no loop under reduced motion', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce', colorScheme: 'dark' });
    await page.addInitScript(COUNT_DRAWS);
    await page.goto('/next/');
    test.skip(
      (await renderer(page)) !== 'webgl2',
      'this engine draws the static canvas 2D frame',
    );
    const first = await draws(page);
    expect(first).toBeLessThanOrEqual(2);
    await page.waitForTimeout(2000);
    expect(await draws(page)).toBe(first);
  });

  test('stops drawing in a hidden tab', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: 'dark' });
    await page.addInitScript(COUNT_DRAWS);
    await page.goto('/next/');
    test.skip(
      (await renderer(page)) !== 'webgl2',
      'this engine draws the static canvas 2D frame',
    );
    await page.waitForTimeout(500);
    expect(await draws(page)).toBeGreaterThan(2);

    await page.evaluate(() => {
      Object.defineProperty(document, 'visibilityState', {
        configurable: true,
        get: () => 'hidden',
      });
      document.dispatchEvent(new Event('visibilitychange'));
    });
    const hidden = await draws(page);
    await page.waitForTimeout(2000);
    expect(await draws(page)).toBe(hidden);
  });

  test('stays inside the main-thread budget over 10 seconds', async ({
    page,
    browserName,
  }) => {
    test.skip(
      browserName !== 'chromium',
      'the trace uses the Chrome DevTools Protocol',
    );
    await page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: 'dark' });
    await page.goto('/next/');
    test.skip(
      (await renderer(page)) !== 'webgl2',
      'no loop runs without WebGL2',
    );

    const chunk = await page.evaluate(async () => {
      const sources = [...document.querySelectorAll('script[src]')].map(
        (script) => (script as HTMLScriptElement).src,
      );
      for (const source of sources) {
        const text = await (await fetch(source)).text();
        if (text.includes('meridian-background')) return source;
      }
      return null;
    });
    expect(
      chunk,
      'no script chunk carries the background marker',
    ).not.toBeNull();

    const session = await page.context().newCDPSession(page);
    const events: {
      name: string;
      dur?: number;
      args?: { data?: { url?: string } };
    }[] = [];
    session.on('Tracing.dataCollected', ({ value }) => events.push(...value));
    const finished = new Promise<void>((resolve) =>
      session.once('Tracing.tracingComplete', () => resolve()),
    );
    await session.send('Tracing.start', {
      categories: 'devtools.timeline',
      transferMode: 'ReportEvents',
    });
    await page.waitForTimeout(10_000);
    await session.send('Tracing.end');
    await finished;

    const calls = events.filter(
      (event) =>
        event.name === 'FunctionCall' && event.args?.data?.url === chunk,
    );
    const totalUs = calls.reduce((sum, event) => sum + (event.dur ?? 0), 0);
    const longest = Math.max(0, ...calls.map((event) => event.dur ?? 0));
    const meanUs = calls.length ? totalUs / calls.length : 0;

    expect(
      totalUs,
      'background main-thread time over 10 s, in µs',
    ).toBeLessThanOrEqual(300_000);
    expect(longest, 'longest background task, in µs').toBeLessThanOrEqual(
      50_000,
    );
    expect(meanUs, 'mean background frame, in µs').toBeLessThanOrEqual(1_000);
  });
});
```

## Group D: The doc-examples loaders

Group D copies the docs-coupled half of the libraries' `tools/doc-examples` at LIBS_SHA into the package the port PR created: the region reader and its loader, the declaration reader, the behaviour reader and the reference loader with a required `classPrefix`, and the `.md` sibling writer. It then registers the region and reference loaders in the app's chain and adds the build steps they need. The standalone half (`expect-comments.ts`, `vite-plugin.ts`, `vite-config.ts`, `index.ts`) is already on `main` and stays as it is apart from new re-exports.

import { mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';

import { expandRegions } from '@nexusdi/doc-examples/mdx-region-loader';
import { RegionError } from '@nexusdi/doc-examples/regions';

const fence = '```';

beforeAll(() => {
  root = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'nexusdi-regions-'));
  mkdirSync(join(root, 'libs/core'), { recursive: true });
  writeFileSync(
    join(root, 'libs/core/README.md'),
    [
      '# NexusDI',
      '',
      '<!-- #region first-ship -->',
      `${fence}ts`,
      'const frequency = 1420;',
      fence,
      '<!-- #endregion first-ship -->',
      '',
    ].join('\n'),
  );
  writeFileSync(
    join(root, 'libs/core/doc-examples.preamble.ts'),
    "import { Nexus } from '@nexusdi/core';\n",
  );
});

afterAll(() => rmSync(root, { recursive: true, force: true }));

describe('expandRegions', () => {
  it('fills an empty fence from the named README region', () => {
    expect(
      expandRegions(
        `${fence}ts file=libs/core/README.md region=first-ship\n${fence}\n`,
        root,
        'tokens.mdx',
      ),
    ).toBe(`${fence}ts\nconst frequency = 1420;\n${fence}\n`);
  });

  it('puts the README preamble behind a cut in a twoslash fence', () => {
    const out = expandRegions(
      `${fence}ts twoslash file=libs/core/README.md region=first-ship\n${fence}\n`,
      root,
      'tokens.mdx',
    );

    expect(out).toBe(
      `${fence}ts twoslash\nimport { Nexus } from '@nexusdi/core';\n// ---cut---\nconst frequency = 1420;\n${fence}\n`,
    );
  });

      expandRegions(
        `${fence}ts file=libs/core/README.md region=first-ship\nstale\n${fence}\n`,
        root,
        'tokens.mdx',
      ),
    ).not.toContain('stale');
  });

  it('fails the build on a region the README does not have', () => {
    expect(() =>
      expandRegions(
        `${fence}ts file=libs/core/README.md region=missing\n${fence}\n`,
        root,

    ).toThrow(RegionError);

});

- [ ] Step 4: Thread `classPrefix` through the reference loader

Save this script outside the repository as `$TMPDIR/class-prefix.mjs` and run it from the workspace root with `node "$TMPDIR/class-prefix.mjs"`. It changes each named line exactly once and throws when a line is missing or repeated, so a drifted copy fails loudly. Do not commit the script.

```js
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';

const path = 'tools/doc-examples/src/mdx-reference-loader.mjs';
let src = readFileSync(path, 'utf8');

function once(from, to) {
  const count = src.split(from).length - 1;
  if (count !== 1) {
    throw new Error(
      `expected one ${JSON.stringify(from)} in ${path}, found ${count}`,
    );
  }
  src = src.replace(from, to);
}

// The helpers that write markup take the prefix as a parameter.
once(
  'function signatureFence(reference) {',
  'function signatureFence(reference, prefix) {',
);
once(
  'function statedBlock(reference, behaviours, library) {',
  'function statedBlock(reference, behaviours, library, prefix) {',
);
once('function head(reference) {', 'function head(reference, prefix) {');
once(
  'function foot(root, reference, behaviours, example, file) {',
  'function foot(root, reference, behaviours, example, file, prefix) {',
);
once('...signatureFence(reference)]', '...signatureFence(reference, prefix)]');
once(
  'statedBlock(reference, behaviours, libraryOf(reference))',
  'statedBlock(reference, behaviours, libraryOf(reference), prefix)',
);
once(
  '...foot(root, open.reference, open.behaviours, open.example, file),',
  '...foot(root, open.reference, open.behaviours, open.example, file, prefix),',
);
once('...head(reference),', '...head(reference, prefix),');

// The options object replaces the positional `read` and `onResolve`.
once(
  `export function expandReferences(
  source,
  root,
  file,
  read = readReference,
  onResolve,
) {`,
  `/**
 * The class prefix every emitted element carries (docs spec §14.1, change 3).
 * It has no default, so a caller that forgets it fails at load time.
 */
function assertClassPrefix(prefix) {
  if (typeof prefix !== 'string' || !/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$/.test(prefix)) {
    throw new TypeError(
      \`expandReferences needs a classPrefix option such as 'nexus' (lower-case letters, digits and hyphens); received \${JSON.stringify(prefix)}.\`,
    );
  }
}

export function expandReferences(source, root, file, options) {
  const { classPrefix: prefix, read = readReference, onResolve } = options ?? {};
  assertClassPrefix(prefix);
`,
);
once(
  '  const { root } = this.getOptions();',
  '  const { root, classPrefix } = this.getOptions();',
);
once(
  `  return expandReferences(
    source,
    root,
    this.resourcePath,
    readReference,
    (reference, behaviours) => {`,
  `  return expandReferences(source, root, this.resourcePath, {
    classPrefix,
    read: readReference,
    onResolve: (reference, behaviours) => {`,
);
once('    },\n  );\n}\n', '    },\n  });\n}\n');

// Every class literal: a quoted string becomes a template reading `prefix`.
src = src.replace(
  /'([^'\n]*docs-api-entry[^'\n]*)'/g,
  (_, body) =>
    `\`${body.replaceAll('docs-api-entry', '${prefix}-api-entry')}\``,
);
src = src.replace(/`[^`\n]*`/g, (span) =>
  span
    .replaceAll('docs-api-entry', '${prefix}-api-entry')
    .replaceAll('baize-kind-', '${prefix}-kind-'),
);

if (/docs-api-entry|baize-kind-/.test(src)) {
  throw new Error('a libraries class name is left in the reference loader');
}

writeFileSync(path, src);
console.log(`rewrote ${path}`);
```

```ts
}
```

- [ ] Step 6: Register the region and reference loaders

`apps/docs/tools/loader-chain.mjs`:

```js
import { join } from 'node:path';

const tool = (name) => join(import.meta.dirname, name);

/**
 * The `*.mdx` loaders, in the order `turbopack.rules` lists them. Turbopack
 * runs the list from last to first:
 *
 * 1. the listing loader wraps a fence carrying an exemption tag in `<Listing>`;
 * 2. the diagram loader rewrites a mermaid fence into `<Diagram>`;
 * 3. the region loader fills every `file=… region=…` fence;
 * 4. the reference loader expands every `<!-- reference … -->` directive and
 *    fills its own example fence;
 * 5. the twoslash prelude runs last, over every fence the others wrote.
 */
export function mdxLoaderChain(workspaceRoot) {
  return [
    { loader: tool('mdx-twoslash-prelude.mjs') },
    {
      loader: '@nexusdi/doc-examples/mdx-reference-loader',
      options: { root: workspaceRoot, classPrefix: 'nexus' },
    },
    {
      loader: '@nexusdi/doc-examples/mdx-region-loader',
      options: { root: workspaceRoot },
    },
    { loader: tool('mdx-diagram-loader.mjs') },
    { loader: tool('mdx-listing-loader.mjs') },
  ];
}
```

`apps/docs/tools/md-siblings.mjs`:

```js
import { mkdirSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';

import { mdSiblings } from '@nexusdi/doc-examples/md-siblings';

/**
 * Writes the `.md` sibling of every page into the static export: `tokens.mdx`
 * becomes `out/tokens.md`, served at `/next/tokens.md` on the /next/ build.
 *
 * A file writer, because the optional catch-all owns every path and a route
 * handler beside it would conflict. It runs from `postbuild`, ahead of
 * Pagefind, which the docs workflow calls as its own step.
 */

const app = join(import.meta.dirname, '..');
const out = join(app, 'out');

const siblings = mdSiblings(join(app, 'content'), join(app, '../..'), {
  classPrefix: 'nexus',
});

for (const [route, markdown] of siblings) {
  const path = join(out, route);
  mkdirSync(dirname(path), { recursive: true });
  writeFileSync(path, markdown);
}

console.log(`wrote ${siblings.size} .md siblings to apps/docs/out`);
```

Set the script in `apps/docs/package.json`:

```json
    "postbuild": "node tools/md-siblings.mjs && node tools/pagefind.mjs"
```

## Group E: The guards and the ported reviewer

Group E ports the libraries docs guards to this site, adds the guards the spec names as new, and ports the reviewer agent and the `docs-page` skill. Every guard follows one shape: a pure rule module in `tools/repo-checks/src/docs/<name>.ts` that returns findings, a clean and a sabotaged fixture tree under `tools/repo-checks/src/__fixtures__/docs/<name>/`, a test file whose first `describe` holds the rule to the fixtures, and a second `describe` that runs the rule over `apps/docs`. Each finding names the file and the fix. The allowance files record the pages and exports Phase 2 has not written yet, and each carries a hygiene test, so an entry leaves the file when its page arrives.

- [ ] Step 5: Write `docs/site.ts`

```ts
import { existsSync, readdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join, relative, sep } from 'node:path';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';

import { workspaceRoot } from '@nx/devkit';
import { parse } from 'yaml';

/**
 * The docs content tree as the guards read it.
 *
 * Textual, the way the libraries guards read it: a fence, a heading and a JSX
 * tag are lines, and every rule here asks a question about lines. Each guard
 * takes the pages this module returns, so a rule runs against a fixture tree
 * and against `apps/docs/content` through the same code.
 */

export const EXEMPTION_TAGS = [
  'signature',
  'no-run',
  'anti-example',
  'fails-type-check',
  'elided',
] as const;

export const SHELL_LANGS = ['sh', 'bash', 'shell', 'console', 'zsh'] as const;

export interface DocsFence {
  lang: string;
  meta: string;
  tags: string[];
  body: string;
  line: number;
  section: string | null;
}

export interface DocsHeading {
  depth: number;
  text: string;
  slug: string;
  line: number;
}

export interface DocsSection {
  heading: DocsHeading;
  body: string;
  fences: DocsFence[];
}

export interface DocsPage {
  slug: string;
  file: string;
  source: string;
  body: string;
  frontmatter: Record<string, unknown>;
  kind: string | undefined;
  headings: DocsHeading[];
  fences: DocsFence[];
  sections: DocsSection[];
}

export interface MetaEntry {
  key: string;
  page: boolean;
  value: unknown;
}

const FENCE = /^(\s*)(`{3,})(.*)$/;
const HEADING = /^(#{1,6})\s+(.+?)\s*$/;

/** The anchor Nextra gives a heading: lower case, code marks and punctuation gone. */
export function slugify(text: string): string {
  return text
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/`/g, '')
    .replace(/[^\p{L}\p{N}\s_-]/gu, '')
    .trim()
    .replace(/\s+/g, '-');
}

/** The text with every fenced block removed. */
export function stripFences(text: string): string {
  const out: string[] = [];
  let open: string | null = null;

  for (const line of text.split('\n')) {
    const marker = FENCE.exec(line);
    if (marker && open === null) {
      open = marker[2] as string;
      continue;
    }
    if (open !== null) {
      if (marker && (marker[2] as string).startsWith(open)) open = null;
      continue;
    }
    out.push(line);
  }

  return out.join('\n');
}

function contentFiles(dir: string): string[] {
  return readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })
    .flatMap((entry) => {
      const path = join(dir, entry.name);
      if (entry.isDirectory()) return contentFiles(path);
      return /\.mdx?$/.test(entry.name) ? [path] : [];
    })
    .sort();
}

function splitFrontmatter(source: string): {
  frontmatter: Record<string, unknown>;
  body: string;
  offset: number;
} {
  const match = /^---\n([\s\S]*?)\n---\n/.exec(source);
  if (!match) return { frontmatter: {}, body: source, offset: 0 };

  const parsed = parse(match[1] ?? '') as unknown;

  return {
    frontmatter:
      parsed !== null && typeof parsed === 'object'
        ? (parsed as Record<string, unknown>)
        : {},
    body: source.slice(match[0].length),
    offset: match[0].split('\n').length - 1,
  };
}

/** One page, parsed. `file` is what a finding prints. */
export function parsePage(
  file: string,
  slug: string,
  source: string,
): DocsPage {
  const { frontmatter, body, offset } = splitFrontmatter(source);
  const headings: DocsHeading[] = [];
  const fences: DocsFence[] = [];
  const sections: DocsSection[] = [];
  let section: DocsSection | null = null;
  let sectionLines: string[] = [];
  let open: {
    ticks: string;
    lang: string;
    meta: string;
    line: number;
    body: string[];
  } | null = null;

  const closeSection = (): void => {
    if (section === null) return;
    section.body = sectionLines.join('\n');
    sections.push(section);
  };

  body.split('\n').forEach((text, index) => {
    const line = index + 1 + offset;
    const marker = FENCE.exec(text);

    if (open !== null) {
      if (
        marker &&
        (marker[2] as string).startsWith(open.ticks) &&
        (marker[3] as string).trim() === ''
      ) {
        const words = open.meta.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
        const fence: DocsFence = {
          lang: open.lang,
          meta: open.meta,
          tags: words.filter((word) =>
            (EXEMPTION_TAGS as readonly string[]).includes(word),
          ),
          body: open.body.join('\n'),
          line: open.line,
          section: section?.heading.text ?? null,
        };
        fences.push(fence);
        section?.fences.push(fence);
        open = null;
      } else {
        open.body.push(text);
      }
      sectionLines.push(text);
      return;
    }

    if (marker) {
      const [lang = '', ...rest] = (marker[3] as string).trim().split(/\s+/);
      open = {
        ticks: marker[2] as string,
        lang,
        meta: rest.join(' '),
        line,
        body: [],
      };
      sectionLines.push(text);
      return;
    }

    const heading = HEADING.exec(text);
    if (heading) {
      const found: DocsHeading = {
        depth: (heading[1] as string).length,
        text: heading[2] as string,
        slug: slugify(heading[2] as string),
        line,
      };
      headings.push(found);

      if (found.depth === 2) {
        closeSection();
        section = { heading: found, body: '', fences: [] };
        sectionLines = [];
        return;
      }
    }

    sectionLines.push(text);
  });

  closeSection();

  return {
    slug,
    file,
    source,
    body,
    frontmatter,
    kind: typeof frontmatter.kind === 'string' ? frontmatter.kind : undefined,
    headings,
    fences,
    sections,
  };
}

/**
 * Every `.mdx` and `.md` page under `contentDir`.
 *
 * `transform` runs on the source before it parses. The live guards pass the
 * region loader's `expandRegions` there, so a fence that cites a region is read
 * with the code the build puts in it.
 */
export function readSite(
  contentDir: string,
  options: { transform?: (source: string, file: string) => string } = {},
): DocsPage[] {
  return contentFiles(contentDir).map((path) => {
    const raw = readFileSync(path, 'utf8');
    const source = options.transform ? options.transform(raw, path) : raw;
    const slug = relative(contentDir, path)
      .split(sep)
      .join('/')
      .replace(/\.mdx?$/, '');

    return parsePage(relative(workspaceRoot, path), slug, source);
  });
}

/**
 * Every `_meta.ts` entry, in order, with a folder's entries after its own key.
 *
 * A separator and an entry with an `href` are navigation and name no page.
 */
export async function readMeta(
  contentDir: string,
  prefix = '',
): Promise<MetaEntry[]> {
  const file = join(contentDir, '_meta.ts');
  if (!existsSync(file)) return [];

  const module_ = (await import(pathToFileURL(file).href)) as {
    default: Record<string, unknown>;
  };
  const entries: MetaEntry[] = [];

  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(module_.default)) {
    const object =
      typeof value === 'object' && value !== null
        ? (value as Record<string, unknown>)
        : null;
    const page = !(
      object !== null &&
      (object.type === 'separator' || typeof object.href === 'string')
    );

    entries.push({ key: `${prefix}${key}`, page, value });

    if (page && existsSync(join(contentDir, key, '_meta.ts'))) {
      entries.push(
        ...(await readMeta(join(contentDir, key), `${prefix}${key}/`)),
      );
    }
  }

  return entries;
}

/** The `_meta.ts` keys that name a page or a folder, in order. */
export async function readMetaKeys(contentDir: string): Promise<string[]> {
  return (await readMeta(contentDir))
    .filter((entry) => entry.page)
    .map((entry) => entry.key);
}

/**
 * The page's prose lines with their source line numbers.
 *
 * Fences, imports, comments, JSX tags and code spans go. The text inside a
 * JSX element stays, because a notice's sentence is prose a reader reads.
 */
export function proseLines(page: DocsPage): { line: number; text: string }[] {
  const offset = page.source.split('\n').length - page.body.split('\n').length;
  const out: { line: number; text: string }[] = [];
  let open: string | null = null;

  page.body.split('\n').forEach((raw, index) => {
    const marker = FENCE.exec(raw);
    if (marker && open === null) {
      open = marker[2] as string;
      return;
    }
    if (open !== null) {
      if (marker && (marker[2] as string).startsWith(open)) open = null;
      return;
    }
    if (/^\s*(import|export)\s/.test(raw)) return;

    const text = raw
      .replace(/<!--.*?-->/g, '')
      .replace(/\{\/\*.*?\*\/\}/g, '')
      .replace(/<\/?[A-Za-z][^>]*>/g, ' ')
      .replace(/`[^`]*`/g, ' ')
      .replace(/\]\([^)]*\)/g, ']')
      .replace(/\s+/g, ' ')
      .trim();

    if (text !== '') out.push({ line: index + 1 + offset, text });
  });

  return out;
}

/** The prose of a page as one string. */
export function proseOf(page: DocsPage): string {
  return proseLines(page)
    .map((line) => line.text)
    .join('\n');
}

/** Semver order over `major.minor.patch` with an optional prerelease. */
export function compareVersions(a: string, b: string): number {
  const split = (version: string): [number[], string | null] => {
    const [core = '', pre] = version.split('-', 2);
    return [core.split('.').map(Number), pre ?? null];
  };
  const [coreA, preA] = split(a);
  const [coreB, preB] = split(b);

  for (let at = 0; at < 3; at += 1) {
    const delta = (coreA[at] ?? 0) - (coreB[at] ?? 0);
    if (delta !== 0) return delta;
  }
  if (preA === preB) return 0;
  if (preA === null) return 1;
  if (preB === null) return -1;
  return preA.localeCompare(preB, 'en', { numeric: true });
}

/**
 * A post that describes a version below 0.4.0.
 *
 * Amendment A2: such a post keeps its original text, 0.3 APIs included, so the
 * fence, domain, export and refused-word guards skip it.
 */
export function isPreFinalPost(page: DocsPage): boolean {
  const version = page.frontmatter.version;
  return (
    page.kind === 'post' &&
    typeof version === 'string' &&
    compareVersions(version, '0.4.0') < 0
  );
}
```

- [ ] Step 6: Write `docs/allowance.ts`

```ts
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';

/** An allowance or ratchet file, parsed. */
export function readAllowance<T>(file: string): T {
  return JSON.parse(readFileSync(file, 'utf8')) as T;
}

/**
 * A count that may only fall.
 *
 * `over` is a count above its entry (or above zero with no entry), `slack` an
 * entry above the count it covers, and `stale` an entry for a key that no
 * longer has a count. The libraries ratchets fail on all three, so the file
 * records the real number and nothing more.
 */
export function ratchet(
  actual: Record<string, number>,
  allowed: Record<string, number>,
): { over: string[]; slack: string[]; stale: string[] } {
  const over: string[] = [];
  const slack: string[] = [];

  for (const [key, count] of Object.entries(actual)) {
    const limit = allowed[key] ?? 0;
    if (count > limit) over.push(`${key}: ${count}, allowance ${limit}`);
    if (key in allowed && count < limit)
      slack.push(`${key}: ${count}, allowance ${limit}`);
  }

  const stale = Object.keys(allowed).filter((key) => !(key in actual));

  return { over: over.sort(), slack: slack.sort(), stale: stale.sort() };
}

/**
 * Work that is coming, keyed by what it is for, with the reason as the value.
 *
 * `stale` is an entry whose work is done, and `unexplained` an entry with an
 * empty reason. Both fail, so an allowance empties as Phase 2 lands.
 */
export function waits(
  done: ReadonlySet<string>,
  allowance: Record<string, string>,
): { stale: string[]; unexplained: string[] } {
  return {
    stale: Object.keys(allowance)
      .filter((key) => done.has(key))
      .sort(),
    unexplained: Object.entries(allowance)
      .filter(([, reason]) => reason.trim() === '')
      .map(([key]) => key)
      .sort(),
  };
}
```

- [ ] Step 4: Write `docs/doc-navigation.ts`

```ts
import { existsSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';

import { DOCS } from './paths';
import type { DocsPage, MetaEntry } from './site';

export interface NavigationModule {
  pageKinds: readonly string[];
  teachingKinds: readonly string[];
  floorPages: Record<string, string>;
  conceptPages: readonly string[];
  toolRoutes: readonly string[];
}

/** `apps/docs/app/navigation.ts`, imported by path so no project depends on the app. */
export async function loadNavigation(): Promise<NavigationModule> {
  return (await import(
    pathToFileURL(join(DOCS, 'app', 'navigation.ts')).href
  )) as NavigationModule;
}

/** A page's `_meta.ts` key: a folder's index answers to the folder. */
function keyOf(slug: string): string {
  return slug.endsWith('/index') ? slug.slice(0, -'/index'.length) : slug;
}

/** The page keys of one `_meta.ts` file, in order. */
function siblingsOf(key: string, meta: readonly MetaEntry[]): string[] {
  const parent = key.includes('/')
    ? key.slice(0, key.lastIndexOf('/') + 1)
    : '';
  return meta
    .filter((entry) => entry.page)
    .map((entry) => entry.key)
    .filter(
      (each) =>
        each.startsWith(parent) && !each.slice(parent.length).includes('/'),
    );
}

/**
 * G1: the sidebar and the content tree name the same pages, each page has one
 * title and a known kind, and `requires` names the pages right before it.
 */
export function checkNavigation(input: {
  pages: DocsPage[];
  meta: MetaEntry[];
  contentDir: string;
  kinds: readonly string[];
  teaching: readonly string[];
}): string[] {
  const { pages, meta, contentDir, kinds, teaching } = input;
  const findings: string[] = [];
  const keys = new Set(
    meta.filter((entry) => entry.page).map((entry) => entry.key),
  );
  const bySlug = new Map(pages.map((page) => [keyOf(page.slug), page]));

  for (const key of keys) {
    const present = ['.mdx', '.md', ''].some((extension) =>
      existsSync(join(contentDir, `${key}${extension}`)),
    );
    if (!present) {
      findings.push(
        `_meta.ts: the key '${key}' names no page. Write ${key}.mdx or remove the key.`,
      );
    }
  }

  for (const page of pages) {
    const key = keyOf(page.slug);
    const titles = page.headings.filter(
      (heading) => heading.depth === 1,
    ).length;

    if (!keys.has(key) && !keys.has(page.slug)) {
      findings.push(
        `${page.file}: the page is not a key in _meta.ts. Add '${key}' in its teaching position.`,
      );
    }
    if (titles !== 1) {
      findings.push(
        `${page.file}: has ${titles} "# " headings. A page has exactly one.`,
      );
    }
    if (page.kind === undefined || !kinds.includes(page.kind)) {
      findings.push(
        `${page.file}: kind '${String(page.kind)}' is not one of ${kinds.join(', ')}. Set a kind from spec section 4.2.`,
      );
    }

    const order = siblingsOf(key, meta);
    const at = order.indexOf(key);
    const before = order.slice(Math.max(0, at - 2), Math.max(0, at));
    const requires = Array.isArray(page.frontmatter.requires)
      ? (page.frontmatter.requires as unknown[]).map(String)
      : [];

    if (
      page.kind !== undefined &&
      teaching.includes(page.kind) &&
      requires.length === 0
    ) {
      const previous = bySlug.get(order[at - 1] ?? '');
      if (previous?.kind !== undefined && teaching.includes(previous.kind)) {
        findings.push(
          `${page.file}: follows the teaching page ${keyOf(previous.slug)} and carries no requires. Name it in requires.`,
        );
      }
    }

    if (requires.length > 2) {
      findings.push(
        `${page.file}: requires names ${requires.length} pages. Name one or two.`,
      );
    }

    for (const required of requires) {
      if (!before.includes(required)) {
        findings.push(
          `${page.file}: requires '${required}', which is not one of the two pages before it in _meta.ts (${before.join(', ') || 'none'}).`,
        );
        continue;
      }
      const target = bySlug.get(required);
      if (target?.kind === undefined || !teaching.includes(target.kind)) {
        findings.push(
          `${page.file}: requires '${required}', whose kind '${String(target?.kind)}' is not a teaching kind. A prerequisite is a tutorial or a concept.`,
        );
      }
    }
  }

  return findings.sort();
}
```

- [ ] Step 5: Write `docs/doc-floor.ts`

```ts
import { relative } from 'node:path';

import { workspaceRoot } from '@nx/devkit';

import { waits } from './allowance';
import { CONTENT } from './paths';
import type { DocsPage } from './site';

/**
 * G2: the floor pages and the named concept pages exist with the right kind.
 *
 * A page Phase 2 has not written sits in `doc-floor-allowance.json` with the
 * reason it waits, and the entry fails once the page exists.
 */
export function checkFloor(input: {
  pages: DocsPage[];
  floor: Record<string, string>;
  concepts: readonly string[];
  allowance: Record<string, string>;
}): string[] {
  const { pages, floor, concepts, allowance } = input;
  const bySlug = new Map(pages.map((page) => [page.slug, page]));
  const required: [string, string, string][] = [
    ...Object.entries(floor).map(
      ([slug, kind]) => [slug, kind, 'floor'] as [string, string, string],
    ),
    ...concepts.map(
      (slug) => [slug, 'concept', 'concept'] as [string, string, string],
    ),
  ];
  const findings: string[] = [];
  const file = (slug: string) =>
    relative(workspaceRoot, `${CONTENT}/${slug}.mdx`);

  for (const [slug, kind, role] of required) {
    const page = bySlug.get(slug);

    if (page === undefined) {
      if (slug in allowance) continue;
      findings.push(
        `${file(slug)}: the ${role} page '${slug}' does not exist. Write it with kind: ${kind}, or record the wait in doc-floor-allowance.json.`,
      );
      continue;
    }

    if (page.kind !== kind) {
      findings.push(
        `${file(slug)}: the ${role} page '${slug}' has kind '${String(page.kind)}'. Set kind: ${kind}.`,
      );
    }
  }

  const { stale, unexplained } = waits(new Set(bySlug.keys()), allowance);
  for (const slug of unexplained) {
    findings.push(
      `doc-floor-allowance.json: '${slug}' records no reason. Say what the page waits for.`,
    );
  }
  for (const slug of stale) {
    findings.push(
      `doc-floor-allowance.json: '${slug}' exists now. Remove the entry.`,
    );
  }

  return findings.sort();
}
```

The finding path names `apps/docs/content`, so the fixture test above expects that prefix for every tree.

- [ ] Step 4: Write `docs/doc-fence.ts`

```ts
import { ratchet } from './allowance';
import {
  EXEMPTION_TAGS,
  SHELL_LANGS,
  type DocsFence,
  type DocsPage,
} from './site';

/** The two tags a writer reaches for when wiring a doctest is the other option. */
const ABUSABLE = ['anti-example', 'no-run'];

/** What the documentation standard section 5 says a fence is. */
export function fenceClass(
  fence: DocsFence,
): 'region' | 'twoslash' | 'shell' | 'diagram' | 'tagged' | 'unexplained' {
  const words = fence.meta.split(/\s+/);
  if (
    /(?:^|\s)file=\S+/.test(fence.meta) &&
    /(?:^|\s)region=[\w-]+/.test(fence.meta)
  ) {
    return 'region';
  }
  if (words.includes('twoslash')) return 'twoslash';
  if ((SHELL_LANGS as readonly string[]).includes(fence.lang)) return 'shell';
  if (fence.lang === 'mermaid') return 'diagram';
  if (
    words.some((word) => (EXEMPTION_TAGS as readonly string[]).includes(word))
  )
    return 'tagged';
  return 'unexplained';
}

/** Per page: fences nothing ran, executed regions, and the two abusable tags. */
export function tallyFences(
  pages: DocsPage[],
): Map<string, { unexplained: number; regions: number; abusable: number }> {
  const tally = new Map<
    string,
    { unexplained: number; regions: number; abusable: number }
  >();

  for (const page of pages) {
    if (page.kind === 'post') continue;
    const held = { unexplained: 0, regions: 0, abusable: 0 };

    for (const fence of page.fences) {
      const kind = fenceClass(fence);
      if (kind === 'region') held.regions += 1;
      if (kind === 'unexplained') held.unexplained += 1;
      if (fence.tags.some((tag) => ABUSABLE.includes(tag))) held.abusable += 1;
    }

    tally.set(page.slug, held);
  }

  return tally;
}

/**
 * G3: every fence is executed, compiled, a shell block, a diagram, or tagged,
 * and no page explains itself mostly by exemption. `post` pages are skipped,
 * because amendment A2 tags a dated post's code `elided`.
 */
export function checkFence(
  pages: DocsPage[],
  allowance: Record<string, number>,
): string[] {
  const tally = tallyFences(pages);
  const counts = Object.fromEntries(
    [...tally].map(([slug, held]) => [slug, held.unexplained]),
  );
  const { over, slack, stale } = ratchet(counts, allowance);
  const findings: string[] = [];

  for (const line of over) {
    const [slug, rest] = line.split(': ');
    const count = Number(rest?.split(',')[0]);
    findings.push(
      `${slug}: ${count} unexplained fence${count === 1 ? '' : 's'}, ${rest?.split(', ')[1]}. Cite a doctested region with file= region=, use a twoslash fence, or tag the block with signature, no-run, anti-example, fails-type-check or elided. The allowance in doc-fence-allowance.json only goes down.`,
    );
  }

  for (const [slug, held] of tally) {
    if (held.abusable > held.regions) {
      findings.push(
        `${slug}: ${held.abusable} fences tagged anti-example or no-run against ${held.regions} executed region${held.regions === 1 ? '' : 's'}. Documentation standard section 5 caps the two tags at the executed count. Cite a region.`,
      );
    }
  }

  for (const line of slack) {
    findings.push(
      `doc-fence-allowance.json: ${line}. Lower the entry to the count, and remove it at zero.`,
    );
  }
  for (const slug of stale) {
    findings.push(
      `doc-fence-allowance.json: ${slug} has no page. Remove the entry.`,
    );
  }

  return findings.sort();
}
```

```ts
import { waits } from './allowance';
import { stripFences, type DocsPage } from './site';

const VIEW = /<ConsoleView\b([\s\S]*?)\/>/g;
const EXEMPT = /<ConsoleExempt\b([\s\S]*?)\/>/g;

function attribute(attributes: string, name: string): string | undefined {
  return new RegExp(`\\b${name}="([^"]*)"`).exec(attributes)?.[1];
}

function controlsIn(text: string): number {
  const body = stripFences(text);
  return (
    (body.match(/<ConsoleView\b/g)?.length ?? 0) +
    (body.match(/<ConsoleExempt\b/g)?.length ?? 0)
  );
}

/** Findings for one page, the allowance ignored. */
function pageFindings(page: DocsPage): string[] {
  const findings: string[] = [];
  const body = stripFences(page.body);

  for (const [, attributes = ''] of body.matchAll(VIEW)) {
    if ((attribute(attributes, 'caption') ?? '').trim() === '') {
      findings.push(
        `${page.file}: a ConsoleView has no caption. Write caption="…" stating in words what the view shows, so a reader without JavaScript loses nothing.`,
      );
    }
  }

  for (const [, attributes = ''] of body.matchAll(EXEMPT)) {
    if ((attribute(attributes, 'reason') ?? '').trim() === '') {
      findings.push(
        `${page.file}: a ConsoleExempt has no reason. Write reason="…" saying why the section has nothing for the console to show.`,
      );
    }
  }

  if (page.slug === 'getting-started' && !/<ConsoleView\b/.test(body)) {
    findings.push(
      `${page.file}: Getting started mounts no ConsoleView. Mount one whose seed is the finished path.`,
    );
  }

  if (page.kind === 'concept') {
    for (const section of page.sections) {
      const count = controlsIn(section.body);
      if (count !== 1) {
        findings.push(
          `${page.file}:${section.heading.line}: the section "${section.heading.text}" mounts ${count} console controls. Mount one ConsoleView, or one ConsoleExempt with a reason.`,
        );
      }
    }
  }

  return findings;
}

/**
 * G4: Getting started mounts a console, every H2 section of a concept page
 * mounts one console control, and every control says in words what it shows or
 * why it shows nothing (amendment A1, spec section 10.1).
 */
export function checkControl(input: {
  pages: DocsPage[];
  allowance: Record<string, string>;
}): string[] {
  const { pages, allowance } = input;
  const findings: string[] = [];
  const passing = new Set<string>();

  for (const page of pages) {
    const found = pageFindings(page);
    if (found.length === 0) passing.add(page.slug);
    if (!(page.slug in allowance)) findings.push(...found);
  }

  const slugs = new Set(pages.map((page) => page.slug));
  const { stale, unexplained } = waits(passing, allowance);

  for (const slug of unexplained) {
    findings.push(
      `doc-control-allowance.json: '${slug}' records no reason. Say what the controls wait for.`,
    );
  }
  for (const slug of Object.keys(allowance)) {
    if (!slugs.has(slug))
      findings.push(
        `doc-control-allowance.json: '${slug}' has no page. Remove the entry.`,
      );
  }
  for (const slug of stale) {
    findings.push(
      `doc-control-allowance.json: '${slug}' mounts its controls now. Remove the entry.`,
    );
  }

  return findings.sort();
}
```

- [ ] Step 5: Write `docs/doc-specimen.ts`

```ts
import { existsSync, readdirSync } from 'node:fs';

import { stripFences, type DocsPage } from './site';

/**
 * G6: every operable specimen is on the MDX map and is mounted in a section.
 *
 * The names come from the folder, so no component name is written here.
 * Standard decision 20 puts a specimen both on the overview and on the page of
 * the section it demonstrates, so a mount on `index` alone does not count.
 */
export function checkSpecimens(input: {
  specimenDir: string;
  mdxComponents: string;
  pages: DocsPage[];
}): string[] {
  const { specimenDir, mdxComponents, pages } = input;
  if (!existsSync(specimenDir)) return [];

  const names = readdirSync(specimenDir)
    .filter((file) => /\.tsx$/.test(file) && !/\.test\.tsx$/.test(file))
    .map((file) => file.replace(/\.tsx$/, ''))
    .sort();
  const map = mdxComponents.slice(mdxComponents.indexOf('return {'));
  const findings: string[] = [];

  for (const name of names) {
    const file = `components/specimens/${name}.tsx`;
    const imported = new RegExp(
      `^import\\s+${name}\\s+from\\s+['"]\\./components/specimens/${name}['"]`,
      'm',
    ).test(mdxComponents);
    const listed = new RegExp(`\\b${name}\\b`).test(map);

    if (!imported || !listed) {
      findings.push(
        `${file}: ${name} is not registered in mdx-components.js. Import it there and add it to the returned map.`,
      );
    }

    const mounted = pages.some(
      (page) =>
        page.slug !== 'index' &&
        new RegExp(`<${name}[\\s/>]`).test(stripFences(page.body)),
    );
    if (!mounted) {
      findings.push(
        `${file}: ${name} is mounted on no content page besides index. Mount it in the section it demonstrates (standard decision 20).`,
      );
    }
  }

  return findings.sort();
}
```
