- Modify: `.prettierignore` (`apps/docs/snapshot/docs` and `apps/docs/snapshot/src`)

Interfaces:

- Consumes: nothing.
- Produces: the overlay directory `apps/docs/snapshot/`, copied verbatim into `snapshot-src/docs/` by Task 39; `newestPublishedPost(dir)` and `announcementBar(post)`; `overlayFiles(snapshotDir: string, sub: string): string[]`, `sourcePages(ref: string, cwd: string): string[]` and `strayPages(overlay: readonly string[], source: readonly string[]): string[]` from `apps/docs/tools/snapshot-overlay.mjs`.

Spec §15.2 step 3, as this plan reads it: the snapshot workflow copies `apps/docs/snapshot/` into the 0.3 site directory with `cp -R apps/docs/snapshot/. snapshot-src/docs/`. The copy replaces whole files and adds new ones, so the overlay can carry four kinds of file:

- the two Docusaurus configs, `docusaurus.overlay.root.ts` and `docusaurus.overlay.archive.ts`, each importing the original `docusaurus.config.ts`;
- `src/pages/index.tsx`, the 0.3 landing page with its logo path fixed;
- `blog/`, the posts the 0.3 blog gains: RC posts (tagged `release-candidate`, which drive the announcement bar) and any other post, such as a 0.3.x release note;
- `docs/`, corrected copies of 0.3 documentation pages. `apps/docs/snapshot/docs/faq.md` is copied to `snapshot-src/docs/docs/faq.md` and replaces the page `docs/docs/faq.md` at `6d5e4f3`.

A file under `snapshot/docs/` whose path matches no page at `6d5e4f3` would add a stray page to the 0.3 site, so a test holds every such path to the page list at that commit. The page copies and the landing page copy are 0.3 files that differ from their originals only by their corrections, so `.prettierignore` keeps prettier off `apps/docs/snapshot/docs` and `apps/docs/snapshot/src`; a format pass would rewrite every other line.

The overlay imports `./docusaurus.config`, which exists only inside the 0.3 site, so `apps/docs/tsconfig.json` and the app's lint config exclude `snapshot/`. The tests read the overlay as text and drive `announcement.mjs` against fixture blog directories.

RC posts carry the `release-candidate` tag. A Docusaurus post named `YYYY-MM-DD-<name>.md` with no `slug` is served at `/blog/YYYY/MM/DD/<name>`, which is the `legacyUrl` shape spec §6.2 records.

- [ ] Step 4: Implement `announcement.mjs`

```js
// apps/docs/snapshot/announcement.mjs
import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';

/**
 * The newest RC post the 0.3 site should announce, read from the blog
 * directory the snapshot build uses. Plain ESM so the Docusaurus overlay
 * config imports it in the 0.3 site and the docs app's tests import it here.
 */
const DATED = /^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})-(.+)\.mdx?$/;

function frontmatter(source) {
  const block = /^---\n([\s\S]*?)\n---/.exec(source);
  const fields = {};
  if (!block) return fields;
  for (const line of block[1].split('\n')) {
    const match = /^(\w+):\s*(.*)$/.exec(line);
    if (match) fields[match[1]] = match[2].trim();
  }
  return fields;
}

function tagsOf(value = '') {
  return value
    .replace(/^\[|\]$/g, '')
    .split(',')
    .map((tag) => tag.trim())
    .filter(Boolean);
}

export function newestPublishedPost(dir) {
  const posts = readdirSync(dir)
    .map((file) => ({ file, match: DATED.exec(file) }))
    .filter(({ match }) => match !== null)
    .filter(({ file }) => {
      const fields = frontmatter(readFileSync(join(dir, file), 'utf8'));
      return (
        fields.draft !== 'true' &&
        tagsOf(fields.tags).includes('release-candidate')
      );
    })
    .sort((a, b) => b.file.localeCompare(a.file));

  const newest = posts[0];
  if (!newest) return null;
  const [, year, month, day, name] = newest.match;
  return {
    file: newest.file,
    permalink: `/blog/${year}/${month}/${day}/${name}`,
  };
}

export function announcementBar(post) {
  if (!post) return undefined;
  return {
    id: `rc-${post.file.replace(/\.mdx?$/, '')}`,
    isCloseable: true,
    content:
      `NexusDI 0.4 is in release candidate. Read the <a href="${post.permalink}">announcement</a>, ` +
      'or the <a href="/next/upgrade/">upgrade guide</a>.',
  };
}
```

```ts
// apps/docs/snapshot/announcement.d.mts
export interface PublishedPost {
  file: string;
  permalink: string;
}
export function newestPublishedPost(dir: string): PublishedPost | null;
export function announcementBar(
  post: PublishedPost | null,
): { id: string; content: string; isCloseable: boolean } | undefined;
```

Then the overlay file reader:

```js
// apps/docs/tools/snapshot-overlay.mjs
import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { existsSync, readdirSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join, relative, sep } from 'node:path';

/**
 * The files under one folder of the snapshot overlay, as sorted paths
 * relative to that folder with forward slashes. A missing folder holds none.
 */
export function overlayFiles(snapshotDir, sub) {
  const dir = join(snapshotDir, sub);
  if (!existsSync(dir)) return [];
  return readdirSync(dir, { recursive: true, withFileTypes: true })
    .filter((entry) => entry.isFile())
    .map((entry) =>
      relative(dir, join(entry.parentPath, entry.name)).split(sep).join('/'),
    )
    .sort();
}

/**
 * The 0.3 documentation pages at `ref`, relative to `docs/docs/`, which is
 * where `cp -R apps/docs/snapshot/. snapshot-src/docs/` puts a file from the
 * overlay's own `docs/` folder.
 */
export function sourcePages(ref, cwd) {
  return execFileSync(
    'git',
    ['ls-tree', '-r', '--name-only', ref, 'docs/docs/'],
    {
      cwd,
      encoding: 'utf8',
    },
  )
    .split('\n')
    .filter(Boolean)
    .map((path) => path.slice('docs/docs/'.length));
}

/** Overlay pages that replace nothing, and so would add a page to the 0.3 site. */
export function strayPages(overlay, source) {
  const pages = new Set(source);
  return overlay.filter((path) => !pages.has(path));
}
```

```ts
// apps/docs/snapshot/docusaurus.overlay.root.ts
import { join } from 'node:path';

import base from './docusaurus.config';
import { announcementBar, newestPublishedPost } from './announcement.mjs';

/**
 * The 0.3 site at the root during the RC (spec §15.2 step 4). It keeps the
 * original config and adds the announcement bar once a published RC post
 * sits in blog/. `docusaurus build` runs from the site directory, so
 * process.cwd() is snapshot-src/docs.
 */
const bar = announcementBar(newestPublishedPost(join(process.cwd(), 'blog')));

export default {
  ...base,
  baseUrl: '/',
  themeConfig: {
    ...base.themeConfig,
    ...(bar ? { announcementBar: bar } : {}),
  },
};
```

```ts
// apps/docs/snapshot/docusaurus.overlay.archive.ts
import base from './docusaurus.config';

/**
 * The 0.3 site under /v0.3/ after 0.4.0 final (spec §15.2 step 4). No blog:
 * the posts move to the new site, and the navbar sends a reader there.
 */
const [[preset, options]] = base.presets as [[string, Record<string, unknown>]];

const items = (base.themeConfig.navbar?.items ?? []).filter(
  (item) => !('to' in item && item.to === '/blog'),
);

export default {
  ...base,
  baseUrl: '/v0.3/',
  noIndex: true,
  presets: [[preset, { ...options, blog: false }]],
  themeConfig: {
    ...base.themeConfig,
    navbar: {
      ...base.themeConfig.navbar,
      items: [
        ...items,
        {
          href: 'https://nexus.js.org/blog/',
          label: 'Blog',
          position: 'right',
        },
      ],
    },
    announcementBar: {
      id: 'v0-3-deprecated',
      isCloseable: false,
      content:
        'This is the documentation for NexusDI 0.3, which is deprecated. The current documentation is at <a href="https://nexus.js.org/">nexus.js.org</a>, and the upgrade guide is at <a href="https://nexus.js.org/upgrade/">nexus.js.org/upgrade/</a>.',
    },
  },
};
```

- [ ] Step 7: Write the draft RC post

A heredoc writes the post, so prettier never reads its frontmatter as Markdown.

````bash
cat > apps/docs/snapshot/blog/2026-10-01-0-4-release-candidate.md <<'EOF'
---
title: NexusDI 0.4 release candidate
authors: [evanion]
tags: [release, release-candidate, migration]
description: NexusDI 0.4 is in release candidate on the next dist-tag, with a codemod and an upgrade guide.
draft: true
---

NexusDI 0.4.0-rc.0 is on npm under the `next` dist-tag. The documentation for 0.4 is at [nexus.js.org/next/](https://nexus.js.org/next/).

<!--truncate-->

## What changed and why

NexusDI 0.4 compiles the whole module graph when the container starts. `Nexus.create` reports every wiring mistake at once, with the fix, before any constructor runs. After startup every `get()` is synchronous.

The 0.3 API is gone. `set()`, `DynamicModule`, symbol tokens and parameter decorators have no 0.4 form. The [upgrade guide](https://nexus.js.org/next/upgrade/) maps each 0.3 API to its replacement.

## The codemod

`npx @nexusdi/codemod@next 0.4` rewrites a 0.3 project. It prints a report of every change it could not make, with a code for each.

## Install the release candidate

```sh
npm install @nexusdi/core@next
````

`npm install @nexusdi/core` keeps installing 0.3.x until 0.4.0 final.

## Feedback

Post feedback in the "0.4 RC feedback" discussion on GitHub, or open an issue with the RC feedback template. A maintainer labels each issue that must be fixed before final.

## The road to 0.4.0 final

0.4.0 final is released once four weeks pass after the last RC with a breaking change, no blocking issue is open, and the codemod has run against at least one external codebase.

## Support for 0.3

`latest` stays on 0.3.x until 0.4.0 final. The 0.3.x line then receives security, crash and data-loss fixes until six months after 0.4.0 final or the release of 0.5.0, whichever is later.
EOF

```js
    expect(next.snapshot).toEqual({
      release: 'docs-snapshot-0.3',
      source: '6d5e4f3',
      revision: 1,
      assets: {
        root: {
          name: 'nexusdi-docs-0.3-root-r1.tar.gz',
          sha256: 'a'.repeat(64),
        },
        archive: {
          name: 'nexusdi-docs-0.3-archive-r1.tar.gz',
          sha256: 'b'.repeat(64),
        },
      },
    });
    expect(validateDeployConfig(next)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('refuses a revision that does not move forward', () => {
    const current = recordSnapshot(config(), {
      revision: 2,
      rootSha256: 'a'.repeat(64),
      archiveSha256: 'b'.repeat(64),
    });
    expect(() =>
      recordSnapshot(current, {
        revision: 2,
        rootSha256: 'c'.repeat(64),
        archiveSha256: 'd'.repeat(64),
      }),
    ).toThrow('revision 2 is not after the recorded revision 2');
  });
});
```

```js
// apps/docs/tools/deploy/record-snapshot.mjs
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';

import { validateDeployConfig } from './deploy-config.mjs';

/** deploy.json after a docs-snapshot.yml run uploaded revision N. */
export function recordSnapshot(
  config,
  { revision, rootSha256, archiveSha256 },
) {
  if (revision <= config.snapshot.revision) {
    throw new Error(
      `revision ${revision} is not after the recorded revision ${config.snapshot.revision}`,
    );
  }
  const next = {
    ...config,
    snapshot: {
      ...config.snapshot,
      revision,
      assets: {
        root: {
          name: `nexusdi-docs-0.3-root-r${revision}.tar.gz`,
          sha256: rootSha256,
        },
        archive: {
          name: `nexusdi-docs-0.3-archive-r${revision}.tar.gz`,
          sha256: archiveSha256,
        },
      },
    },
  };
  const findings = validateDeployConfig(next);
  if (findings.length > 0) throw new Error(findings.join('\n'));
  return next;
}

if (import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1] ?? '').href) {
  const [path, revision, rootSha256, archiveSha256] = process.argv.slice(2);
  const config = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, 'utf8'));
  const next = recordSnapshot(config, {
    revision: Number(revision),
    rootSha256,
    archiveSha256,
  });
  writeFileSync(path, `${JSON.stringify(next, null, 2)}\n`);
}
```

```js
// apps/docs/tools/deploy/snapshot-assets.mjs
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { basename } from 'node:path';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';

export function sha256File(path) {
  return createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(path)).digest('hex');
}

/**
 * Stops the deploy before an archive is unpacked when its bytes differ from
 * what deploy.json records (spec §15.2).
 */
export function verifyChecksum(file, expected) {
  const name = basename(file);
  if (!existsSync(file))
    throw new Error(`${name}: the release asset was not downloaded.`);
  const actual = sha256File(file);
  if (actual !== expected) {
    throw new Error(
      `${name}: sha256 is ${actual}, and deploy.json records ${expected}. The deploy stops before unpacking it.`,
    );
  }
}

if (import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1] ?? '').href) {
  const [command, file, expected] = process.argv.slice(2);
  if (command !== 'verify')
    throw new Error('usage: snapshot-assets.mjs verify <file> <sha256>');
  verifyChecksum(file, expected);
  console.log(`${basename(file)}: checksum matches`);
}
```

- [ ] Step 7: Write the workflow

```yaml
# .github/workflows/docs-snapshot.yml
name: Docs snapshot

# Builds the 0.3 Docusaurus site from `source` plus the overlay in
# apps/docs/snapshot/, stores both variants as assets of the GitHub Release
# `docs-snapshot-0.3`, and opens a pull request recording them in
# apps/docs/deploy.json (docs spec §15.2). A release asset is permanent; a
# workflow artifact expires after at most 90 days, and the snapshot has to
# last until the /v0.3/ retention ends.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      source:
        description: Commit of the 0.3 Docusaurus site
        required: true
        default: 6d5e4f3

permissions:
  contents: write # create the release and upload its assets
  pull-requests: write # open the deploy.json pull request

concurrency:
  group: docs-snapshot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  snapshot:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      SOURCE: ${{ inputs.source }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.source }}
          path: snapshot-src

      # Docusaurus 3.8.1 exists only at the source commit. The docs spec's
      # review built it on Node 22.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: snapshot-src/docs/package-lock.json

      # Inside the site directory: Docusaurus does not resolve its preset
      # from a config file outside it. The copy replaces whole files: the
      # configs and the landing page, the posts in blog/, and each corrected
      # 0.3 page in docs/ over the page at the same path.
      - name: Copy the overlay
        run: cp -R apps/docs/snapshot/. snapshot-src/docs/

      - name: Build the root and archive variants
        working-directory: snapshot-src/docs
        run: |
          npm ci
          npx docusaurus build --config docusaurus.overlay.root.ts --out-dir build-root
          npx docusaurus build --config docusaurus.overlay.archive.ts --out-dir build-archive

      - name: Pack the next revision
        id: pack
        working-directory: snapshot-src/docs
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          current="$(node -p "require('${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/apps/docs/deploy.json').snapshot.revision")"
          revision=$((current + 1))
          rm -f build-root/CNAME build-archive/CNAME
          tar -czf "nexusdi-docs-0.3-root-r${revision}.tar.gz" -C build-root .
          tar -czf "nexusdi-docs-0.3-archive-r${revision}.tar.gz" -C build-archive .
          sha256sum "nexusdi-docs-0.3-root-r${revision}.tar.gz" "nexusdi-docs-0.3-archive-r${revision}.tar.gz" > SHA256SUMS
          {
            echo "revision=${revision}"
            echo "root_sha256=$(sha256sum "nexusdi-docs-0.3-root-r${revision}.tar.gz" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
            echo "archive_sha256=$(sha256sum "nexusdi-docs-0.3-archive-r${revision}.tar.gz" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Upload to the docs-snapshot-0.3 release
        working-directory: snapshot-src/docs
        env:
          REVISION: ${{ steps.pack.outputs.revision }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if ! gh release view docs-snapshot-0.3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release create docs-snapshot-0.3 --target "$(git -C "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/snapshot-src" rev-parse HEAD)" \
              --title "Docs snapshot 0.3" --notes "The 0.3 documentation site, built from ${SOURCE}." --latest=false
          fi
          gh release upload docs-snapshot-0.3 --clobber \
            "nexusdi-docs-0.3-root-r${REVISION}.tar.gz" \
            "nexusdi-docs-0.3-archive-r${REVISION}.tar.gz" \
            SHA256SUMS

      - name: Open the deploy.json pull request
        env:
          REVISION: ${{ steps.pack.outputs.revision }}
          ROOT_SHA256: ${{ steps.pack.outputs.root_sha256 }}
          ARCHIVE_SHA256: ${{ steps.pack.outputs.archive_sha256 }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          branch="docs/snapshot-r${REVISION}"
          node apps/docs/tools/deploy/record-snapshot.mjs apps/docs/deploy.json "$REVISION" "$ROOT_SHA256" "$ARCHIVE_SHA256"
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git switch -c "$branch"
          git add apps/docs/deploy.json
          git commit -m "chore(docs): record docs snapshot revision ${REVISION}"
          git push origin "$branch"
          gh pr create --base main --head "$branch" \
            --title "chore(docs): record docs snapshot revision ${REVISION}" \
            --body "docs-snapshot.yml built ${SOURCE} with the overlay and uploaded revision ${REVISION} to the docs-snapshot-0.3 release. This records the asset names and checksums in apps/docs/deploy.json."
```

### Task 40: Artifact assembly per mode

Files:

- Create: `apps/docs/tools/deploy/assemble.mjs`
- Create: `apps/docs/tools/deploy/assemble.d.mts`
- Test: `apps/docs/tools/deploy/assemble.test.mjs`

Interfaces:

- Consumes: `apps/docs/out` from `npx nx build @nexusdi/docs` plus `npm run postbuild` (Tasks 2, 13, 24).
- Produces:
  - `assemble({ mode, site, nextOut, rootOut, snapshotRoot, snapshotArchive, legacyPosts, probe }): { files: number }` where `legacyPosts: { legacyUrl: string; slug: string }[]` (Phase 2 fills it from `content/blog/`) and `probe?: string` (Task 43).
  - `rootNotFoundScript(): string` and `stubHtml(target: string): string`.
  - A CLI `node apps/docs/tools/deploy/assemble.mjs` reading `DEPLOY_MODE`, `SITE_DIR`, `NEXT_OUT`, `ROOT_OUT`, `SNAPSHOT_ROOT`, `SNAPSHOT_ARCHIVE`, `SANDBOX_PROBE_DIR`.

The layout per mode is spec §15.1's table: `snapshot-only` puts the snapshot's root variant at the root and nothing else; `rc` adds the new site under `next/` and the root 404 script; `final` puts the new site's release build at the root, the new site from `main` under `next/`, the archive variant under `v0.3/`, and writes the redirect stubs of §15.6; `retired` replaces every `v0.3/` page with a stub to `/upgrade/`.

```js
// apps/docs/tools/deploy/assemble.mjs
import {
  cpSync,
  existsSync,
  mkdirSync,
  readdirSync,
  readFileSync,
  rmSync,
  statSync,
  writeFileSync,
} from 'node:fs';
import { dirname, join, relative, sep } from 'node:path';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';

/**
 * Lays out the GitHub Pages artifact for one deploy mode (docs spec §15.1,
 * §15.5, §15.6). Every input is a directory already built; this copies and
 * writes, and builds nothing.
 */

const DOMAIN = 'nexus.js.org';

/**
 * The root 404.html of the 0.3 snapshot answers every missing path. During the
 * RC a missing /next/ path would get a 0.3 page, so the first thing the page
 * runs sends it to the new site's own 404 page.
 */
export function rootNotFoundScript() {
  return (
    '<script>(function(){var p=location.pathname;' +
    "if(p.indexOf('/next/')===0&&p!=='/next/404.html'){location.replace('/next/404.html');}" +
    '})();</script>'
  );
}

/** A redirect page: GitHub Pages has no redirect mechanism of its own. */
export function stubHtml(target) {
  return [
    '<!doctype html>',
    '<html lang="en">',
    '<head>',
    '<meta charset="utf-8">',
    '<meta name="robots" content="noindex">',
    `<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0; url=${target}">`,
    `<link rel="canonical" href="https://${DOMAIN}${target}">`,
    '<title>Moved</title>',
    '</head>',
    '<body>',
    `<p>This page moved to <a href="${target}">${target}</a>.</p>`,
    '</body>',
    '</html>',
    '',
  ].join('\n');
}

function files(dir) {
  return readdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })
    .map((entry) => String(entry))
    .filter((entry) => statSync(join(dir, entry)).isFile())
    .map((entry) => entry.split(sep).join('/'));
}

function copyInto(from, to) {
  mkdirSync(to, { recursive: true });
  cpSync(from, to, { recursive: true });
}

function write(site, path, body, { overwrite = true } = {}) {
  const target = join(site, path);
  if (!overwrite && existsSync(target)) return;
  mkdirSync(dirname(target), { recursive: true });
  writeFileSync(target, body);
}

function injectNotFoundScript(site) {
  const path = join(site, '404.html');
  const html = readFileSync(path, 'utf8');
  if (!/<head[^>]*>/i.test(html))
    throw new Error(
      'the root 404.html has no <head> to hold the /next/ script',
    );
  writeFileSync(
    path,
    html.replace(/<head([^>]*)>/i, (tag) => `${tag}${rootNotFoundScript()}`),
  );
}

function removeNestedCname(site) {
  for (const path of files(site)) {
    if (path !== 'CNAME' && path.endsWith('/CNAME')) rmSync(join(site, path));
  }
}

function pathOf(file) {
  return `/${file.replace(/index\.html$/, '')}`;
}

function finalStubs(site, snapshotRoot, legacyPosts) {
  for (const file of files(snapshotRoot)) {
    if (!file.endsWith('.html')) continue;
    if (file.startsWith('docs/')) {
      write(site, file, stubHtml(`/v0.3${pathOf(file)}`), { overwrite: false });
    } else if (/^blog\/(tags|archive|authors)\//.test(file)) {
      write(site, file, stubHtml('/blog/'), { overwrite: false });
    }
  }
  for (const post of legacyPosts) {
    const path = `${post.legacyUrl.replace(/^\//, '').replace(/\/$/, '')}/index.html`;
    write(site, path, stubHtml(`/blog/${post.slug}/`), { overwrite: false });
  }
}

export function assemble({
  mode,
  site,
  nextOut,
  rootOut,
  snapshotRoot,
  snapshotArchive,
  legacyPosts = [],
  probe,
}) {
  rmSync(site, { recursive: true, force: true });

  if (mode === 'snapshot-only' || mode === 'rc') {
    copyInto(snapshotRoot, site);
    if (mode === 'rc') {
      if (existsSync(join(snapshotRoot, 'next'))) {
        throw new Error('the snapshot root already has a next/ directory');
      }
      copyInto(nextOut, join(site, 'next'));
      injectNotFoundScript(site);
    }
  } else if (mode === 'final' || mode === 'retired') {
    copyInto(rootOut, site);
    copyInto(nextOut, join(site, 'next'));
    finalStubs(site, snapshotRoot, legacyPosts);
    if (mode === 'final') {
      copyInto(snapshotArchive, join(site, 'v0.3'));
    } else {
      for (const file of files(snapshotArchive)) {
        if (file.endsWith('.html'))
          write(site, `v0.3/${file}`, stubHtml('/upgrade/'));
      }
    }
  } else {
    throw new Error(`unknown deploy mode "${mode}"`);
  }

  if (probe) copyInto(probe, join(site, '_sandbox-probe'));

  removeNestedCname(site);
  write(site, 'CNAME', `${DOMAIN}\n`);
  write(site, '.nojekyll', '');

  return { files: files(site).length };
}

if (import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1] ?? '').href) {
  const env = process.env;
  const { files: count } = assemble({
    mode: env.DEPLOY_MODE,
    site: env.SITE_DIR ?? 'site',
    nextOut: env.NEXT_OUT,
    rootOut: env.ROOT_OUT,
    snapshotRoot: env.SNAPSHOT_ROOT,
    snapshotArchive: env.SNAPSHOT_ARCHIVE,
    probe: env.SANDBOX_PROBE_DIR || undefined,
  });
  console.log(
    `assembled ${count} files in ${relative(process.cwd(), env.SITE_DIR ?? 'site')} for mode ${env.DEPLOY_MODE}`,
  );
}
```

```ts
  mode: 'snapshot-only' | 'rc' | 'final' | 'retired';
  site: string;
  nextOut?: string;
  rootOut?: string;
  snapshotRoot: string;
  snapshotArchive?: string;
  legacyPosts?: { legacyUrl: string; slug: string }[];
  probe?: string;
}
export function assemble(input: AssembleInput): { files: number };
export function rootNotFoundScript(): string;
export function stubHtml(target: string): string;
```

- [ ] Step 3: Implement the checks

```js
// apps/docs/tools/deploy/check-artifact.mjs
import { existsSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join, sep } from 'node:path';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';

import { rootNotFoundScript } from './assemble.mjs';

/**
 * The "Check deploy artefacts" step of docs spec §15.5. Each finding names
 * the file and what is wrong with it; the CLI fails the deploy on any.
 */

function files(site) {
  return readdirSync(site, { recursive: true })
    .map((entry) => String(entry))
    .filter((entry) => statSync(join(site, entry)).isFile())
    .map((entry) => entry.split(sep).join('/'));
}

export function siteCounts(site) {
  const counts = { root: 0, next: 0, 'v0.3': 0 };
  for (const file of files(site)) {
    if (file.startsWith('next/')) counts.next += 1;
    else if (file.startsWith('v0.3/')) counts['v0.3'] += 1;
    else counts.root += 1;
  }
  return counts;
}

const NEXT_REQUIRED = [
  'next/index.html',
  'next/404.html',
  'next/_pagefind/pagefind.js',
  'next/getting-started.md',
];

function requireFiles(findings, site, mode, paths) {
  for (const path of paths) {
    if (!existsSync(join(site, path)))
      findings.push(`missing from the ${mode} artifact: ${path}`);
  }
}

function requireMatch(findings, all, mode, label, pattern) {
  if (!all.some((file) => pattern.test(file))) {
    findings.push(`missing from the ${mode} artifact: ${label}`);
  }
}

const EXTERNAL = /^(?:[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:|\/\/|#)/i;

function checkArchive(findings, site, all) {
  for (const file of all.filter(
    (f) => f.startsWith('v0.3/') && f.endsWith('.html'),
  )) {
    const html = readFileSync(join(site, file), 'utf8');
    if (!/<meta\s+name="robots"\s+content="[^"]*noindex/i.test(html)) {
      findings.push(`${file}: carries no noindex robots meta.`);
    }
    for (const [, attribute, value] of html.matchAll(
      /\s(href|src)="([^"]*)"/g,
    )) {
      if (EXTERNAL.test(value) || value.startsWith('/v0.3/') || value === '')
        continue;
      if (value.startsWith('/')) {
        findings.push(
          `${file}: ${attribute} "${value}" is root-relative outside /v0.3/.`,
        );
      }
    }
  }
}

export function checkArtifact(site, mode, options = {}) {
  const findings = [];
  const all = files(site);

  if (all.length === 0) return [`the ${mode} artifact is empty.`];

  if (!existsSync(join(site, 'CNAME'))) {
    findings.push(`missing from the ${mode} artifact: CNAME`);
  } else {
    const domain = readFileSync(join(site, 'CNAME'), 'utf8').trim();
    if (domain !== 'nexus.js.org') {
      findings.push(`CNAME reads "${domain}", and the site is nexus.js.org.`);
    }
  }
  for (const file of all) {
    if (file !== 'CNAME' && file.endsWith('/CNAME')) {
      findings.push(`${file}: only the root carries a CNAME.`);
    }
  }
  requireFiles(findings, site, mode, ['.nojekyll', 'index.html', '404.html']);

  const hasNext = all.some((file) => file.startsWith('next/'));

  if (mode === 'snapshot-only') {
    requireFiles(findings, site, mode, ['blog/rss.xml', 'blog/atom.xml']);
    if (hasNext)
      findings.push(
        'next/ exists in snapshot-only mode, which deploys the snapshot alone.',
      );
  }

  if (mode === 'rc' || mode === 'final' || mode === 'retired') {
    requireFiles(findings, site, mode, NEXT_REQUIRED);
    requireMatch(
      findings,
      all,
      mode,
      'next/runtime/types-*.json',
      /^next\/runtime\/types-[^/]+\.json$/,
    );
    requireMatch(
      findings,
      all,
      mode,
      'next/runtime/core-*/index.js',
      /^next\/runtime\/core-[^/]+\/index\.js$/,
    );
    if (all.some((file) => file.startsWith('next/blog/'))) {
      findings.push(
        'next/blog/ exists. The /next/ build leaves content/blog/ out.',
      );
    }
  }

  if (mode === 'rc') {
    requireFiles(findings, site, mode, ['blog/rss.xml', 'blog/atom.xml']);
    const notFound = join(site, '404.html');
    if (
      existsSync(notFound) &&
      !readFileSync(notFound, 'utf8').includes(rootNotFoundScript())
    ) {
      findings.push(
        '404.html does not carry the script that sends a missing /next/ path to /next/404.html.',
      );
    }
  }

  if (mode === 'final' || mode === 'retired') {
    requireFiles(findings, site, mode, [
      'blog/atom.xml',
      'blog/rss.xml',
      'blog/index.html',
      'v0.3/index.html',
      ...(options.posts ?? []).map((slug) => `blog/${slug}/index.html`),
    ]);
  }

  if (mode === 'final') checkArchive(findings, site, all);

  if (mode === 'retired') {
    for (const file of all.filter(
      (f) => f.startsWith('v0.3/') && f.endsWith('.html'),
    )) {
      if (
        !readFileSync(join(site, file), 'utf8').includes('http-equiv="refresh"')
      ) {
        findings.push(
          `${file}: retired mode serves redirect stubs under /v0.3/.`,
        );
      }
    }
  }

  return findings;
}

if (import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1] ?? '').href) {
  const [site = 'site', mode] = process.argv.slice(2);
  const findings = checkArtifact(site, mode, {
    allowProbe: process.env.SANDBOX_PROBE === '1',
  });
  for (const [part, count] of Object.entries(siteCounts(site)))
    console.log(`${part}: ${count} files`);
  if (findings.length > 0) {
    console.error(findings.map((finding) => `- ${finding}`).join('\n'));
    process.exit(1);
  }
  console.log(`the ${mode} artifact looks deployable`);
}
```

```ts
export function checkArtifact(
  site: string,
  mode: string,
  options?: { allowProbe?: boolean; posts?: string[] },
): string[];
export function siteCounts(site: string): Record<string, number>;
```

The `retired` case of the "fails a retired v0.3 page that is not a stub" test uses the clean `final()` tree, whose `v0.3/index.html` is a normal page, so that finding names `v0.3/index.html`.

```js
describe('smokeTargets', () => {
  const origin = 'https://nexus.js.org';

  it('requests the root and the old feed in snapshot-only mode', () => {
    expect(smokeTargets('snapshot-only', origin)).toEqual([
      'https://nexus.js.org/',
      'https://nexus.js.org/blog/rss.xml',
    ]);
  });

  it('adds /next/ and its .md sibling in rc mode', () => {
    expect(smokeTargets('rc', origin)).toEqual([
      'https://nexus.js.org/',
      'https://nexus.js.org/blog/rss.xml',
      'https://nexus.js.org/next/',
      'https://nexus.js.org/next/getting-started.md',
    ]);
  });

  it('adds /v0.3/ and the root sibling in final mode', () => {
    expect(smokeTargets('final', origin)).toEqual([
      'https://nexus.js.org/',
      'https://nexus.js.org/blog/rss.xml',
      'https://nexus.js.org/next/',
      'https://nexus.js.org/next/getting-started.md',
      'https://nexus.js.org/getting-started.md',
      'https://nexus.js.org/v0.3/',
    ]);
  });

  it('drops /v0.3/ in retired mode', () => {
    expect(smokeTargets('retired', origin)).not.toContain(
      'https://nexus.js.org/v0.3/',
    );
  });
});

describe('checkResponse', () => {
  it('passes a 200 without an injected script', () => {
    expect(
      checkResponse('https://nexus.js.org/', 200, '<html></html>'),
    ).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('fails a status other than 200', () => {
    expect(checkResponse('https://nexus.js.org/next/', 404, '')).toEqual([
      'https://nexus.js.org/next/ answered 404.',
    ]);
  });

  it('fails a body that references /cdn-cgi/', () => {
    expect(
      checkResponse(
        'https://nexus.js.org/',
        200,
        '<script src="/cdn-cgi/scripts/rocket-loader.min.js"></script>',
      ),
    ).toEqual([
      'https://nexus.js.org/ carries /cdn-cgi/, so Cloudflare rewrote the HTML. Turn off Rocket Loader and every HTML-rewriting feature for the zone.',
    ]);
  });
});

describe('runSmoke against a local server', () => {
  let server;
  let origin;
  let flaky = 0;

  beforeAll(async () => {
    server = createServer((request, response) => {
      const path = new URL(request.url, 'http://x').pathname;
      if (path === '/') return response.writeHead(200).end('<html>root</html>');
      if (path === '/blog/rss.xml')
        return response.writeHead(200).end('<rss/>');
      if (path === '/injected/')
        return response
          .writeHead(200)
          .end('<script src="/cdn-cgi/x.js"></script>');
      if (path === '/flaky/') {
        flaky += 1;
        return response.writeHead(flaky < 3 ? 502 : 200).end('ok');
      }
      response.writeHead(404).end('missing');
    });
    await new Promise((resolve) => server.listen(0, resolve));
    origin = `http://localhost:${server.address().port}`;
  });

  afterAll(() => server.close());

  it('passes when every target answers 200', async () => {
    expect(
      await runSmoke(smokeTargets('snapshot-only', origin), fetch, {
        attempts: 1,
        delayMs: 0,
      }),
    ).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('retries a target until it answers', async () => {
    expect(
      await runSmoke([`${origin}/flaky/`], fetch, { attempts: 5, delayMs: 0 }),
    ).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('reports a missing page after its last attempt', async () => {
    expect(
      await runSmoke([`${origin}/next/`], fetch, { attempts: 2, delayMs: 0 }),
    ).toEqual([`${origin}/next/ answered 404.`]);
  });

  it('reports an injected script', async () => {
    expect(
      await runSmoke([`${origin}/injected/`], fetch, {
        attempts: 1,
        delayMs: 0,
      }),
    ).toEqual([
      `${origin}/injected/ carries /cdn-cgi/, so Cloudflare rewrote the HTML. Turn off Rocket Loader and every HTML-rewriting feature for the zone.`,
    ]);
  });
});
```

- [ ] Step 3: Implement the smoke check

```js
// apps/docs/tools/deploy/smoke.mjs
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';

/**
 * The post-deploy smoke check of docs spec §17.3, run through the Cloudflare
 * proxy. Any status other than 200 fails, and so does served HTML carrying
 * /cdn-cgi/, which means Cloudflare injected a script into the page.
 */
export function smokeTargets(mode, origin) {
  const targets = ['/', '/blog/rss.xml'];
  if (mode !== 'snapshot-only')
    targets.push('/next/', '/next/getting-started.md');
  if (mode === 'final' || mode === 'retired')
    targets.push('/getting-started.md');
  if (mode === 'final') targets.push('/v0.3/');
  return targets.map((path) => `${origin}${path}`);
}

export function checkResponse(url, status, body) {
  const findings = [];
  if (status !== 200) findings.push(`${url} answered ${status}.`);
  if (body.includes('/cdn-cgi/')) {
    findings.push(
      `${url} carries /cdn-cgi/, so Cloudflare rewrote the HTML. Turn off Rocket Loader and every HTML-rewriting feature for the zone.`,
    );
  }
  return findings;
}

const wait = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));

export async function runSmoke(targets, fetchImpl, { attempts, delayMs }) {
  const findings = [];
  for (const url of targets) {
    let last = [];
    for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= attempts; attempt += 1) {
      const busted = `${url}${url.includes('?') ? '&' : '?'}smoke=${Date.now()}`;
      try {
        const response = await fetchImpl(busted, { redirect: 'manual' });
        last = checkResponse(url, response.status, await response.text());
      } catch (error) {
        last = [`${url} did not answer: ${error.message}.`];
      }
      if (last.length === 0) break;
      if (attempt < attempts) await wait(delayMs);
    }
    findings.push(...last);
  }
  return findings;
}

if (import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1] ?? '').href) {
  const [origin = 'https://nexus.js.org', mode] = process.argv.slice(2);
  const targets = smokeTargets(mode, origin);
  const findings = await runSmoke(targets, fetch, {
    attempts: 5,
    delayMs: 30_000,
  });
  for (const url of targets) console.log(`checked ${url}`);
  if (findings.length > 0) {
    console.error(findings.map((finding) => `- ${finding}`).join('\n'));
    process.exit(1);
  }
}
```

```ts
// apps/docs/tools/deploy/smoke.d.mts
export function smokeTargets(mode: string, origin: string): string[];
export function checkResponse(
  url: string,
  status: number,
  body: string,
): string[];
export function runSmoke(
  targets: string[],
  fetchImpl: typeof fetch,
  options: { attempts: number; delayMs: number },
): Promise<string[]>;
```

```ts
};
```

- [ ] Step 7: Write the workflow

```yaml
# .github/workflows/docs.yml
name: Docs

# Builds and deploys nexus.js.org (docs spec §15.3). apps/docs/deploy.json
# holds the mode, and the mode decides which sites the artifact holds.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    # GitHub evaluates no path filter on a tag push, so a release tag always
    # deploys: the root builds from the newest stable tag after final.
    tags: ['@nexusdi/core@*']
    paths:
      # tools/repo-checks/src/docs/docs-trigger.ts holds this list against the
      # release projects and the docs project's inputs.
      - 'apps/docs/**'
      - 'libs/**'
      - 'internal/**'
      - 'examples/meridian/**'
      - 'tools/doc-examples/**'
      - 'package.json'
      - 'package-lock.json'
      - '.github/workflows/docs.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write # publish the Pages deployment
  id-token: write # Pages deployments are OIDC-authenticated

concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      mode: ${{ steps.config.outputs.mode }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      # The release notice reads the newest stable and RC tags, and the root
      # build after final checks out the newest stable tag.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: .nvmrc
          cache: 'npm'

      - run: npm ci

      - uses: actions/configure-pages@45bfe0192ca1faeb007ade9deae92b16b8254a0d # v6.0.0

      - name: Read deploy.json
        id: config
        run: node apps/docs/tools/deploy/deploy-config.mjs apps/docs/deploy.json

      - name: Require a snapshot revision
        if: steps.config.outputs.revision == '0'
        run: |
          echo "apps/docs/deploy.json records no snapshot yet. Run docs-snapshot.yml and merge its pull request." >&2
          exit 1

      - name: Build the /next/ site
        if: steps.config.outputs.mode != 'snapshot-only'
        env:
          DOCS_BASE_PATH: /next
          DOCS_CHANNEL: next
        run: |
          npx nx build @nexusdi/docs
          npm --prefix apps/docs run postbuild
          node apps/docs/tools/check-budgets.mjs
          mkdir -p build
          mv apps/docs/out build/next-out

      - name: Build the root site from the release
        if: steps.config.outputs.mode == 'final' || steps.config.outputs.mode == 'retired'
        env:
          ROOT_SHA: ${{ steps.config.outputs.root_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -n "$ROOT_SHA" ]; then
            ref="$ROOT_SHA"
          else
            ref="$(git tag --list '@nexusdi/core@*' --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '@[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -n 1)"
          fi
          echo "root builds from ${ref}"
          git worktree add --detach build/root-src "$ref"
          rm -rf build/root-src/apps/docs/content/blog
          cp -R apps/docs/content/blog build/root-src/apps/docs/content/blog
          (cd build/root-src && npm ci && DOCS_BASE_PATH= DOCS_CHANNEL=release npx nx build @nexusdi/docs && npm --prefix apps/docs run postbuild)
          mv build/root-src/apps/docs/out build/root-out

      - name: Download and verify the snapshot
        env:
          MODE: ${{ steps.config.outputs.mode }}
          ROOT_ASSET: ${{ steps.config.outputs.root_asset }}
          ROOT_SHA256: ${{ steps.config.outputs.root_sha256 }}
          ARCHIVE_ASSET: ${{ steps.config.outputs.archive_asset }}
          ARCHIVE_SHA256: ${{ steps.config.outputs.archive_sha256 }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p build/assets build/snapshot-root build/snapshot-archive
          gh release download docs-snapshot-0.3 --pattern "$ROOT_ASSET" --dir build/assets
          node apps/docs/tools/deploy/snapshot-assets.mjs verify "build/assets/$ROOT_ASSET" "$ROOT_SHA256"
          tar -xzf "build/assets/$ROOT_ASSET" -C build/snapshot-root
          if [ "$MODE" = final ] || [ "$MODE" = retired ]; then
            gh release download docs-snapshot-0.3 --pattern "$ARCHIVE_ASSET" --dir build/assets
            node apps/docs/tools/deploy/snapshot-assets.mjs verify "build/assets/$ARCHIVE_ASSET" "$ARCHIVE_SHA256"
            tar -xzf "build/assets/$ARCHIVE_ASSET" -C build/snapshot-archive
          fi

      - name: Assemble the site
        env:
          DEPLOY_MODE: ${{ steps.config.outputs.mode }}
          SITE_DIR: site
          NEXT_OUT: build/next-out
          ROOT_OUT: build/root-out
          SNAPSHOT_ROOT: build/snapshot-root
          SNAPSHOT_ARCHIVE: build/snapshot-archive
        run: node apps/docs/tools/deploy/assemble.mjs

      - name: Check deploy artefacts
        run: node apps/docs/tools/deploy/check-artifact.mjs site "${{ steps.config.outputs.mode }}"

      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@fc324d3547104276b827a68afc52ff2a11cc49c9 # v5.0.0
        with:
          path: site

  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@368f82528645a54fb793d4d04e342629a3f51346 # v5.0.1

  # Requests the deployed site through Cloudflare. A status other than 200, or
  # HTML carrying /cdn-cgi/, fails the run (docs spec §17.3).
  smoke:
    needs: [build, deploy]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # The smoke check needs its own script and the Node version, nothing else.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          sparse-checkout: |
            apps/docs/tools/deploy
            .nvmrc
          sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: .nvmrc

      - run: node apps/docs/tools/deploy/smoke.mjs https://nexus.js.org "${{ needs.build.outputs.mode }}"
```

- [ ] Step 12: Merge Group F and run the first deploy

The snapshot-only subset merges to `main` as its own pull request, ahead of everything else, so nexus.js.org deploys from the new pipeline as soon as possible (spec §18.1 step 5). The subset is Tasks 1, 2 and 25, the `docs-trigger` half of Task 35, and Tasks 37, 38, 39, 40 (unit-tested assembly only), 41 and 42. Each of them runs without the shell, the design system, the runtime or any experiment, and Task 69 holds the `rc`-mode e2e back until the first `rc` deploy. The owner runs the first deploy by hand after the merge:

```bash
gh workflow run docs-snapshot.yml --ref main -f source=6d5e4f3
gh run watch "$(gh run list --workflow docs-snapshot.yml --limit 1 --json databaseId --jq '.[0].databaseId')"
gh release view docs-snapshot-0.3
gh pr list --head docs/snapshot-r1
gh pr merge docs/snapshot-r1 --squash
```

The release lists `nexusdi-docs-0.3-root-r1.tar.gz`, `nexusdi-docs-0.3-archive-r1.tar.gz` and `SHA256SUMS`, and the pull request changes only `apps/docs/deploy.json` to `revision: 1` with both checksums. GitHub starts no workflow for a pull request that `GITHUB_TOKEN` opened, so `ci.yml` does not run on it by itself; close and reopen the pull request (`gh pr close docs/snapshot-r1 && gh pr reopen docs/snapshot-r1`) to start the required checks before the merge. Its merge to `main` triggers `docs.yml` through the `apps/docs/**` path filter. If it does not start, run it by hand:

```bash
gh workflow run docs.yml --ref main
gh run watch "$(gh run list --workflow docs.yml --limit 1 --json databaseId --jq '.[0].databaseId')"
```

Then check nexus.js.org:

```bash
curl -sI https://nexus.js.org/ | grep -Ei '^(HTTP|access-control-allow-origin|cache-control)'
curl -s https://nexus.js.org/ | grep -c 'cdn-cgi'
curl -s https://nexus.js.org/img/logo-white.svg -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n'
curl -s https://nexus.js.org/blog/rss.xml | head -c 200
curl -s https://nexus.js.org/next/ -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n'
```

Expected: `HTTP/2 200`, `access-control-allow-origin: *`, `cache-control: max-age=600`; `0`; `200`; the 0.3 RSS feed; `404` (snapshot-only deploys nothing under `/next/`). In the Cloudflare dashboard for the zone, confirm Rocket Loader, Email Address Obfuscation, Auto Minify for HTML and every other HTML-rewriting feature are off (spec §11.4). The `smoke` job of the run shows each target it checked.

- Produces: a pass or fail record for the sandbox design of spec §11.4 served through Cloudflare. Group G builds on it.

Pass criterion: in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, against `https://nexus.js.org/_sandbox-probe/` through the Cloudflare proxy, every probe field is `true` (the `data:` module import ran, the same-origin module loaded from the opaque-origin frame, `fetch` to another origin was refused, `parent.document` threw `SecurityError`, `indexedDB.open` threw `SecurityError`); the module response carries `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`; the served HTML holds no `/cdn-cgi/`.

Fallback: inline the runtime as one `data:` module. `runtime-assets.mjs` (Task 50) bundles `libs/core/dist` and the harness into one ESM file with esbuild, and `srcdoc.ts` (Task 51) puts its base64 `data:` URL in the import map under `@nexusdi/core`. The CSP already allows `data:` in `script-src`, so the frame makes no module fetch and the Cloudflare CORS behaviour stops mattering. It changes Tasks 50 and 51 and raises the per-run srcdoc size by about 40 kB.

```js
// apps/docs-e2e/probe/sandbox/probe.js
// The parent half of the probe: it builds the sandboxed frame the way the
// playground's srcdoc builder will, then writes what the frame reports.
const base = new URL('.', location.href).href;
const dataModule = `data:text/javascript;base64,${btoa('export const ran = true;')}`;
const importMap = JSON.stringify({
  imports: { '@probe/data': dataModule, '@probe/same': `${base}mod.js` },
});

const digest = await crypto.subtle.digest(
  'SHA-256',
  new TextEncoder().encode(importMap),
);
const hash = btoa(String.fromCharCode(...new Uint8Array(digest)));
const csp = `default-src 'none'; script-src ${location.origin} data: 'sha256-${hash}'; connect-src 'none'`;

const frame = document.createElement('iframe');
frame.setAttribute('sandbox', 'allow-scripts');
frame.srcdoc =
  '<!doctype html><html><head>' +
  `<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="${csp}">` +
  `<script type="importmap">${importMap}</script>` +
  `<script type="module" src="${base}frame.js"></script>` +
  '</head><body></body></html>';

const output = document.getElementById('result');
window.addEventListener('message', (event) => {
  if (event.source !== frame.contentWindow || !event.data?.probe) return;
  output.textContent = JSON.stringify(event.data.probe, null, 2);
  output.dataset.done = 'true';
});
document.body.append(frame);
```

```js
// apps/docs-e2e/probe/sandbox/frame.js
// The frame half: runs inside sandbox="allow-scripts" with an opaque origin.
const result = {
  dataImport: false,
  sameOriginModule: false,
  fetchRefused: false,
  parentDocumentBlocked: false,
  indexedDbBlocked: false,
};

try {
  result.dataImport = (await import('@probe/data')).ran === true;
} catch {
  result.dataImport = false;
}

try {
  result.sameOriginModule = (await import('@probe/same')).loaded === true;
} catch {
  result.sameOriginModule = false;
}

try {
  await fetch('https://example.com/');
} catch {
  result.fetchRefused = true;
}

try {
  void parent.document.title;
} catch (error) {
  result.parentDocumentBlocked =
    error instanceof DOMException && error.name === 'SecurityError';
}

try {
  indexedDB.open('probe');
} catch (error) {
  result.indexedDbBlocked =
    error instanceof DOMException && error.name === 'SecurityError';
}

parent.postMessage({ probe: result }, '*');
```

- [ ] Step 3: Write the Playwright spec

```ts
// apps/docs-e2e/src/sandbox-probe.spec.ts
import { expect, test } from '@playwright/test';

/**
 * Experiment E7 (docs spec §18.1): the sandbox of §11.4 holds when the site is
 * served through Cloudflare. PROBE_URL names the probe page; the spec skips
 * without it, so the default suite never depends on the network.
 */
const probeUrl = process.env.PROBE_URL;

test.describe('the sandbox probe', () => {
  test.skip(!probeUrl, 'set PROBE_URL to run the sandbox probe');

  test('holds every sandbox property', async ({ page, request }) => {
    const module = page.waitForResponse((response) =>
      response.url().endsWith('/mod.js'),
    );
    await page.goto(probeUrl as string);

    const response = await module;
    expect(response.headers()['access-control-allow-origin']).toBe('*');

    const result = page.locator('#result[data-done="true"]');
    await expect(result).toBeAttached({ timeout: 10_000 });
    expect(JSON.parse((await result.textContent()) ?? '{}')).toEqual({
      dataImport: true,
      sameOriginModule: true,
      fetchRefused: true,
      parentDocumentBlocked: true,
      indexedDbBlocked: true,
    });

    const html = await (await request.get(probeUrl as string)).text();
    expect(html).not.toContain('/cdn-cgi/');
  });
});
```

## Group G: The playground runtime

Group G builds the runtime that the console, the Playground and the Academy share (spec §11). The worker compiles and checks reader code. The sandboxed frame runs it, the harness reports what core did, and the parent validates every message it receives. Until the engine merges, `libs/core/dist` is 0.3.1, so unit tests use a fixture core build and the harness refuses a core without `Nexus.create`.

- [ ] Step 1: Write the core types

`types.ts` restates core spec §10 so the runtime and the views compile before the engine exports them. Task 68 replaces the bodies with `export type { … } from '@nexusdi/core'`.

```ts
// apps/docs/components/graph/types.ts
/**
 * The shapes of `graph()` and of the `trace` callback, restated from
 * specs/2026-09-23-core-0.4-design.md §10 at b5ab435. The engine does not
 * export them yet. Task 68 of the Phase 1 plan swaps this file for a type
 * re-export from `@nexusdi/core`.
 */
export type Lifetime = 'singleton' | 'scoped' | 'transient';

export interface NexusGraph {
  modules: Array<{
    id: string;
    name: string;
    global: boolean;
    imports: string[];
    exports: string[];
  }>;
  providers: Array<{
    id: string;
    token: string;
    module: string;
    lifetime: Lifetime | null;
    kind: 'class' | 'value' | 'factory' | 'alias';
    async: boolean | null;
  }>;
  edges: Array<{
    from: string;
    to: string;
    kind: 'required' | 'optional' | 'lazy' | 'all' | 'alias';
  }>;
}

export type TraceEvent =
  | {
      type: 'compile';
      phase: 'create' | 'load';
      modules: number;
      providers: number;
      errors: number;
      durationMs: number;
    }
  | {
      type: 'construct';
      token: string;
      providerId: string;
      module: string;
      lifetime: Lifetime | null;
      scope: string | null;
      async: boolean;
      durationMs: number;
    }
  | {
      type: 'untracked';
      token: string;
      providerId: string;
      reason: 'root-transient' | 'singleton-thunk';
    }
  | { type: 'init'; token: string; providerId: string; durationMs: number }
  | { type: 'scope:create'; scope: string; built: number; durationMs: number }
  | {
      type: 'scope:dispose';
      scope: string;
      disposed: number;
      errors: number;
      durationMs: number;
    }
  | {
      type: 'dispose:instance';
      token: string;
      providerId: string;
      scope: string | null;
    }
  | { type: 'dispose'; disposed: number; errors: number; durationMs: number };
```

- [ ] Step 4: Implement `protocol.ts`

```ts
// apps/docs/components/runtime/protocol.ts
import type { NexusGraph, TraceEvent } from '../graph/types';

/**
 * The messages a sandboxed run posts to the page (spec §11.5).
 *
 * The frame posts and the page never answers: the `srcdoc` carries
 * everything a run needs. The page trusts nothing in these messages. It
 * checks the sender, the version, the run id and the shape, and it renders
 * every string as text.
 */

export type SerializedValue =
  | { t: 'undefined' }
  | { t: 'null' }
  | { t: 'boolean'; v: boolean }
  | { t: 'number'; v: string }
  | { t: 'bigint'; v: string }
  | { t: 'string'; v: string; truncated?: number }
  | { t: 'symbol'; v: string }
  | { t: 'function'; name: string; isClass: boolean }
  | { t: 'array'; items: SerializedValue[]; more?: number }
  | {
      t: 'object';
      className: string | null;
      entries: [string, SerializedValue][];
      more?: number;
    }
  | { t: 'map'; entries: [SerializedValue, SerializedValue][]; more?: number }
  | { t: 'set'; items: SerializedValue[]; more?: number }
  | { t: 'error'; error: SerializedError }
  | { t: 'circular' }
  | { t: 'depth' }
  | { t: 'opaque'; className: string };

export interface SerializedError {
  name: string;
  message: string;
  code?: string;
  stack?: string;
  path?: string[];
  errors?: SerializedError[];
  cause?: SerializedError;
  issues?: { message: string; path?: string[] }[];
}

export type ConsoleLevel = 'log' | 'info' | 'warn' | 'error';

export type RunnerMessageBody =
  | { type: 'ready' }
  | { type: 'console'; level: ConsoleLevel; args: SerializedValue[] }
  | { type: 'trace'; event: TraceEvent }
  | { type: 'graph'; graph: NexusGraph }
  | {
      type: 'test';
      objectiveId: string;
      status: 'pass' | 'fail';
      message?: string;
    }
  | {
      type: 'error';
      phase: 'runtime' | 'timeout' | 'loop';
      name: string;
      code?: string;
      message: string;
      stack?: string;
      errors?: SerializedError[];
      cause?: SerializedError;
    }
  | { type: 'heartbeat' }
  | { type: 'done'; durationMs: number };

export type RunnerMessage = { v: 1; runId: string } & RunnerMessageBody;

type Guard = (value: unknown) => boolean;

const isRecord = (value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> =>
  typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value);
const isString: Guard = (value) => typeof value === 'string';
const isNumber: Guard = (value) =>
  typeof value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(value);
const isBoolean: Guard = (value) => typeof value === 'boolean';
const optional =
  (guard: Guard): Guard =>
  (value) =>
    value === undefined || guard(value);
const nullable =
  (guard: Guard): Guard =>
  (value) =>
    value === null || guard(value);
const oneOf =
  (...allowed: readonly unknown[]): Guard =>
  (value) =>
    allowed.includes(value);
const arrayOf =
  (guard: Guard): Guard =>
  (value) =>
    Array.isArray(value) && value.every(guard);

/** Every listed field passes its guard. Extra fields are ignored. */
function shape(value: unknown, fields: Record<string, Guard>): boolean {
  if (!isRecord(value)) return false;
  return Object.entries(fields).every(([key, guard]) => guard(value[key]));
}

const LIFETIME = oneOf('singleton', 'scoped', 'transient');

/** Nested values and errors stop being checked below this depth. */
const MAX_DEPTH = 16;

function isSerializedError(value: unknown, depth = 0): boolean {
  if (depth > MAX_DEPTH) return false;
  const nested: Guard = (inner) => isSerializedError(inner, depth + 1);
  return shape(value, {
    name: isString,
    message: isString,
    code: optional(isString),
    stack: optional(isString),
    path: optional(arrayOf(isString)),
    errors: optional(arrayOf(nested)),
    cause: optional(nested),
    issues: optional(
      arrayOf((issue) =>
        shape(issue, { message: isString, path: optional(arrayOf(isString)) }),
      ),
    ),
  });
}

function isSerializedValue(value: unknown, depth = 0): boolean {
  if (depth > MAX_DEPTH || !isRecord(value)) return false;
  const nested: Guard = (inner) => isSerializedValue(inner, depth + 1);
  const pair: Guard = (entry) =>
    Array.isArray(entry) &&
    entry.length === 2 &&
    nested(entry[0]) &&
    nested(entry[1]);
  const more = optional(isNumber);

  switch (value.t) {
    case 'undefined':
    case 'null':
    case 'circular':
    case 'depth':
      return true;
    case 'boolean':
      return isBoolean(value.v);
    case 'number':
    case 'bigint':
    case 'symbol':
      return isString(value.v);
    case 'string':
      return isString(value.v) && optional(isNumber)(value.truncated);
    case 'function':
      return isString(value.name) && isBoolean(value.isClass);
    case 'array':
    case 'set':
      return arrayOf(nested)(value.items) && more(value.more);
    case 'object':
      return (
        nullable(isString)(value.className) &&
        arrayOf(
          (entry) =>
            Array.isArray(entry) &&
            entry.length === 2 &&
            isString(entry[0]) &&
            nested(entry[1]),
        )(value.entries) &&
        more(value.more)
      );
    case 'map':
      return arrayOf(pair)(value.entries) && more(value.more);
    case 'error':
      return isSerializedError(value.error, depth + 1);
    case 'opaque':
      return isString(value.className);
    default:
      return false;
  }
}

function isTraceEvent(value: unknown): boolean {
  if (!isRecord(value)) return false;
  switch (value.type) {
    case 'compile':
      return shape(value, {
        phase: oneOf('create', 'load'),
        modules: isNumber,
        providers: isNumber,
        errors: isNumber,
        durationMs: isNumber,
      });
    case 'construct':
      return shape(value, {
        token: isString,
        providerId: isString,
        module: isString,
        lifetime: nullable(LIFETIME),
        scope: nullable(isString),
        async: isBoolean,
        durationMs: isNumber,
      });
    case 'untracked':
      return shape(value, {
        token: isString,
        providerId: isString,
        reason: oneOf('root-transient', 'singleton-thunk'),
      });
    case 'init':
      return shape(value, {
        token: isString,
        providerId: isString,
        durationMs: isNumber,
      });
    case 'scope:create':
      return shape(value, {
        scope: isString,
        built: isNumber,
        durationMs: isNumber,
      });
    case 'scope:dispose':
      return shape(value, {
        scope: isString,
        disposed: isNumber,
        errors: isNumber,
        durationMs: isNumber,
      });
    case 'dispose:instance':
      return shape(value, {
        token: isString,
        providerId: isString,
        scope: nullable(isString),
      });
    case 'dispose':
      return shape(value, {
        disposed: isNumber,
        errors: isNumber,
        durationMs: isNumber,
      });
    default:
      return false;
  }
}

function isGraph(value: unknown): boolean {
  return shape(value, {
    modules: arrayOf((module) =>
      shape(module, {
        id: isString,
        name: isString,
        global: isBoolean,
        imports: arrayOf(isString),
        exports: arrayOf(isString),
      }),
    ),
    providers: arrayOf((provider) =>
      shape(provider, {
        id: isString,
        token: isString,
        module: isString,
        lifetime: nullable(LIFETIME),
        kind: oneOf('class', 'value', 'factory', 'alias'),
        async: nullable(isBoolean),
      }),
    ),
    edges: arrayOf((edge) =>
      shape(edge, {
        from: isString,
        to: isString,
        kind: oneOf('required', 'optional', 'lazy', 'all', 'alias'),
      }),
    ),
  });
}

/** The hand-written guard spec §11.5 requires. No schema library runs here. */
export function isRunnerMessage(data: unknown): data is RunnerMessage {
  if (!isRecord(data) || data.v !== 1 || !isString(data.runId)) return false;

  switch (data.type) {
    case 'ready':
    case 'heartbeat':
      return true;
    case 'done':
      return isNumber(data.durationMs);
    case 'console':
      return (
        oneOf('log', 'info', 'warn', 'error')(data.level) &&
        arrayOf((arg) => isSerializedValue(arg))(data.args)
      );
    case 'trace':
      return isTraceEvent(data.event);
    case 'graph':
      return isGraph(data.graph);
    case 'test':
      return shape(data, {
        objectiveId: isString,
        status: oneOf('pass', 'fail'),
        message: optional(isString),
      });
    case 'error':
      return shape(data, {
        phase: oneOf('runtime', 'timeout', 'loop'),
        name: isString,
        code: optional(isString),
        message: isString,
        stack: optional(isString),
        errors: optional(arrayOf((error) => isSerializedError(error))),
        cause: optional((error) => isSerializedError(error)),
      });
    default:
      return false;
  }
}

/**
 * The message, when it comes from the current run's frame, carries the
 * current run id and has a valid shape. Anything else returns null and the
 * caller drops it.
 */
export function acceptMessage(
  event: { source: unknown; data: unknown },
  run: { window: unknown; runId: string },
): RunnerMessage | null {
  if (event.source !== run.window) return null;
  if (!isRunnerMessage(event.data)) return null;
  if (event.data.runId !== run.runId) return null;
  return event.data;
}
```

```ts
// apps/docs/components/runtime/serialize.ts
import type { SerializedError, SerializedValue } from './protocol';

/**
 * Turns anything a reader's code logs or throws into data that structured
 * clone accepts and that the page renders as text (spec §11.5).
 *
 * The harness serializes before it posts, so `postMessage` never meets a
 * function, a symbol or a class instance. Every limit here keeps one run's
 * payload inside the 256 kB the run controller allows.
 */

export const MAX_STRING = 10_000;
export const MAX_ENTRIES = 100;

const OPAQUE = [
  ['WeakMap', typeof WeakMap === 'undefined' ? null : WeakMap],
  ['WeakSet', typeof WeakSet === 'undefined' ? null : WeakSet],
  ['WeakRef', typeof WeakRef === 'undefined' ? null : WeakRef],
  ['Promise', Promise],
] as const;

function isClass(fn: unknown): boolean {
  try {
    return /^class[\s{]/.test(Function.prototype.toString.call(fn));
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

/** The constructor name, or null for a plain object or a null prototype. */
function className(object: object): string | null {
  const proto: unknown = Object.getPrototypeOf(object);
  if (proto === null || proto === Object.prototype) return null;
  const ctor = (proto as { constructor?: unknown }).constructor;
  return typeof ctor === 'function' && ctor.name !== '' ? ctor.name : null;
}

function text(value: string): SerializedValue {
  return value.length > MAX_STRING
    ? {
        t: 'string',
        v: value.slice(0, MAX_STRING),
        truncated: value.length - MAX_STRING,
      }
    : { t: 'string', v: value };
}

function messageOf(error: unknown): string {
  if (error instanceof Error) return error.message;
  try {
    return String(error);
  } catch {
    return 'an unprintable value';
  }
}

function walk(
  value: unknown,
  depth: number,
  path: WeakSet<object>,
): SerializedValue {
  switch (typeof value) {
    case 'undefined':
      return { t: 'undefined' };
    case 'boolean':
      return { t: 'boolean', v: value };
    case 'number':
      return { t: 'number', v: Object.is(value, -0) ? '-0' : String(value) };
    case 'bigint':
      return { t: 'bigint', v: value.toString() };
    case 'string':
      return text(value);
    case 'symbol':
      return { t: 'symbol', v: value.description ?? '' };
    case 'function':
      return { t: 'function', name: value.name, isClass: isClass(value) };
  }

  if (value === null) return { t: 'null' };
  const object = value as object;

  if (path.has(object)) return { t: 'circular' };
  if (object instanceof Error) {
    return { t: 'error', error: serializeError(object, depth) };
  }
  for (const [name, ctor] of OPAQUE) {
    if (ctor && object instanceof ctor) return { t: 'opaque', className: name };
  }
  if (depth <= 0) return { t: 'depth' };

  path.add(object);
  try {
    const next = (inner: unknown) => walk(inner, depth - 1, path);

    if (Array.isArray(object)) {
      const items = object.slice(0, MAX_ENTRIES).map(next);
      return object.length > MAX_ENTRIES
        ? { t: 'array', items, more: object.length - MAX_ENTRIES }
        : { t: 'array', items };
    }
    if (object instanceof Map) {
      const entries = [...object]
        .slice(0, MAX_ENTRIES)
        .map(
          ([key, inner]) =>
            [next(key), next(inner)] as [SerializedValue, SerializedValue],
        );
      return object.size > MAX_ENTRIES
        ? { t: 'map', entries, more: object.size - MAX_ENTRIES }
        : { t: 'map', entries };
    }
    if (object instanceof Set) {
      const items = [...object].slice(0, MAX_ENTRIES).map(next);
      return object.size > MAX_ENTRIES
        ? { t: 'set', items, more: object.size - MAX_ENTRIES }
        : { t: 'set', items };
    }

    const keys = Object.keys(object);
    const entries = keys
      .slice(0, MAX_ENTRIES)
      .map((key): [string, SerializedValue] => {
        try {
          return [key, next((object as Record<string, unknown>)[key])];
        } catch (error) {
          return [key, text(`[getter threw: ${messageOf(error)}]`)];
        }
      });
    const out: SerializedValue = {
      t: 'object',
      className: className(object),
      entries,
    };
    return keys.length > MAX_ENTRIES
      ? { ...out, more: keys.length - MAX_ENTRIES }
      : out;
  } finally {
    path.delete(object);
  }
}

export function serializeValue(value: unknown, depth = 3): SerializedValue {
  return walk(value, depth, new WeakSet());
}

function stringList(value: unknown): string[] | undefined {
  if (!Array.isArray(value)) return undefined;
  return value.map((item) =>
    typeof item === 'object' && item !== null && 'key' in item
      ? String((item as { key: unknown }).key)
      : String(item),
  );
}

/**
 * An error as data. A NexusError keeps its `code` and `path`; a
 * `BlueprintError` keeps every entry of `errors`; a `ProviderError` keeps
 * its `cause`; a module options error keeps the schema's `issues`.
 * `depth` bounds the nesting, so a cause chain that loops ends.
 */
export function serializeError(error: unknown, depth = 3): SerializedError {
  if (!(error instanceof Error)) {
    return { name: 'Error', message: messageOf(error) };
  }

  const fields = error as Error & Record<string, unknown>;
  const out: SerializedError = { name: error.name, message: error.message };

  if (typeof error.stack === 'string')
    out.stack = error.stack.slice(0, MAX_STRING);
  if (typeof fields.code === 'string') out.code = fields.code;
  const path = stringList(fields.path);
  if (path) out.path = path;

  if (depth > 0) {
    if (Array.isArray(fields.errors)) {
      out.errors = fields.errors
        .slice(0, MAX_ENTRIES)
        .map((inner) => serializeError(inner, depth - 1));
    }
    if (fields.cause !== undefined)
      out.cause = serializeError(fields.cause, depth - 1);
  }

  if (Array.isArray(fields.issues)) {
    out.issues = fields.issues.slice(0, MAX_ENTRIES).map((issue) => {
      const record = (issue ?? {}) as { message?: unknown; path?: unknown };
      const issuePath = stringList(record.path);
      return issuePath
        ? { message: String(record.message), path: issuePath }
        : { message: String(record.message) };
    });
  }

  return out;
}

const more = (count: number | undefined) =>
  count === undefined ? [] : [`… ${count} more`];

/** The text the console log shows for a value. Strings nest quoted. */
export function renderValue(value: SerializedValue, nested = false): string {
  const inner = (item: SerializedValue) => renderValue(item, true);

  switch (value.t) {
    case 'undefined':
    case 'null':
      return value.t;
    case 'boolean':
      return String(value.v);
    case 'number':
      return value.v;
    case 'bigint':
      return `${value.v}n`;
    case 'string': {
      const body = nested ? `'${value.v}'` : value.v;
      return value.truncated === undefined
        ? body
        : `${body} (${value.truncated} more characters)`;
    }
    case 'symbol':
      return `Symbol(${value.v})`;
    case 'function': {
      const kind = value.isClass ? 'class' : 'function';
      return value.name ? `[${kind} ${value.name}]` : `[${kind}]`;
    }
    case 'array':
      return `[${[...value.items.map(inner), ...more(value.more)].join(', ')}]`;
    case 'object': {
      const body = [
        ...value.entries.map(([key, item]) => `${key}: ${inner(item)}`),
        ...more(value.more),
      ];
      const braces = body.length === 0 ? '{}' : `{ ${body.join(', ')} }`;
      return value.className ? `${value.className} ${braces}` : braces;
    }
    case 'map': {
      const body = [
        ...value.entries.map(
          ([key, item]) => `${inner(key)} => ${inner(item)}`,
        ),
        ...more(value.more),
      ];
      return body.length === 0 ? 'Map {}' : `Map { ${body.join(', ')} }`;
    }
    case 'set': {
      const body = [...value.items.map(inner), ...more(value.more)];
      return body.length === 0 ? 'Set {}' : `Set { ${body.join(', ')} }`;
    }
    case 'error':
      return `${value.error.name}: ${value.error.message}`;
    case 'circular':
      return '[Circular]';
    case 'depth':
      return '[…]';
    case 'opaque':
      return `[${value.className}]`;
  }
}
```

```ts
// apps/docs/components/runtime/guard.test.ts

import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

import { GUARD_BUDGET_MS, RunawayError, createGuard } from './guard';

function clock(start = 0) {
  let time = start;
  return {
    now: () => time,
    advance(ms: number) {
      time += ms;
    },
  };
}

describe('createGuard', () => {
  it('lets a turn run for the whole budget', () => {
    const time = clock();
    const { guard } = createGuard(time.now);
    time.advance(GUARD_BUDGET_MS);
    expect(() => guard()).not.toThrow();
  });

  it('throws a RunawayError once one turn runs past the budget', () => {
    const time = clock();
    const { guard } = createGuard(time.now);
    time.advance(GUARD_BUDGET_MS + 1);
    expect(() => guard()).toThrow(RunawayError);
  });

  it('measures from the latest resetTurn', () => {
    const time = clock();
    const state = createGuard(time.now);
    time.advance(900);
    state.resetTurn();
    time.advance(900);
    expect(() => state.guard()).not.toThrow();
    time.advance(101);
    expect(() => state.guard()).toThrow(RunawayError);
  });

  it('stays tripped after a reset, so a catch cannot loop again', () => {
    const time = clock();
    const state = createGuard(time.now);
    time.advance(GUARD_BUDGET_MS + 1);
    expect(() => state.guard()).toThrow(RunawayError);
    state.resetTurn();
    expect(state.tripped).toBe(true);
    expect(() => state.guard()).toThrow(RunawayError);
    expect(() => state.guard()).toThrow(RunawayError);
  });

  it('takes a custom budget', () => {
    const time = clock();
    const { guard } = createGuard(time.now, 50);
    time.advance(51);
    expect(() => guard()).toThrow('more than 50 ms');
  });

  it('names the error for the console and the error view', () => {
    const error = new RunawayError(1000);
    expect(error.name).toBe('RunawayError');
    expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(Error);
    expect(error.message).toBe(
      'A loop or function ran for more than 1000 ms without yielding. The run stopped so the page stays responsive.',
    );
  });
```

- [ ] Step 3: Implement

```ts
// apps/docs/components/runtime/guard.ts

/** One macrotask turn may run this long before the guard ends the run. */
export const GUARD_BUDGET_MS = 1000;

export class RunawayError extends Error {
  override readonly name = 'RunawayError';

  constructor(budgetMs: number) {
    super(
      `A loop or function ran for more than ${budgetMs} ms without yielding. ` +
        'The run stopped so the page stays responsive.',
    );
  }
}

/**
 * The loop guard of spec §11.6.
 *
 * `guard()` compares the clock with the start of the current macrotask turn
 * and throws once the turn has run past the budget. `resetTurn()` marks a new
 * turn; the sandbox calls it from a `setTimeout(0)` chain, so a chain of
 * microtasks that never yields also trips it. Once tripped, every call
 * throws until the frame is removed, so reader code that catches the error
 * cannot loop again.
 */
export function createGuard(
  now: () => number,
  budgetMs = GUARD_BUDGET_MS,
): { guard(): void; resetTurn(): void; readonly tripped: boolean } {
  let turnStart = now();
  let tripped = false;

  return {
    guard() {
      if (!tripped && now() - turnStart <= budgetMs) return;
      tripped = true;
      throw new RunawayError(budgetMs);
    },
    resetTurn() {
      turnStart = now();
    },
    get tripped() {
      return tripped;
    },
  };
}
```
