```ts
// apps/docs/components/runtime/transform.ts
import type * as TS from 'typescript';

import { compilerOptions } from './compiler-options.ts';

/** The global the sandbox boot script installs and every guarded body calls. */
export const GUARD_NAME = '__guard';

const EXTENSION = /\.(?:[cm]?tsx?|[cm]?js)$/;

/** `engineering.ts` becomes `@ship/engineering`, the name the import map serves. */
export function specifierFor(path: string): string {
  return `@ship/${path.replace(/^\.\//, '').replace(EXTENSION, '')}`;
}

/** The reader file a relative specifier names, as a `.ts` path from the root. */
export function resolveRelative(importer: string, spec: string): string {
  const parts = importer.split('/').slice(0, -1);
  for (const segment of spec.split('/')) {
    if (segment === '.' || segment === '') continue;
    if (segment === '..') parts.pop();
    else parts.push(segment);
  }
  return `${parts.join('/').replace(EXTENSION, '')}.ts`;
}

/**
 * The options of compiler-options.ts as TypeScript's own enums.
 *
 * The same JSON goes through `convertCompilerOptionsFromJson` here and in the
 * twoslash prelude, so a fence on a page and a run in the Playground compile
 * under one set of options (spec §14.2).
 */
export function toTsOptions(ts: typeof TS): TS.CompilerOptions {
  const { options, errors } = ts.convertCompilerOptionsFromJson(
    { ...compilerOptions, lib: [...compilerOptions.lib] },
    '/',
  );
  if (errors.length > 0) {
    throw new Error(
      `compiler-options.ts holds an option TypeScript rejects: ${errors
        .map((error) => ts.flattenDiagnosticMessageText(error.messageText, ' '))
        .join('; ')}`,
    );
  }
  return options;
}

function rewriteImports(
  ts: typeof TS,
  importer: string,
): TS.TransformerFactory<TS.SourceFile> {
  return (context) => (sourceFile) => {
    const { factory } = context;

    const rewrite = (node: TS.Expression | undefined) =>
      node && ts.isStringLiteral(node) && node.text.startsWith('.')
        ? factory.createStringLiteral(
            specifierFor(resolveRelative(importer, node.text)),
          )
        : undefined;

    const visit = (node: TS.Node): TS.Node => {
      if (ts.isImportDeclaration(node)) {
        const specifier = rewrite(node.moduleSpecifier);
        if (specifier) {
          return factory.updateImportDeclaration(
            node,
            node.modifiers,
            node.importClause,
            specifier,
            node.attributes,
          );
        }
      }
      if (ts.isExportDeclaration(node) && node.moduleSpecifier) {
        const specifier = rewrite(node.moduleSpecifier);
        if (specifier) {
          return factory.updateExportDeclaration(
            node,
            node.modifiers,
            node.isTypeOnly,
            node.exportClause,
            specifier,
            node.attributes,
          );
        }
      }
      if (
        ts.isCallExpression(node) &&
        node.expression.kind === ts.SyntaxKind.ImportKeyword
      ) {
        const specifier = rewrite(node.arguments[0]);
        if (specifier) {
          return factory.updateCallExpression(
            node,
            node.expression,
            node.typeArguments,
            [specifier, ...node.arguments.slice(1)],
          );
        }
      }
      return ts.visitEachChild(node, visit, context);
    };

    return ts.visitNode(sourceFile, visit) as TS.SourceFile;
  };
}

function insertGuards(ts: typeof TS): TS.TransformerFactory<TS.SourceFile> {
  return (context) => (sourceFile) => {
    const { factory } = context;

    const call = () =>
      factory.createExpressionStatement(
        factory.createCallExpression(
          factory.createIdentifier(GUARD_NAME),
          undefined,
          [],
        ),
      );

    const loopBody = (statement: TS.Statement): TS.Block =>
      ts.isBlock(statement)
        ? factory.updateBlock(statement, [call(), ...statement.statements])
        : factory.createBlock([call(), statement], true);

    // A derived constructor keeps its super call first, so the guard goes
    // straight after it. Every other body starts with the guard.
    const functionBody = (body: TS.Block): TS.Block => {
      const statements = [...body.statements];
      const superAt = statements.findIndex(
        (statement) =>
          ts.isExpressionStatement(statement) &&
          ts.isCallExpression(statement.expression) &&
          statement.expression.expression.kind === ts.SyntaxKind.SuperKeyword,
      );
      statements.splice(superAt + 1, 0, call());
      return factory.updateBlock(body, statements);
    };

    const visit = (original: TS.Node): TS.Node => {
      const node = ts.visitEachChild(original, visit, context);

      if (ts.isForStatement(node)) {
        return factory.updateForStatement(
          node,
          node.initializer,
          node.condition,
          node.incrementor,
          loopBody(node.statement),
        );
      }
      if (ts.isForInStatement(node)) {
        return factory.updateForInStatement(
          node,
          node.initializer,
          node.expression,
          loopBody(node.statement),
        );
      }
      if (ts.isForOfStatement(node)) {
        return factory.updateForOfStatement(
          node,
          node.awaitModifier,
          node.initializer,
          node.expression,
          loopBody(node.statement),
        );
      }
      if (ts.isWhileStatement(node)) {
        return factory.updateWhileStatement(
          node,
          node.expression,
          loopBody(node.statement),
        );
      }
      if (ts.isDoStatement(node)) {
        return factory.updateDoStatement(
          node,
          loopBody(node.statement),
          node.expression,
        );
      }
      if (ts.isFunctionDeclaration(node) && node.body) {
        return factory.updateFunctionDeclaration(
          node,
          node.modifiers,
          node.asteriskToken,
          node.name,
          node.typeParameters,
          node.parameters,
          node.type,
          functionBody(node.body),
        );
      }
      if (ts.isFunctionExpression(node)) {
        return factory.updateFunctionExpression(
          node,
          node.modifiers,
          node.asteriskToken,
          node.name,
          node.typeParameters,
          node.parameters,
          node.type,
          functionBody(node.body),
        );
      }
      if (ts.isArrowFunction(node)) {
        const body = ts.isBlock(node.body)
          ? functionBody(node.body)
          : factory.createBlock(
              [call(), factory.createReturnStatement(node.body)],
              false,
            );
        return factory.updateArrowFunction(
          node,
          node.modifiers,
          node.typeParameters,
          node.parameters,
          node.type,
          node.equalsGreaterThanToken,
          body,
        );
      }
      if (ts.isMethodDeclaration(node) && node.body) {
        return factory.updateMethodDeclaration(
          node,
          node.modifiers,
          node.asteriskToken,
          node.name,
          node.questionToken,
          node.typeParameters,
          node.parameters,
          node.type,
          functionBody(node.body),
        );
      }
      if (ts.isConstructorDeclaration(node) && node.body) {
        return factory.updateConstructorDeclaration(
          node,
          node.modifiers,
          node.parameters,
          functionBody(node.body),
        );
      }
      if (ts.isGetAccessorDeclaration(node) && node.body) {
        return factory.updateGetAccessorDeclaration(
          node,
          node.modifiers,
          node.name,
          node.parameters,
          node.type,
          functionBody(node.body),
        );
      }
      if (ts.isSetAccessorDeclaration(node) && node.body) {
        return factory.updateSetAccessorDeclaration(
          node,
          node.modifiers,
          node.name,
          node.parameters,
          functionBody(node.body),
        );
      }
      return node;
    };

    return ts.visitNode(sourceFile, visit) as TS.SourceFile;
  };
}

const MAP_COMMENT = /\n?\/\/# sourceMappingURL=\S+\s*$/;

/**
 * Transpiles every reader file for one run.
 *
 * `transpileModule` reports no type errors, so a file the checker flags still
 * runs. The worker shows the diagnostics beside it, and the reader decides.
 */
export function transpileRun(
  ts: typeof TS,
  files: Record<string, string>,
): Record<string, { specifier: string; js: string; map: string }> {
  const options = toTsOptions(ts);
  const out: Record<string, { specifier: string; js: string; map: string }> =
    {};

  for (const [path, source] of Object.entries(files)) {
    const result = ts.transpileModule(source, {
      compilerOptions: options,
      fileName: path,
      reportDiagnostics: false,
      transformers: { before: [rewriteImports(ts, path), insertGuards(ts)] },
    });
    out[path] = {
      specifier: specifierFor(path),
      js: result.outputText.replace(MAP_COMMENT, '\n'),
      map: result.sourceMapText ?? '',
    };
  }

  return out;
}
```

```ts
// apps/docs/components/runtime/worker-protocol.ts

/** What the page asks of the TypeScript worker (spec §11.2). */
export type WorkerRequest =
  | { type: 'init'; typesUrl: string }
  | { type: 'update'; files: Record<string, string> }
  | { type: 'emit'; id: number; files: Record<string, string> };

export interface WorkerDiagnostic {
  from: number;
  to: number;
  code: number;
  message: string;
  severity: 'error' | 'warning';
}

export interface EmittedModule {
  specifier: string;
  js: string;
  map: string;
}

export type WorkerResponse =
  | { type: 'ready'; version: string }
  | { type: 'diagnostics'; files: Record<string, WorkerDiagnostic[]> }
  | { type: 'emitted'; id: number; modules: Record<string, EmittedModule> }
  | { type: 'failed'; message: string; id?: number };
```

- [ ] Step 5: Implement the worker core

```ts
// apps/docs/components/runtime/worker-core.ts
import type * as VFS from '@typescript/vfs';
import type * as TS from 'typescript';

import { toTsOptions, transpileRun } from './transform';
import type { EmittedModule, WorkerDiagnostic } from './worker-protocol';

export interface WorkerCore {
  readonly version: string;
  update(files: Record<string, string>): Record<string, WorkerDiagnostic[]>;
  emit(files: Record<string, string>): Record<string, EmittedModule>;
}

const GLOBALS = '/runtime-globals.d.ts';
const absolute = (path: string) => `/${path.replace(/^\.?\//, '')}`;

/**
 * The part of the worker that runs in Node as well as in a Worker, so the
 * tests exercise the real type checker.
 *
 * One virtual environment lives for the whole editor session (spec §11.2).
 * It is rebuilt only when the set of reader files changes, because
 * `@typescript/vfs` updates a file in place but has no call that removes one.
 */
export function createWorkerCore(
  ts: typeof TS,
  vfs: typeof VFS,
  typesMap: Record<string, string>,
): WorkerCore {
  const options = toTsOptions(ts);
  let env: VFS.VirtualTypeScriptEnvironment | null = null;
  let known: string[] = [];

  const rebuild = (files: Record<string, string>) => {
    const fsMap = new Map(Object.entries(typesMap));
    for (const [path, source] of Object.entries(files))
      fsMap.set(absolute(path), source);
    const system = vfs.createSystem(fsMap);
    const roots = [GLOBALS, ...Object.keys(files).map(absolute)].filter(
      (path) => fsMap.has(path),
    );
    env = vfs.createVirtualTypeScriptEnvironment(system, roots, ts, options);
    known = Object.keys(files).sort();
  };

  const toDiagnostic = (diagnostic: TS.Diagnostic): WorkerDiagnostic => {
    const from = diagnostic.start ?? 0;
    return {
      from,
      to: from + (diagnostic.length ?? 0),
      code: diagnostic.code,
      message: ts.flattenDiagnosticMessageText(diagnostic.messageText, '\n'),
      severity:
        diagnostic.category === ts.DiagnosticCategory.Error
          ? 'error'
          : 'warning',
    };
  };

  return {
    version: ts.version,

    update(files) {
      const paths = Object.keys(files).sort();
      if (!env || paths.join('\0') !== known.join('\0')) {
        rebuild(files);
      } else {
        for (const [path, source] of Object.entries(files)) {
          env.updateFile(absolute(path), source);
        }
      }

      const service = env!.languageService;
      const out: Record<string, WorkerDiagnostic[]> = {};
      for (const path of paths) {
        const file = absolute(path);
        out[path] = [
          ...service.getSyntacticDiagnostics(file),
          ...service.getSemanticDiagnostics(file),
        ]
          .filter(
            (diagnostic) =>
              diagnostic.category !== ts.DiagnosticCategory.Suggestion,
          )
          .map(toDiagnostic);
      }
      return out;
    },

    emit(files) {
      return transpileRun(ts, files);
    },
  };
}
```

- [ ] Step 7: Replace the E1 spike with the real worker

The spike from Task 4 only posted its version. The worker now builds the environment once the declarations arrive, debounces diagnostics and emits on request. It keeps the literal `new URL('./ts.worker.ts', import.meta.url)` pattern E1 proved.

```ts
// apps/docs/components/runtime/ts.worker.ts
import * as vfs from '@typescript/vfs';
import ts from 'typescript';

import { transpileRun } from './transform';
import { createWorkerCore, type WorkerCore } from './worker-core';
import type { WorkerRequest, WorkerResponse } from './worker-protocol';

export const UPDATE_DEBOUNCE_MS = 300;

/**
 * The worker's global scope, typed by hand. The app's tsconfig carries the
 * `dom` lib, and adding the `webworker` lib beside it redeclares the same
 * globals.
 */
const scope = self as unknown as {
  postMessage(message: WorkerResponse): void;
  onmessage: ((event: MessageEvent<WorkerRequest>) => void) | null;
};

let core: WorkerCore | null = null;
let pending: Record<string, string> | null = null;
let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;

function flush() {
  if (!core || !pending) return;
  const files = pending;
  pending = null;
  scope.postMessage({ type: 'diagnostics', files: core.update(files) });
}

function schedule() {
  clearTimeout(timer);
  timer = setTimeout(flush, UPDATE_DEBOUNCE_MS);
}

async function handle(request: WorkerRequest) {
  switch (request.type) {
    case 'init': {
      const response = await fetch(request.typesUrl);
      if (!response.ok) {
        throw new Error(
          `The type declarations did not load (HTTP ${response.status}).`,
        );
      }
      core = createWorkerCore(
        ts,
        vfs,
        (await response.json()) as Record<string, string>,
      );
      scope.postMessage({ type: 'ready', version: ts.version });
      if (pending) schedule();
      return;
    }
    case 'update':
      pending = request.files;
      if (core) schedule();
      return;
    case 'emit':
      // Emit needs no declarations, so Run works before `init` finishes.
      scope.postMessage({
        type: 'emitted',
        id: request.id,
        modules: core
          ? core.emit(request.files)
          : transpileRun(ts, request.files),
      });
      return;
  }
}

scope.onmessage = (event) => {
  const request = event.data;
  handle(request).catch((error: unknown) => {
    scope.postMessage({
      type: 'failed',
      message: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error),
      id: request.type === 'emit' ? request.id : undefined,
    });
  });
};
```

- [ ] Step 10: Implement the client

```ts
// apps/docs/components/runtime/worker-client.ts
import type {
  EmittedModule,
  WorkerDiagnostic,
  WorkerRequest,
  WorkerResponse,
} from './worker-protocol';

export type { EmittedModule } from './worker-protocol';

/** The part of `Worker` the client uses, so a test can pass a fake. */
export interface WorkerLike {
  postMessage(message: WorkerRequest): void;
  addEventListener(
    type: 'message',
    listener: (event: { data: WorkerResponse }) => void,
  ): void;
  terminate(): void;
}

export interface TypeChecker {
  ready: Promise<string>;
  update(files: Record<string, string>): void;
  emit(files: Record<string, string>): Promise<Record<string, EmittedModule>>;
  onDiagnostics(
    cb: (files: Record<string, WorkerDiagnostic[]>) => void,
  ): () => void;
  dispose(): void;
}

/**
 * Starts the TypeScript worker. Call it on the reader's first edit or Run,
 * never during render: the worker chunk is about 1 MB gzipped and no page
 * loads it before that (spec §11.7).
 *
 * The `new Worker(new URL(…, import.meta.url))` expression stays literal,
 * because that is the form the bundler recognises and emits as its own chunk.
 */
export function createTypeChecker(options: {
  typesUrl: string;
  createWorker?: () => WorkerLike;
}): TypeChecker {
  const worker =
    options.createWorker?.() ??
    (new Worker(new URL('./ts.worker.ts', import.meta.url), {
      type: 'module',
    }) as unknown as WorkerLike);

  const listeners = new Set<
    (files: Record<string, WorkerDiagnostic[]>) => void
  >();
  const pending = new Map<
    number,
    {
      resolve: (modules: Record<string, EmittedModule>) => void;
      reject: (error: Error) => void;
    }
  >();
  let nextId = 1;
  let settleReady!: {
    resolve: (version: string) => void;
    reject: (error: Error) => void;
  };
  const ready = new Promise<string>((resolve, reject) => {
    settleReady = { resolve, reject };
  });
  // A page that never awaits `ready` must not log an unhandled rejection.
  ready.catch(() => undefined);

  worker.addEventListener('message', ({ data }) => {
    switch (data.type) {
      case 'ready':
        settleReady.resolve(data.version);
        return;
      case 'diagnostics':
        for (const listener of listeners) listener(data.files);
        return;
      case 'emitted':
        pending.get(data.id)?.resolve(data.modules);
        pending.delete(data.id);
        return;
      case 'failed':
        if (data.id === undefined) {
          settleReady.reject(new Error(data.message));
        } else {
          pending.get(data.id)?.reject(new Error(data.message));
          pending.delete(data.id);
        }
        return;
    }
  });

  worker.postMessage({ type: 'init', typesUrl: options.typesUrl });

  return {
    ready,
    update(files) {
      worker.postMessage({ type: 'update', files });
    },
    emit(files) {
      const id = nextId++;
      return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
        pending.set(id, { resolve, reject });
        worker.postMessage({ type: 'emit', id, files });
      });
    },
    onDiagnostics(cb) {
      listeners.add(cb);
      return () => listeners.delete(cb);
    },
    dispose() {
      worker.terminate();
      for (const { reject } of pending.values())
        reject(new Error('The type checker stopped.'));
      pending.clear();
      listeners.clear();
    },
  };
}
```

```js
          exports: [],
        },
      ],

}
```

```js
// apps/docs/tools/playground-types.mjs
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import {
  mkdirSync,
  readFileSync,
  readdirSync,
  rmSync,
  writeFileSync,
} from 'node:fs';
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
import { dirname, join, relative, sep } from 'node:path';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import { gzipSync } from 'node:zlib';

import { compilerOptions } from '../components/runtime/compiler-options.ts';

/**
 * Writes the declarations the playground's TypeScript worker compiles
 * against, as one JSON file keyed by virtual path (spec §11.3).
 *
 * The file name carries a hash of the contents, so a new core build or a
 * TypeScript bump changes the URL and a browser never type-checks against a
 * cached copy of the old API.
 *
 * Runs before `next build` as `nx run @nexusdi/docs:playground-types`. It
 * imports compiler-options.ts directly; Node 24 strips the types.
 */

const REFERENCE_LIB = /^\/\/\/\s*<reference\s+lib="([^"]+)"\s*\/>/gm;

/** Every lib file the given lib names reach, keyed by file name. */
export function libChain(tsLibDir, roots = compilerOptions.lib) {
  const files = new Map();
  const visit = (name) => {
    const file = `lib.${name.toLowerCase()}.d.ts`;
    if (files.has(file)) return;
    const text = readFileSync(join(tsLibDir, file), 'utf8');
    files.set(file, text);
    for (const [, next] of text.matchAll(REFERENCE_LIB)) visit(next);
  };
  for (const root of roots) visit(root);
  return files;
}

function walk(dir) {
  return readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true }).flatMap((entry) => {
    const path = join(dir, entry.name);
    return entry.isDirectory() ? walk(path) : [path];
  });
}

const posix = (path) => path.split(sep).join('/');

export function collectDeclarations({ root, coreDist, valibotDir }) {
  const out = {};

  for (const [file, text] of libChain(
    join(root, 'node_modules/typescript/lib'),
  )) {
    out[`/${file}`] = text;
  }

  out['/runtime-globals.d.ts'] = readFileSync(
    join(root, 'apps/docs/components/runtime/runtime-globals.d.ts'),
    'utf8',
  );

  // `./node` imports node:async_hooks, which no browser has, so it stays out.
  for (const file of walk(coreDist)) {
    const rel = posix(relative(coreDist, file));
    if (!rel.endsWith('.d.ts') || rel.startsWith('node/')) continue;
    out[`/node_modules/@nexusdi/core/dist/${rel}`] = readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
  }
  out['/node_modules/@nexusdi/core/package.json'] = JSON.stringify({
    name: '@nexusdi/core',
    type: 'module',
    types: './dist/index.d.ts',
    exports: {
      '.': { types: './dist/index.d.ts' },
      './testing': { types: './dist/testing/index.d.ts' },
    },
  });

  const valibot = JSON.parse(
    readFileSync(join(valibotDir, 'package.json'), 'utf8'),
  );
  out['/node_modules/valibot/package.json'] = JSON.stringify({
    name: 'valibot',
    version: valibot.version,
    type: 'module',
    types: './dist/index.d.mts',
    exports: { '.': { types: './dist/index.d.mts' } },
  });
  out['/node_modules/valibot/dist/index.d.mts'] = readFileSync(
    join(valibotDir, 'dist/index.d.mts'),
    'utf8',
  );

  return out;
}

export function writeTypes({ runtimeDir, declarations }) {
  const sorted = Object.fromEntries(
    Object.keys(declarations)
      .sort()
      .map((key) => [key, declarations[key]]),
  );
  const json = JSON.stringify(sorted);
  const hash = createHash('sha256').update(json).digest('hex').slice(0, 16);
  const file = `types-${hash}.json`;

  mkdirSync(runtimeDir, { recursive: true });
  for (const old of readdirSync(runtimeDir)) {
    if (/^types-[0-9a-f]{16}\.json$/.test(old) && old !== file) {
      rmSync(join(runtimeDir, old));
    }
  }
  writeFileSync(join(runtimeDir, file), json);
  writeFileSync(
    join(runtimeDir, 'types-manifest.json'),
    `${JSON.stringify({ typesFile: file }, null, 2)}\n`,
  );

  return {
    file,
    bytes: Buffer.byteLength(json),
    gzipBytes: gzipSync(json).length,
  };
}

if (import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1] ?? '').href) {
  const app = join(import.meta.dirname, '..');
  const root = join(app, '../..');
  const coreDist = process.env.DOCS_CORE_DIST ?? join(root, 'libs/core/dist');
  // valibot exports no `./package.json`, so the entry point locates it.
  const valibotDir = dirname(
    dirname(createRequire(import.meta.url).resolve('valibot')),
  );
  const { file, gzipBytes } = writeTypes({
    runtimeDir: join(app, 'public/runtime'),
    declarations: collectDeclarations({ root, coreDist, valibotDir }),
  });
  console.log(
    `wrote public/runtime/${file} (${(gzipBytes / 1024).toFixed(1)} kB gzipped)`,
  );
}
```

```ts
// apps/docs/components/runtime/sandbox/post.ts
import type { RunnerMessage, RunnerMessageBody } from '../protocol';

export type Post = (body: RunnerMessageBody) => void;

/**
 * Posts one run's messages to the page. The frame has an opaque origin and
 * the page's origin cannot be named from inside it, so the target origin is
 * `'*'`; the page checks the sender itself (spec §11.5).
 */
export function createPoster(
  runId: string,
  target: { postMessage(message: unknown, targetOrigin: string): void },
): Post {
  return (body) => {
    const message = { v: 1, runId, ...body } as RunnerMessage;
    target.postMessage(message, '*');
  };
}

const KEY = '__nexusPost';

/** Boot calls this before it imports the reader's code. */
export function publishPoster(post: Post): void {
  (globalThis as Record<string, unknown>)[KEY] = post;
}

/** The poster boot published, read on every call because boot runs first. */
export function sharedPoster(): Post {
  return (body) => {
    const post = (globalThis as Record<string, unknown>)[KEY] as
      Post | undefined;
    post?.(body);
  };
}
```

```ts
// apps/docs/components/runtime/sandbox/harness.ts
import type { NexusGraph, TraceEvent } from '../../graph/types';
import type { Post } from './post';

interface ContainerLike {
  graph(): NexusGraph;
}

type CreateOptions = { trace?: (event: TraceEvent) => void } & Record<
  string,
  unknown
>;

export interface NexusLike {
  create?: (root: unknown, options?: CreateOptions) => Promise<ContainerLike>;
  prototype: { load?: (this: ContainerLike, module: unknown) => Promise<void> };
}

export const MISSING_CREATE =
  '[harness] @nexusdi/core in this build has no Nexus.create. The playground needs the 0.4 engine.';

const PATCHED = Symbol.for('nexusdi.harness.patched');

/**
 * Patches the real `Nexus` class so a run reports what core did (spec §11.4).
 *
 * The static `create` posts every trace event, then calls the reader's own
 * `trace`, and posts `graph()` once the container is built. `load()` posts
 * `graph()` after it resolves. No subclass exists, so `instanceof Nexus`
 * holds and the reader observes no change apart from the reports.
 */
export function installHarness(core: { Nexus: NexusLike }, post: Post): void {
  const { Nexus } = core;
  if ((Nexus as unknown as Record<symbol, boolean>)[PATCHED]) return;

  const create = Nexus.create;
  if (typeof create !== 'function') throw new Error(MISSING_CREATE);

  Nexus.create = async function (this: unknown, root, options = {}) {
    const readerTrace = options.trace;
    const container = await create.call(this, root, {
      ...options,
      trace: (event: TraceEvent) => {
        post({ type: 'trace', event });
        readerTrace?.(event);
      },
    });
    post({ type: 'graph', graph: container.graph() });
    return container;
  };

  const load = Nexus.prototype.load;
  if (typeof load === 'function') {
    Nexus.prototype.load = async function (
      this: ContainerLike,
      module: unknown,
    ) {
      await load.call(this, module);
      post({ type: 'graph', graph: this.graph() });
    };
  }

  Object.defineProperty(Nexus, PATCHED, { value: true });
}
```

```ts
// apps/docs/components/runtime/sandbox/harness-testing.ts
import type { NexusGraph } from '../../graph/types';
import type { Post } from './post';

const hasCreate = (
  value: unknown,
): value is { create: (...args: unknown[]) => unknown } =>
  typeof value === 'object' &&
  value !== null &&
  typeof (value as { create?: unknown }).create === 'function';

/**
 * Wraps a testing builder so its `create` posts the graph, and so every
 * builder a chained call returns is wrapped the same way. Core spec §11
 * makes the builder immutable: each `override` returns a new builder.
 */
export function wrapTestingBuilder<B extends object>(
  builder: B,
  post: Post,
): B {
  return new Proxy(builder, {
    get(target, property) {
      const value = Reflect.get(target, property, target) as unknown;
      if (typeof value !== 'function') return value;

      if (property === 'create') {
        return async (...args: unknown[]) => {
          const container = (await value.apply(target, args)) as {
            graph(): NexusGraph;
          };
          post({ type: 'graph', graph: container.graph() });
          return container;
        };
      }

      return (...args: unknown[]) => {
        const result = value.apply(target, args) as unknown;
        return hasCreate(result) ? wrapTestingBuilder(result, post) : result;
      };
    },
  });
}

export function wrapCreateTestingContainer<
  A extends unknown[],
  B extends object,
>(createTestingContainer: (...args: A) => B, post: Post): (...args: A) => B {
  return (...args) => wrapTestingBuilder(createTestingContainer(...args), post);
}
```

A testing container built through the patched `Nexus.create` posts its graph twice: once from `create`, once from the wrapper. The views keep the newest graph, so the second post changes nothing a reader sees.

```ts
        type: 'error',
        phase: 'loop',
        name: 'RunawayError',
      }),

      fake.advance(1001);
      try {

      } catch (error) {

      expect.objectContaining({ type: 'error', phase: 'loop' }),
    );

    const fake = fakeEnv(async () => undefined);
    await boot(fake.env);
    fake.listeners.unhandledrejection({ reason: new Error('late') });
    fake.listeners.error({ error: new RangeError('bad rods') });
    const errors = fake.sent

      .map((m) => (m as { message: string }).message);
    expect(errors).toEqual(['late', 'bad rods']);
```

- [ ] Step 7: Implement boot

```ts
// apps/docs/components/runtime/sandbox/boot.ts
import { GUARD_BUDGET_MS, RunawayError, createGuard } from '../guard';
import type { ConsoleLevel } from '../protocol';
import { serializeError, serializeValue } from '../serialize';
import { createPoster, publishPoster } from './post';

export const RUN_META = 'nexus-run';
export const HEARTBEAT_MS = 250;

/** Everything boot touches, passed in so a test can run it in Node. */
export interface BootEnv {
  runId: string;
  parent: { postMessage(message: unknown, targetOrigin: string): void };
  global: Record<string, unknown>;
  console: Record<ConsoleLevel, (...args: unknown[]) => void>;
  now(): number;
  setInterval(cb: () => void, ms: number): unknown;
  setTimeout(cb: () => void, ms: number): unknown;
  addEventListener(
    type: 'error' | 'unhandledrejection',
    cb: (event: {
      error?: unknown;
      message?: string;
      reason?: unknown;
    }) => void,
  ): void;
  importMain(): Promise<unknown>;
}

const LEVELS: ConsoleLevel[] = ['log', 'info', 'warn', 'error'];

/**
 * Runs one reader program inside the sandboxed frame (spec §11.4 to §11.6).
 *
 * Order matters. The poster and the guard exist before the reader's first
 * module evaluates, because the harness posts through the poster and every
 * transpiled body calls `__guard()`.
 */
export async function boot(env: BootEnv): Promise<void> {
  const post = createPoster(env.runId, env.parent);
  publishPoster(post);

  const guard = createGuard(() => env.now(), GUARD_BUDGET_MS);
  env.global.__guard = guard.guard;

  env.setInterval(() => post({ type: 'heartbeat' }), HEARTBEAT_MS);

  // A new macrotask turn starts whenever this callback runs. A synchronous
  // loop or a microtask chain that never yields keeps it from running, and
  // the guard trips.
  const tick = () => {
    guard.resetTurn();
    env.setTimeout(tick, 0);
  };
  env.setTimeout(tick, 0);

  for (const level of LEVELS) {
    const original = env.console[level];
    env.console[level] = (...args: unknown[]) => {
      post({
        type: 'console',
        level,
        args: args.map((arg) => serializeValue(arg)),
      });
      original.apply(env.console, args);
    };
  }

  const report = (error: unknown) => {
    const serialized = serializeError(error);
    post({
      type: 'error',
      phase:
        error instanceof RunawayError || guard.tripped ? 'loop' : 'runtime',
      name: serialized.name,
      code: serialized.code,
      message: serialized.message,
      stack: serialized.stack,
      errors: serialized.errors,
      cause: serialized.cause,
    });
  };

  env.addEventListener('error', (event) =>
    report(event.error ?? event.message),
  );
  env.addEventListener('unhandledrejection', (event) => report(event.reason));

  post({ type: 'ready' });
  const started = env.now();
  try {
    await env.importMain();
    // Reader code that caught the RunawayError and finished still ran away.
    if (guard.tripped) report(new RunawayError(GUARD_BUDGET_MS));
  } catch (error) {
    report(error);
  }
  post({ type: 'done', durationMs: env.now() - started });
}
```

```ts
// apps/docs/components/runtime/sandbox/boot-entry.ts
import { boot, RUN_META } from './boot';

const runId = document
  .querySelector(`meta[name="${RUN_META}"]`)
  ?.getAttribute('content');
if (!runId)
  throw new Error(`The sandbox document carries no <meta name="${RUN_META}">.`);

void boot({
  runId,
  parent: window.parent,
  global: globalThis as unknown as Record<string, unknown>,
  console: console as unknown as Record<
    'log' | 'info' | 'warn' | 'error',
    (...args: unknown[]) => void
  >,
  now: () => performance.now(),
  setInterval: (cb, ms) => setInterval(cb, ms),
  setTimeout: (cb, ms) => setTimeout(cb, ms),
  addEventListener: (type, cb) =>
    window.addEventListener(type, cb as unknown as EventListener),
  // `@ship/main` is the reader's entry file, a data: URL in the import map.
  importMain: () => import('@ship/main'),
});
```

Spec §11.4 and §14.2: `runtime/core-<hash>/` is a copy of `libs/core/dist`, so the code a reader runs is the code the workspace built and tested at that commit. The hash covers the core files and the three bundles, so a harness change also changes the URL (spec §11.7). `DOCS_CORE_DIST` points the script at another build; the e2e suite uses it until the engine merges.

- [ ] Step 4: Implement

```js
// apps/docs/tools/runtime-assets.mjs
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import {
  cpSync,
  existsSync,
  mkdirSync,
  readFileSync,
  readdirSync,
  rmSync,
  writeFileSync,
} from 'node:fs';
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
import { dirname, join, relative, sep } from 'node:path';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';

import { build } from 'esbuild';

/**
 * Writes what the sandboxed frame loads (spec §11.4, §14.2):
 *
 * - `core-<hash>/`: core's built JavaScript, plus `harness.js`,
 *   `harness-testing.js` and `boot.js`, served at the URLs the import map
 *   names. The hash covers every file in the directory, so any change moves
 *   the URL and a cached copy never runs against a new page.
 * - `valibot-1.5.0/index.min.mjs`: valibot's own minified ESM build. The
 *   version sits in the path.
 * - `manifest.json`: the hash and the declarations file, which the page reads
 *   to write the import map.
 *
 * `DOCS_CORE_DIST` replaces `libs/core/dist`. Until the 0.4 engine merges the
 * e2e build points it at a fixture core, because 0.3.1 has no `Nexus.create`.
 */

export const VALIBOT_VERSION = '1.5.0';
const VALIBOT_DIR = `valibot-${VALIBOT_VERSION}`;

const posix = (path) => path.split(sep).join('/');

function walk(dir) {
  return readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true }).flatMap((entry) => {
    const path = join(dir, entry.name);
    return entry.isDirectory() ? walk(path) : [path];
  });
}

/** Core's runtime files: JavaScript and its maps, no declarations. */
function coreFiles(coreDist) {
  return walk(coreDist)
    .map((file) => ({ path: posix(relative(coreDist, file)), file }))
    .filter(({ path }) => /\.(?:m?js|js\.map)$/.test(path))
    .map(({ path, file }) => ({ path, contents: readFileSync(file) }));
}

export function hashTree(files) {
  const hash = createHash('sha256');
  for (const { path, contents } of [...files].sort((a, b) =>
    a.path.localeCompare(b.path),
  )) {
    hash.update(path).update('\0').update(contents).update('\0');
  }
  return hash.digest('hex').slice(0, 12);
}

export function assertValibot(valibotDir, expected = VALIBOT_VERSION) {
  const { version } = JSON.parse(
    readFileSync(join(valibotDir, 'package.json'), 'utf8'),
  );
  if (version !== expected) {
    throw new Error(
      `valibot ${version} is installed, and the playground runtime serves ${expected}. ` +
        'Bump apps/docs, examples/meridian and VALIBOT_VERSION in tools/runtime-assets.mjs together.',
    );
  }
}

/** Keeps the three specifiers the import map owns out of the bundles. */
const sandboxSpecifiers = {
  name: 'sandbox-specifiers',
  setup(builder) {
    builder.onResolve({ filter: /^@nexusdi\/core$/ }, () => ({
      path: './index.js',
      external: true,
    }));
    builder.onResolve({ filter: /^@nexusdi\/core\/testing$/ }, () => ({
      path: './testing/index.js',
      external: true,
    }));
    builder.onResolve({ filter: /^@ship\/main$/ }, () => ({
      path: '@ship/main',
      external: true,
    }));
  },
};

async function bundle(appDir) {
  const sandbox = join(appDir, 'components/runtime/sandbox');
  const result = await build({
    absWorkingDir: appDir,
    entryPoints: {
      harness: join(sandbox, 'harness-entry.ts'),
      'harness-testing': join(sandbox, 'harness-testing-entry.ts'),
      boot: join(sandbox, 'boot-entry.ts'),
    },
    outdir: 'out',
    bundle: true,
    format: 'esm',
    platform: 'browser',
    target: 'es2022',
    minify: true,
    write: false,
    logLevel: 'silent',
    plugins: [sandboxSpecifiers],
  });
  return result.outputFiles.map((output) => ({
    path: posix(relative(join(appDir, 'out'), output.path)),
    contents: Buffer.from(output.contents),
  }));
}

export async function buildRuntimeAssets({
  appDir,
  outDir,
  coreDist,
  valibotDir,
}) {
  const typesManifest = join(outDir, 'types-manifest.json');
  if (!existsSync(typesManifest)) {
    throw new Error(
      `${typesManifest} is missing. Run \`npx nx run @nexusdi/docs:playground-types\` first.`,
    );
  }
  const { typesFile } = JSON.parse(readFileSync(typesManifest, 'utf8'));

  if (!existsSync(join(coreDist, 'index.js'))) {
    throw new Error(
      `${coreDist} holds no index.js. Build core with \`npx nx build @nexusdi/core\`.`,
    );
  }
  assertValibot(valibotDir);

  const files = [...coreFiles(coreDist), ...(await bundle(appDir))];
  const coreHash = hashTree(files);
  const coreDir = join(outDir, `core-${coreHash}`);

  mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true });
  for (const entry of readdirSync(outDir)) {
    if (/^core-[0-9a-f]{12}$/.test(entry) && entry !== `core-${coreHash}`) {
      rmSync(join(outDir, entry), { recursive: true, force: true });
    }
  }
  for (const { path, contents } of files) {
    const target = join(coreDir, path);
    mkdirSync(dirname(target), { recursive: true });
    writeFileSync(target, contents);
  }

  mkdirSync(join(outDir, VALIBOT_DIR), { recursive: true });
  cpSync(
    join(valibotDir, 'dist/index.min.mjs'),
    join(outDir, VALIBOT_DIR, 'index.min.mjs'),
  );

  writeFileSync(
    join(outDir, 'manifest.json'),
    `${JSON.stringify({ coreHash, typesFile, valibot: VALIBOT_DIR }, null, 2)}\n`,
  );

  return { coreHash, coreDir };
}

if (import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1] ?? '').href) {
  const appDir = join(import.meta.dirname, '..');
  const root = join(appDir, '../..');
  const { coreHash } = await buildRuntimeAssets({
    appDir,
    outDir: join(appDir, 'public/runtime'),
    coreDist: process.env.DOCS_CORE_DIST ?? join(root, 'libs/core/dist'),
    valibotDir: dirname(
      dirname(createRequire(import.meta.url).resolve('valibot')),
    ),
  });
  console.log(`wrote public/runtime/core-${coreHash}/`);
}
```

```ts
// @vitest-environment node
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';

import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

import { buildSrcdoc, dataUrlFor, importMapHash } from './srcdoc';

const manifest = {
  coreHash: 'abc123',
  typesFile: 'types-def456.json',
  valibot: 'valibot-1.5.0',
};

async function document() {
  return buildSrcdoc({
    origin: 'https://nexus.js.org',
    basePath: '/next',
    manifest,
    runId: 'run-1',
    modules: {
      '@ship/main':
        "import { reactor } from '@ship/engineering';\nconsole.log(reactor);",
      '@ship/engineering': "export const reactor = 'online';",
    },
  });
}

function importMapText(html: string): string {
  const match = /<script type="importmap">([\s\S]*?)<\/script>/.exec(html);
  if (!match?.[1]) throw new Error('the srcdoc carries no import map');
  return match[1];
}

describe('importMapHash', () => {
  it('is the base64 SHA-256 of the exact text', async () => {
    const text = '{"imports":{}}';
    expect(await importMapHash(text)).toBe(
      createHash('sha256').update(text).digest('base64'),
    );
  });
});

describe('dataUrlFor', () => {
  it('round-trips UTF-8 source through base64', () => {
    const js = "console.log('Kepler-442b · 1.21 GW');";
    const url = dataUrlFor(js);
    expect(url.startsWith('data:text/javascript;base64,')).toBe(true);
    expect(
      Buffer.from(
        url.slice('data:text/javascript;base64,'.length),
        'base64',
      ).toString('utf8'),
    ).toBe(js);
  });
});

describe('buildSrcdoc', () => {
  it('allows the origin, data: modules and the hash of its own import map', async () => {
    const html = await document();
    const hash = createHash('sha256')
      .update(importMapText(html))
      .digest('base64');

    expect(html).toContain(
      `<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="default-src 'none'; script-src https://nexus.js.org data: 'sha256-${hash}'; connect-src 'none'">`,
    );
  });

  it('maps core, testing and valibot to runtime URLs under the base path', async () => {
    const { imports } = JSON.parse(importMapText(await document())) as {
      imports: Record<string, string>;
    };

    expect(imports['@nexusdi/core']).toBe(
      'https://nexus.js.org/next/runtime/core-abc123/harness.js',
    );
    expect(imports['@nexusdi/core/testing']).toBe(
      'https://nexus.js.org/next/runtime/core-abc123/harness-testing.js',
    );
    expect(imports['valibot']).toBe(
      'https://nexus.js.org/next/runtime/valibot-1.5.0/index.min.mjs',
    );
  });

  it('carries every reader module as a data: URL', async () => {
    const { imports } = JSON.parse(importMapText(await document())) as {
      imports: Record<string, string>;
    };

    expect(imports['@ship/engineering']).toBe(
      dataUrlFor("export const reactor = 'online';"),
    );
    expect(
      imports['@ship/main']?.startsWith('data:text/javascript;base64,'),
    ).toBe(true);
  });

  it('names the run in a meta tag and loads boot.js as its only other script', async () => {
    const html = await document();

    expect(html).toContain('<meta name="nexus-run" content="run-1">');
    expect(html.match(/<script\b/g)).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(html).toContain(
      '<script type="module" src="https://nexus.js.org/next/runtime/core-abc123/boot.js"></script>',
    );

  it('escapes a run id before it reaches an attribute', async () => {

      origin: 'http://localhost:4310',
      basePath: '',
      manifest,
      runId: '"><script>',
      modules: {},
    });

    expect(html).toContain('content="&quot;&gt;&lt;script&gt;"');
  });
});
```

```ts
/** What `tools/runtime-assets.mjs` writes to `public/runtime/manifest.json`. */
export interface RuntimeManifest {
  /** The content hash in `runtime/core-<coreHash>/`. */
  coreHash: string;
  /** The declarations file, `types-<hash>.json`, relative to `runtime/`. */
  typesFile: string;
  /** The valibot directory under `runtime/`, `valibot-1.5.0`. */

}
```

`apps/docs/components/runtime/srcdoc.ts`:

```ts
import type { RuntimeManifest } from './manifest';

const encoder = new TextEncoder();

function base64(bytes: Uint8Array): string {
  let binary = '';
  // Chunked, so a large module never exceeds the argument limit of
  // String.fromCharCode.
  for (let at = 0; at < bytes.length; at += 0x8000) {
    binary += String.fromCharCode(...bytes.subarray(at, at + 0x8000));
  }
  return btoa(binary);
}

/** A module as the import map and every stack frame name it. */
export function dataUrlFor(js: string): string {
  return `data:text/javascript;base64,${base64(encoder.encode(js))}`;
}

/** The SHA-256 of the import map text, base64, as CSP's hash source takes it. */
export async function importMapHash(json: string): Promise<string> {
  const digest = await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', encoder.encode(json));
  return base64(new Uint8Array(digest));
}

export function runtimeUrl(
  origin: string,
  basePath: string,
  path: string,
): string {
  return `${origin}${basePath}/runtime/${path}`;
}

function attribute(value: string): string {
  return value
    .replace(/&/g, '&amp;')
    .replace(/"/g, '&quot;')
    .replace(/</g, '&lt;')
    .replace(/>/g, '&gt;');
}

export interface SrcdocInput {
  origin: string;
  basePath: string;
  manifest: RuntimeManifest;
  runId: string;
  /** Bare specifier (`@ship/main`) to emitted JavaScript. */
  modules: Record<string, string>;
}

/**
 * The whole document of one sandboxed run (spec §11.4).
 *
 * The frame receives everything here and the parent posts nothing after it
 * creates the frame. The import map is the only inline script, so the CSP
 * allows exactly its hash and needs no 'unsafe-inline'.
 */
export async function buildSrcdoc(input: SrcdocInput): Promise<string> {
  const { origin, basePath, manifest, runId, modules } = input;
  const core = `core-${manifest.coreHash}`;

  const imports: Record<string, string> = {
    '@nexusdi/core': runtimeUrl(origin, basePath, `${core}/harness.js`),
    '@nexusdi/core/testing': runtimeUrl(
      origin,
      basePath,
      `${core}/harness-testing.js`,
    ),
    valibot: runtimeUrl(origin, basePath, `${manifest.valibot}/index.min.mjs`),
  };
  for (const [specifier, js] of Object.entries(modules).sort(([a], [b]) =>
    a.localeCompare(b),
  )) {
    imports[specifier] = dataUrlFor(js);
  }

  const map = JSON.stringify({ imports });
  const hash = await importMapHash(map);
  const csp = `default-src 'none'; script-src ${origin} data: 'sha256-${hash}'; connect-src 'none'`;

  return [
    '<!doctype html>',
    '<html lang="en">',
    '<head>',
    '<meta charset="utf-8">',
    `<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="${attribute(csp)}">`,
    `<meta name="nexus-run" content="${attribute(runId)}">`,
    `<script type="importmap">${map}</script>`,
    `<script type="module" src="${attribute(runtimeUrl(origin, basePath, `${core}/boot.js`))}"></script>`,
    '</head>',
    '<body></body>',
    '</html>',
  ].join('\n');
}
```

```ts
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';

import {
  createRunController,
  type RunControllerOptions,
} from './run-controller';

const html = '<!doctype html><title>run</title>';

function setup(options: RunControllerOptions = {}) {
  const host = document.createElement('div');
  document.body.append(host);
  const frames: HTMLIFrameElement[] = [];
  let next = 0;
  const controller = createRunController(host, {
    createFrame: () => {
      const frame = document.createElement('iframe');
      frames.push(frame);
      return frame;
    },
    newRunId: () => `run-${(next += 1)}`,
    ...options,
  });
  return { host, frames, controller };
}

function post(source: Window | null, data: unknown) {
  window.dispatchEvent(new MessageEvent('message', { data, source }));
}

const flush = () => vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(0);

beforeEach(() => {
  vi.useFakeTimers();
});

afterEach(() => {
  vi.useRealTimers();
  document.body.replaceChildren();
});

describe('createRunController', () => {
  it('creates one frame whose sandbox is exactly allow-scripts', async () => {
    const { host, frames, controller } = setup();
    controller.run({ document: () => html });
    await flush();

    expect(frames).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(frames[0]?.getAttribute('sandbox')).toBe('allow-scripts');
    expect(host.querySelectorAll('iframe')).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it('accepts messages from its frame and ends on done', async () => {
    const { frames, controller } = setup();
    const handle = controller.run({ document: () => html });
    await flush();
    const source = frames[0]!.contentWindow;

    post(source, { v: 1, runId: handle.runId, type: 'ready' });
    post(source, {
      v: 1,
      runId: handle.runId,
      type: 'console',
      level: 'log',
      args: [{ t: 'string', v: 'ShipComputer online' }],
    });
    post(source, { v: 1, runId: handle.runId, type: 'done', durationMs: 4 });

    await expect(handle.done).resolves.toEqual({ status: 'done', dropped: 0 });
    expect(handle.messages.map((message) => message.type)).toEqual([
      'ready',
      'console',
      'done',
    ]);
    expect(frames[0]!.isConnected).toBe(false);
  });

  it('drops a wrong run id, a wrong version and a stranger window', async () => {
    const { frames, controller } = setup();
    const stranger = document.createElement('iframe');
    document.body.append(stranger);
    const handle = controller.run({ document: () => html });
    await flush();
    const source = frames[0]!.contentWindow;

    post(source, { v: 1, runId: 'run-99', type: 'ready' });
    post(source, { v: 2, runId: handle.runId, type: 'ready' });
    post(stranger.contentWindow, { v: 1, runId: handle.runId, type: 'ready' });
    post(source, {
      v: 1,
      runId: handle.runId,
      type: 'console',
      level: 'shout',
    });

    expect(handle.messages).toEqual([]);

    for (let at = 0; at < 1_005; at += 1) {

        runId: handle.runId,
        type: 'console',
        level: 'log',
        args: [{ t: 'number', v: String(at) }],
      });
    }
    post(source, { v: 1, runId: handle.runId, type: 'done', durationMs: 1 });

    await expect(handle.done).resolves.toEqual({ status: 'done', dropped: 5 });
    expect(
      handle.messages.filter((message) => message.type === 'console'),
    ).toHaveLength(1_000);
  });

  it('drops a message that would pass 256 kB of payload', async () => {
    const { frames, controller } = setup();
    const handle = controller.run({ document: () => html });
    await flush();

    post(frames[0]!.contentWindow, {
      v: 1,
      runId: handle.runId,
      type: 'console',
      level: 'log',
      args: [{ t: 'string', v: 'x'.repeat(300 * 1024) }],
    });
    post(frames[0]!.contentWindow, {

      runId: handle.runId,
      type: 'done',
      durationMs: 1,
    });

    await expect(handle.done).resolves.toEqual({ status: 'done', dropped: 1 });
  });

  it('ends a run at the 10-second wall clock and removes the frame', async () => {
    const { frames, controller } = setup();
    const handle = controller.run({ document: () => html });
    await flush();

    await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(10_000);

    await expect(handle.done).resolves.toEqual({

    const { frames, controller } = setup();
    const handle = controller.run({ document: () => html });
    await flush();
    const source = frames[0]!.contentWindow;

    post(source, { v: 1, runId: handle.runId, type: 'ready' });
    for (let beat = 0; beat < 12; beat += 1) {
      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(250);
      post(source, { v: 1, runId: handle.runId, type: 'heartbeat' });
    }
    expect(frames[0]!.isConnected).toBe(true);

    await expect(handle.done).resolves.toEqual({
      status: 'watchdog',
      dropped: 0,
    });
    expect(frames[0]!.isConnected).toBe(false);

  it('reports a loop error as the loop status', async () => {
    const { frames, controller } = setup();
    const handle = controller.run({ document: () => html });
    await flush();

    post(frames[0]!.contentWindow, {
      v: 1,
      runId: handle.runId,
      type: 'error',

    const { frames, controller } = setup();
    const first = controller.run({ document: () => html });
    await flush();
    const firstFrame = frames[0]!;
    const firstWindow = firstFrame.contentWindow;

    const second = controller.run({ document: () => html });
    await flush();
    const secondWindow = frames[1]!.contentWindow;

    expect(firstFrame.isConnected).toBe(false);
    await expect(first.done).resolves.toEqual({
      status: 'superseded',
      dropped: 0,
    });

    const late = {
      type: 'console',
      level: 'log',
      args: [{ t: 'string', v: 'late' }],
    };
    post(firstWindow, { v: 1, runId: first.runId, ...late });
    post(secondWindow, { v: 1, runId: first.runId, ...late });
    post(firstWindow, { v: 1, runId: second.runId, ...late });

    expect(second.messages).toEqual([]);
    expect(first.messages).toEqual([]);

    post(secondWindow, { v: 1, runId: second.runId, type: 'ready' });
    expect(second.messages.map((message) => message.type)).toEqual(['ready']);
  });

  it('ends a run whose document fails to build', async () => {
    const { host, controller } = setup();
    const handle = controller.run({
      document: () =>
        Promise.reject(new Error('The runtime manifest is missing.')),
    });
    await flush();

    await expect(handle.done).resolves.toEqual({ status: 'error', dropped: 0 });
    expect(host.querySelectorAll('iframe')).toHaveLength(0);
    expect(handle.messages.at(-1)).toMatchObject({
      type: 'error',
      name: 'SandboxError',
      message: 'The runtime manifest is missing.',
    });
  });
});
```

- [ ] Step 7: Implement the run controller

`apps/docs/components/runtime/run-controller.ts`:

```ts
import { acceptMessage, type RunnerMessage } from './protocol';

export interface RunInput {
  /** The srcdoc for this run; `buildSrcdoc` with the run id filled in. */
  document: (runId: string) => Promise<string> | string;
}

export type RunStatus =
  'done' | 'error' | 'timeout' | 'watchdog' | 'loop' | 'superseded';

export interface RunOutcome {
  status: RunStatus;
  /** Messages refused by the entry or payload cap. */
  dropped: number;
}

export interface RunHandle {
  runId: string;
  messages: RunnerMessage[];
  onMessage(callback: (message: RunnerMessage) => void): () => void;
  done: Promise<RunOutcome>;
}

export interface RunController {
  run(input: RunInput): RunHandle;
  dispose(): void;
}

export interface RunControllerOptions {
  wallClockMs?: number;
  watchdogMs?: number;
  maxEntries?: number;
  maxBytes?: number;
  createFrame?: () => HTMLIFrameElement;
  target?: Window;
  newRunId?: () => string;
}

/**
 * One sandboxed iframe per run, removed when the run ends (spec §11.4 to §11.6).
 *
 * The controller holds at most one live run. A new run removes the old frame
 * first, which ends everything the old run started, and the old run's listener
 * goes with it, so nothing the old frame posted can reach the new run.
 */
export function createRunController(
  host: HTMLElement,
  options: RunControllerOptions = {},
): RunController {
  const {
    wallClockMs = 10_000,
    watchdogMs = 2_000,
    maxEntries = 1_000,
    maxBytes = 256 * 1024,
    createFrame = () => host.ownerDocument.createElement('iframe'),
    target = host.ownerDocument.defaultView as Window,
    newRunId = () => crypto.randomUUID(),
  } = options;

  let current: { finish(status: RunStatus): void } | null = null;

  function run(input: RunInput): RunHandle {
    current?.finish('superseded');

    const runId = newRunId();
    const messages: RunnerMessage[] = [];
    const listeners = new Set<(message: RunnerMessage) => void>();
    let resolve!: (outcome: RunOutcome) => void;
    const done = new Promise<RunOutcome>((settle) => {
      resolve = settle;
    });

    const frame = createFrame();
    // The attribute goes on before srcdoc and before the frame joins the
    // document, so no navigation ever happens without it.
    frame.setAttribute('sandbox', 'allow-scripts');
    frame.setAttribute('title', 'Run output');
    frame.hidden = true;

    let consoleEntries = 0;
    let bytes = 0;
    let dropped = 0;
    let finished = false;
    let wallClock: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
    let watchdog: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;

    const push = (message: RunnerMessage) => {
      messages.push(message);
      for (const listener of listeners) listener(message);
    };

    const report = (
      phase: 'runtime' | 'timeout',
      name: string,
      message: string,
    ) => push({ v: 1, runId, type: 'error', phase, name, message });

    const finish = (status: RunStatus) => {
      if (finished) return;
      finished = true;
      clearTimeout(wallClock);
      clearTimeout(watchdog);
      target.removeEventListener('message', onMessage);
      frame.remove();
      if (current === active) current = null;
      resolve({ status, dropped });
    };

    const armWatchdog = () => {
      clearTimeout(watchdog);
      watchdog = setTimeout(() => {
        report(
          'timeout',
          'WatchdogError',
          `The run stopped responding. It sent no heartbeat for ${watchdogMs / 1000} seconds.`,
        );
        finish('watchdog');
      }, watchdogMs);
    };

    function onMessage(event: MessageEvent) {
      if (finished || frame.contentWindow === null) return;
      const message = acceptMessage(event, {
        window: frame.contentWindow,
        runId,
      });
      if (message === null) return;

      switch (message.type) {
        case 'heartbeat':
          armWatchdog();
          return;
        case 'ready':
          armWatchdog();
          push(message);
          return;
        case 'done':
          push(message);
          finish('done');
          return;
        case 'error':
          push(message);
          finish(
            message.phase === 'loop'
              ? 'loop'
              : message.phase === 'timeout'
                ? 'timeout'
                : 'error',
          );
          return;
        default: {
          const size = JSON.stringify(message).length;
          const overEntries =
            message.type === 'console' && consoleEntries >= maxEntries;
          if (overEntries || bytes + size > maxBytes) {
            dropped += 1;
            return;
          }
          if (message.type === 'console') consoleEntries += 1;
          bytes += size;
          push(message);
        }
      }
    }

    const active = { finish };
    current = active;
    target.addEventListener('message', onMessage);
    wallClock = setTimeout(() => {
      report(
        'timeout',
        'TimeoutError',
        `The run did not finish within ${wallClockMs / 1000} seconds.`,
      );
      finish('timeout');
    }, wallClockMs);

    void Promise.resolve()
      .then(() => input.document(runId))
      .then(
        (html) => {
          if (finished) return;
          frame.srcdoc = html;
          host.append(frame);
        },
        (error: unknown) => {
          report(
            'runtime',
            'SandboxError',
            error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error),
          );
          finish('error');
        },
      );

    return {
      runId,
      messages,
      onMessage(callback) {
        listeners.add(callback);
        return () => listeners.delete(callback);
      },
      done,
    };
  }

  return {
    run,
    dispose() {
      current?.finish('superseded');
    },
  };
}
```

`apps/docs/components/runtime/stack-map.ts`:

```ts
import { originalPositionFor, TraceMap } from '@jridgewell/trace-mapping';

export interface MappedFrame {
  /** The reader's file (`main.ts`), or null for a frame outside their code. */
  file: string | null;
  line: number | null;
  column: number | null;
  raw: string;
}

export interface StackModule {
  dataUrl: string;
  path: string;
  map: string;
}

// `at fn (url:line:col)` and `at url:line:col`.
const CHROMIUM = /^at (?:.*? \()?(.+?):(\d+):(\d+)\)?$/;
// `fn@url:line:col`, `@url:line:col` and `url:line:col`.
const GECKO_WEBKIT = /^(?:[^@]*@)?(.+?):(\d+):(\d+)$/;
// Only URLs name a frame; this keeps a message like "failed at 3:4" out.
const URL_SCHEME = /^(?:data|https?|blob|file):/;

function parse(
  line: string,
): { url: string; line: number; column: number } | null {
  const match = CHROMIUM.exec(line) ?? GECKO_WEBKIT.exec(line);
  if (!match?.[1] || !URL_SCHEME.test(match[1])) return null;
  return { url: match[1], line: Number(match[2]), column: Number(match[3]) };
}

/**
 * Turns a stack from the sandbox into editor locations (spec §11.5).
 *
 * A frame in a `data:` module carries the whole data URL, and no browser
 * applies a source map to `Error.stack`. The URL identifies the reader's file,
 * and that file's source map from the worker gives the line in the editor.
 */
export function mapStack(
  stack: string,
  modules: Record<string, StackModule>,
): MappedFrame[] {
  const byUrl = new Map(
    Object.values(modules).map((module) => [module.dataUrl, module]),
  );
  const maps = new Map<string, TraceMap>();
  const frames: MappedFrame[] = [];

  for (const text of stack.split('\n')) {
    const raw = text.trim();
    const frame = parse(raw);
    if (!frame) continue;

    const module = byUrl.get(frame.url);
    if (!module) {
      frames.push({ file: null, line: null, column: null, raw });
      continue;
    }

    let traced = maps.get(module.path);
    if (!traced) {
      traced = new TraceMap(module.map);
      maps.set(module.path, traced);
    }

    const original = originalPositionFor(traced, {
      line: frame.line,
      column: frame.column - 1,
    });
    frames.push({
      file: module.path,
      line: original.line,
      column: original.column === null ? null : original.column + 1,
      raw,
    });
  }

  return frames;
}
```

```ts
function binding(focus: ReturnType<typeof escapeThenTab>, key: string) {
  const found = focus.bindings.find((each) => each.key === key);
  if (!found) throw new Error(`no binding for ${key}`);
  return found;
}

describe('escapeThenTab', () => {
```

```ts
import type { Diagnostic } from '@codemirror/lint';

import type { WorkerDiagnostic } from '../runtime/worker-protocol';

/** Worker diagnostics as CodeMirror lint entries, drawn as squiggles. */
export function toLintDiagnostics(
  diagnostics: WorkerDiagnostic[],
  length: number,
): Diagnostic[] {
  return diagnostics.map((diagnostic) => {
    const from = Math.min(Math.max(diagnostic.from, 0), length);
    const to = Math.min(Math.max(diagnostic.to, from), length);
    return {
      from,
      to,
      severity: diagnostic.severity,
      message: `TS${diagnostic.code}: ${diagnostic.message}`,
    };
  });
}
```

`apps/docs/components/editor/extensions.ts`:

```ts
import {
  defaultKeymap,
  history,
  historyKeymap,
  indentLess,
  indentMore,
} from '@codemirror/commands';
import { javascript } from '@codemirror/lang-javascript';
import { linter, lintGutter, type Diagnostic } from '@codemirror/lint';
import type { Extension } from '@codemirror/state';
import {
  EditorView,
  keymap,
  lineNumbers,
  type Command,
  type KeyBinding,
} from '@codemirror/view';

/**
 * Tab indents inside the editor, and Escape followed by Tab leaves it
 * (spec §11.8, WCAG 2.1.2).
 *
 * A Tab binding that returns false hands the key back to the browser, whose
 * default moves focus to the next control.
 */
export function escapeThenTab(
  indent: Command = indentMore,
  outdent: Command = indentLess,
) {
  let armed = false;

  const bindings: KeyBinding[] = [
    {
      key: 'Escape',
      run: () => {
        armed = true;
        return true;
      },
    },
    {
      key: 'Tab',
      run: (view) => {
        if (armed) {
          armed = false;
          return false;
        }
        return indent(view);
      },
      shift: (view) => {
        if (armed) {
          armed = false;
          return false;
        }
        return outdent(view);
      },
    },
  ];

  return {
    bindings,
    get armed() {
      return armed;
    },
    disarm() {
      armed = false;
    },
  };
}

export interface EditorExtensionOptions {
  label: string;
  onChange(text: string): void;
  diagnostics(length: number): Diagnostic[];
}

export function editorExtensions(options: EditorExtensionOptions): Extension[] {
  const focus = escapeThenTab();

  return [
    lineNumbers(),
    history(),
    javascript({ typescript: true }),
    lintGutter(),
    linter((view) => options.diagnostics(view.state.doc.length), { delay: 0 }),
    keymap.of([...focus.bindings, ...defaultKeymap, ...historyKeymap]),
    EditorView.domEventHandlers({
      keydown(event) {
        if (event.key !== 'Escape' && event.key !== 'Tab') focus.disarm();
        return false;
      },
    }),
    EditorView.updateListener.of((update) => {
      if (update.docChanged) options.onChange(update.state.doc.toString());
    }),
    EditorView.contentAttributes.of({
      'aria-label': `${options.label}. Press Escape then Tab to leave the editor.`,
    }),
  ];
}
```

```tsx
'use client';

import { forceLinting } from '@codemirror/lint';
import { EditorState } from '@codemirror/state';
import { EditorView } from '@codemirror/view';
import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';

import type { WorkerDiagnostic } from '../runtime/worker-protocol';
import { toLintDiagnostics } from './diagnostics';
import { editorExtensions } from './extensions';
import './editor.css';

export interface EditorProps {
  files: Record<string, string>;
  active: string;
  onActive(path: string): void;
  onChange(path: string, text: string): void;
  diagnostics: Record<string, WorkerDiagnostic[]>;
  label: string;
  /** A new value discards every file's editor state (Reset to seed). */
  revision: number;
}

export default function Editor(props: EditorProps) {
  const { files, active, onActive, diagnostics, label, revision } = props;
  const parent = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const view = useRef<EditorView | null>(null);
  const states = useRef(new Map<string, EditorState>());
  const shown = useRef(active);
  const latest = useRef(props);
  latest.current = props;

  function stateFor(path: string): EditorState {
    const kept = states.current.get(path);
    if (kept) return kept;
    const made = EditorState.create({
      doc: latest.current.files[path] ?? '',
      extensions: editorExtensions({
        label: `${label}, ${path}`,
        onChange: (text) => latest.current.onChange(path, text),
        diagnostics: (length) =>
          toLintDiagnostics(latest.current.diagnostics[path] ?? [], length),
      }),
    });
    states.current.set(path, made);
    return made;
  }

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!parent.current) return;
    states.current.clear();
    shown.current = latest.current.active;
    const editor = new EditorView({
      parent: parent.current,
      state: stateFor(shown.current),
    });
    view.current = editor;
    return () => {
      editor.destroy();
      view.current = null;
    };
    // The editor is rebuilt only when the reader resets to the seed.
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [revision]);

  useEffect(() => {
    const editor = view.current;
    if (!editor || shown.current === active) return;
    states.current.set(shown.current, editor.state);
    shown.current = active;
    editor.setState(stateFor(active));
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [active]);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (view.current) forceLinting(view.current);
  }, [diagnostics]);

  const paths = Object.keys(files);

  return (
    <div className="nexus-editor">
      {paths.length > 1 ? (
        <div className="nexus-editor__tabs" role="tablist" aria-label="Files">
          {paths.map((path) => (
            <button
              key={path}
              type="button"
              role="tab"
              aria-selected={path === active}
              className="nexus-editor__tab"
              onClick={() => onActive(path)}
            >
              {path}
            </button>
          ))}
        </div>
      ) : null}
      <div ref={parent} className="nexus-editor__surface" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

```ts
/** One editor file of a seed, read from a doctested region. */
export interface SeedFile {
  /** The editor's file name, `main.ts`. */
  path: string;
  /** The workspace-relative file that holds the region. */
  file: string;
  region: string;
}

export interface Seed {
  files: SeedFile[];
  /** The file `boot.js` imports, as `@ship/<name>`. */
  entry: string;
}

/**
 * Every program the console, the Playground and the Academy can start from
 * (spec §11.9). A link names one of these ids and never carries code.
 */
export const seeds: Record<string, Seed> = {
  'playground/first-light': {
    files: [
      {
        path: 'main.ts',
        file: 'examples/meridian/src/playground/first-light/main.ts',
        region: 'first-light',
      },
    ],
    entry: 'main.ts',
  },
};
```

Add to `apps/docs/tools/playground-types.mjs`, beside `writeTypes`:

```js
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';

import { readRegion } from '@nexusdi/doc-examples/regions';
import ts from 'typescript';

import { seeds } from '../components/runtime/seeds.ts';
import { transpileRun } from '../components/runtime/transform.ts';

/** `playground/first-light` plus a content hash, as one flat file name. */
export function seedFileName(id, json) {
  const hash = createHash('sha256').update(json).digest('hex').slice(0, 12);
  return `${id.replaceAll('/', '__')}-${hash}.json`;
}

/**
 * A seed as the Playground loads it: the editor text of every file, and the
 * JavaScript the worker would emit for it, so Run works on an unedited seed
 * before the worker arrives (spec §11.7).
 */
export function bundleSeed(root, id, seed) {
  const files = Object.fromEntries(
    seed.files.map((file) => [
      file.path,
      readRegion(
        readFileSync(join(root, file.file), 'utf8'),
        file.file,
        file.region,
      ).code,
    ]),
  );
  return { id, entry: seed.entry, files, modules: transpileRun(ts, files) };
}

/** Writes `seeds/<file>.json` per seed and `seeds/index.json` under `runtimeDir`. */
export function emitSeeds(root, runtimeDir, registry = seeds) {
  const dir = join(runtimeDir, 'seeds');
  mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
  const index = {};
  for (const [id, seed] of Object.entries(registry)) {
    const json = JSON.stringify(bundleSeed(root, id, seed));
    const name = seedFileName(id, json);
    writeFileSync(join(dir, name), json);
    index[id] = `seeds/${name}`;
  }
  writeFileSync(join(dir, 'index.json'), JSON.stringify(index));
  return index;
}
```

- [ ] Step 9: Implement the helper

`apps/docs/components/playground/run.ts`:

```ts
import type { RunnerMessage } from '../runtime/protocol';
import { dataUrlFor } from '../runtime/srcdoc';
import { mapStack } from '../runtime/stack-map';

export interface EmittedModule {
  specifier: string;
  js: string;
  map: string;
}

export interface SeedBundle {
  id: string;
  entry: string;
  files: Record<string, string>;
  modules: Record<string, EmittedModule>;
}

/** Emitted modules, keyed by path, as the import map's specifier-to-source table. */
export function toRunModules(
  modules: Record<string, EmittedModule>,
): Record<string, string> {
  return Object.fromEntries(
    Object.values(modules).map((module) => [module.specifier, module.js]),
  );
}

/** One line for the error region: name, code, message and the editor location. */
export function describeError(
  message: Extract<RunnerMessage, { type: 'error' }>,
  modules: Record<string, EmittedModule>,
): string {
  const code = message.code ? ` [${message.code}]` : '';
  const head = `${message.name}${code}: ${message.message}`;
  if (!message.stack) return head;

  const table = Object.fromEntries(
    Object.entries(modules).map(([path, module]) => [
      module.specifier,
      { dataUrl: dataUrlFor(module.js), path, map: module.map },
    ]),
  );
  const frame = mapStack(message.stack, table).find(
    (each) => each.file !== null,
  );
  return frame ? `${head} (${frame.file}:${frame.line})` : head;
}
```

`apps/docs/components/playground/Playground.tsx`:

```tsx
'use client';

import { useSearchParams } from 'next/navigation';
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';

import LazyEditor from '../editor/LazyEditor';
import { basePath } from '../runtime/base-path';
import type { RuntimeManifest } from '../runtime/manifest';
import {
  createRunController,
  type RunController,
} from '../runtime/run-controller';
import { renderValue } from '../runtime/serialize';
import { buildSrcdoc } from '../runtime/srcdoc';
import { createTypeChecker, type TypeChecker } from '../runtime/worker-client';
import type { WorkerDiagnostic } from '../runtime/worker-protocol';
import {
  describeError,
  toRunModules,
  type EmittedModule,
  type SeedBundle,
} from './run';
import './playground.css';

const DEFAULT_SEED = 'playground/first-light';

interface Line {
  key: number;
  level: string;
  text: string;
}

async function fetchJson<T>(path: string): Promise<T> {
  const response = await fetch(`${basePath}/runtime/${path}`);
  if (!response.ok)
    throw new Error(`${path} answered HTTP ${response.status}.`);
  return (await response.json()) as T;
}

export default function Playground() {
  const id = useSearchParams().get('seed') ?? DEFAULT_SEED;
  const [manifest, setManifest] = useState<RuntimeManifest | null>(null);
  const [seed, setSeed] = useState<SeedBundle | null>(null);
  const [problem, setProblem] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [files, setFiles] = useState<Record<string, string>>({});
  const [active, setActive] = useState('main.ts');
  const [editing, setEditing] = useState(false);
  const [edited, setEdited] = useState(false);
  const [checking, setChecking] = useState(false);
  const [revision, setRevision] = useState(0);
  const [diagnostics, setDiagnostics] = useState<
    Record<string, WorkerDiagnostic[]>
  >({});
  const [lines, setLines] = useState<Line[]>([]);
  const [failure, setFailure] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [status, setStatus] = useState('');
  const host = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const controller = useRef<RunController | null>(null);
  const checker = useRef<TypeChecker | null>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    let live = true;
    (async () => {
      const [runtime, index] = await Promise.all([
        fetchJson<RuntimeManifest>('manifest.json'),
        fetchJson<Record<string, string>>('seeds/index.json'),
      ]);
      if (!live) return;
      setManifest(runtime);
      const file = index[id];
      if (!file) {
        setProblem(`No seed named ${id} exists.`);
        return;
      }
      const bundle = await fetchJson<SeedBundle>(file);
      if (!live) return;
      setSeed(bundle);
      setFiles(bundle.files);
      setActive(bundle.entry);
    })().catch((error: unknown) => {
      if (live)
        setProblem(error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error));
    });
    return () => {
      live = false;
    };
  }, [id]);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!host.current) return;
    const created = createRunController(host.current);
    controller.current = created;
    return () => {
      created.dispose();
      checker.current?.dispose();
    };
  }, []);

  function startChecker(next: Record<string, string>) {
    if (!manifest) return;
    if (!checker.current) {
      // The worker and the declarations load here, on the first edit, and at
      // no earlier point (spec §11.7).
      setChecking(true);
      const created = createTypeChecker({
        typesUrl: `${basePath}/runtime/${manifest.typesFile}`,
      });
      created.onDiagnostics((reported) => {
        setChecking(false);
        setDiagnostics(reported);
      });
      checker.current = created;
    }
    checker.current.update(next);
  }

  function change(path: string, text: string) {
    const next = { ...files, [path]: text };
    setFiles(next);
    setEdited(true);
    startChecker(next);
  }

  function reset() {
    if (!seed) return;
    setFiles(seed.files);
    setEdited(false);
    setDiagnostics({});
    setRevision((value) => value + 1);
    setStatus('The editor holds the seed again.');
  }

  async function run() {
    if (!manifest || !seed || !controller.current) return;
    setLines([]);
    setFailure(null);
    setStatus('Running.');
    const modules: Record<string, EmittedModule> =
      edited && checker.current
        ? await checker.current.emit(files)
        : seed.modules;
    const handle = controller.current.run({
      document: (runId) =>
        buildSrcdoc({
          origin: location.origin,
          basePath,
          manifest,
          runId,
          modules: toRunModules(modules),
        }),
    });
    handle.onMessage((message) => {
      if (message.type === 'console') {
        setLines((previous) => [
          ...previous,
          {
            key: previous.length,
            level: message.level,
            text: message.args.map(renderValue).join(' '),
          },
        ]);
      }
      if (message.type === 'error') setFailure(describeError(message, modules));
    });
    const outcome = await handle.done;
    if (outcome.status === 'superseded') return;
    const dropped =
      outcome.dropped > 0
        ? ` The page dropped ${outcome.dropped} messages past the limit.`
        : '';
    setStatus(
      outcome.status === 'done'
        ? `Run finished.${dropped}`
        : `Run ended.${dropped}`,
    );
  }

  if (problem) {
    return (
      <p role="alert" className="nexus-playground__problem">
        {problem}
      </p>
    );
  }

  return (
    <div className="nexus-playground">
      <div className="nexus-playground__actions">
        <button type="button" onClick={run} disabled={!seed}>
          Run
        </button>
        <button
          type="button"
          onClick={() => setEditing(true)}
          disabled={!seed || editing}
        >
          Edit
        </button>
        <button type="button" onClick={reset} disabled={!seed}>
          Reset to seed
        </button>
        {checking ? (
          <span className="nexus-playground__checking">
            Loading the type checker
          </span>
        ) : null}
      </div>

      {editing ? (
        <LazyEditor
          files={files}
          active={active}
          onActive={setActive}
          onChange={change}
          diagnostics={diagnostics}
          label="Playground editor"
          revision={revision}
        />
      ) : (
        <pre
          className="nexus-playground__source"
          tabIndex={0}
          onFocus={() => setEditing(true)}
        >
          <code>{files[active] ?? ''}</code>
        </pre>
      )}

      <ol className="nexus-playground__log" role="log" aria-label="Run output">
        {lines.map((line) => (
          <li key={line.key} data-level={line.level}>
            {line.text}
          </li>
        ))}
      </ol>
      {failure ? (
        <p role="alert" className="nexus-playground__failure">
          {failure}
        </p>
      ) : null}
      <p className="nexus-playground__status" aria-live="polite">
        {status}
      </p>

      <p className="nexus-playground__help">
        Your code runs in a sandboxed frame with no network access and no access
        to this page. A loop that runs past one second stops with an error. A
        single built-in call that runs for a long time, such as a huge string
        repeat, a regular expression that backtracks without end or a sort over
        a very large array, can freeze this tab until the call finishes.
      </p>

      <div ref={host} className="nexus-playground__frames" />
    </div>
  );
}
```
